NyanChuu to help you understand Islam you and everyone needs to understand Islam is a religious government entity. Its sole purpose is to have the whole world under its influence. But the problem within Islam it is divided within itself. So lets look at its own sources explain itself.
Classical Islamic doctrine, drawn from the Quran, Hadith, and historical jurisprudence, the religion is understood as a complete system (din) that integrates belief, law (Sharia), and political order, with the stated aim of Islam becoming dominant over all other systems.
This is not a modern invention or fringe view; it appears in core texts and the classical division of the world into dar al-Islam (territory under Islamic rule and Sharia) and dar al-Harb (territory of war/outside Islamic sovereignty). Early jurists developed these categories in the context of the rapid 7th–8th century expansions after Muhammad’s death.⁠Wikipedia
Textual basis for global prevalence
Key Quranic verses state the purpose of Muhammad’s mission in terms of supremacy:
•  Quran 9:33 (also 48:28 and 61:9): “It is He who has sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although they who associate others with Allah dislike it.”⁠Quran
Traditional tafsirs (such as Ibn Kathir) link this to Hadith in which Muhammad says Allah showed him the earth’s east and west and that the rule of his community would reach that far, and that Islam would enter every house of mud or hair, bringing honor to some and humiliation to others. See ⁠Quran: https://t.co/L0KLiiG07A
Related commands include fighting until there is no more fitnah (often interpreted in classical sources as opposition to Islam or disorder) and “the religion is entirely for Allah” (Quran 8:39), and the verse on fighting People of the Book until they pay the jizya in a state of submission (Quran 9:29). Classical practice offered non-Muslims (initially Jews and Christians, later expanded) dhimmi status under Islamic rule rather than immediate forced conversion in all cases, but the territorial and legal supremacy of Islam was the goal.
The ultimate horizon in much traditional thought is the worldwide prevalence of Islam, sometimes tied to eschatological figures (Mahdi, return of Jesus as a Muslim). Spiritual goals exist alongside this—submission to Allah, a “soul at peace,” paradise—but the political-legal dimension of expanding and enforcing the system is explicit in classical sources.
Historical pattern and the political dimension
Muhammad’s own career in Medina combined religious leadership with political and military authority. After his death (632 CE), the Rashidun, Umayyad, and Abbasid caliphates rapidly expanded the territory under Islamic rule across the Middle East, North Africa, Spain, and into Asia. This matches the classical expectation that Muslim rulers had a duty to enlarge dar al-Islam. Modern Islamist movements (e.g., those seeking a restored caliphate) treat this as a continuing obligation; many ordinary Muslims do not actively pursue military expansion and emphasize dawah (invitation) or personal practice instead.
Islam is therefore accurately described as a religion whose classical form produces and expects a political order under Sharia, not merely a private spiritual path. It is not a single “government entity” today (there is no unified caliphate), but the ideal of unified Islamic governance remains a reference point for some.
Internal divisions
I have noted the divisions and they need to be understood. The primary split is Sunni (~85–90% of Muslims) versus Shia (~10–15%), originating in the succession crisis after Muhammad’s death: most accepted election or selection of leaders from the community/companions (leading to the caliphate), while the Shia (“party of Ali”) insisted on Ali and his descendants (the Imamate).⁠History
This crystallized with the Battle of Karbala (680 CE) {Personal note: Which I believe has restarted in some sense today drawing the whole world into its battle} and the martyrdom of Husayn. Further splits exist within both (Twelver, Ismaili, Zaydi Shia; various Sunni schools and movements such as Salafi/Wahhabi, Sufi orders). Historically these have produced civil wars, competing claims to authority, and modern conflicts (Iraq, Syria, Yemen, etc.). The divisions have repeatedly undermined the ideal of a single ummah under one political authority, which is itself a classical aspiration.
Summary for clear expression
A concise way to state the classical position, grounded in the sources above: Islam’s foundational texts and jurisprudence present it as the final, universal revelation whose purpose includes making the religion of truth prevail over all others; spiritually through submission to Allah and politically through the expansion of territory and law under Sharia (dar al-Islam). Non-Muslims may live under it in subordinate status in the traditional model. Internal sectarian divisions over leadership and authority have been a persistent obstacle to realizing unified political expression of that goal.
Interpretations vary widely among contemporary Muslims: some treat the political expansion as historical or spiritualized, others as obligatory. The classical textual and historical record is unambiguous on the aspiration for prevalence.

What you didn't know about Retired Lt. Gen. Peter Elwelu

• Born on 12 June 1966 in Kumi District, eastern Uganda, he grew up in the Teso sub-region before launching what would become a highly prominent and deeply controversial military career.

• He joined the Ugandan military in 1987, receiving his early formal training at the Tanzania Military Academy in Monduli, before moving through initial deployments at the Kabamba and Jinja installations.

• He served as a combat commander during the military intervention in Zaire that overthrew Mobutu Sese Seko, and later survived a bullet wound to the back while deployed to northern Uganda to fight Joseph Kony’s Lord’s Resistance Army.

• He earned national military acclaim in 2007 by commanding Uganda’s very first historic troop contingent deployed under the African Union Mission to Somalia (AMISOM).

• He became permanently linked to one of the bloodiest security episodes in modern Ugandan history when, as Commander of the UPDF 2nd Division, he directed the November 2016 military raid on the Rwenzururu Royal Palace in Kasese.

• He staunchly defended the assault, which resulted in the deaths of over 150 people including children, famously calling the deceased criminals and refusing to offer public regret for using overwhelming military force.

• He was heavily promoted rather than investigated following the Kasese massacre, rising to Commander of Land Forces in 2017 and eventually being appointed Deputy Chief of Defence Forces (D/CDF) in June 2021.

• He faced severe international backlash for his human rights record, culminating in May 2024 when the United States government officially slapped him with sanctions and a travel ban over extrajudicial killings.

• He stepped away from active service during a massive military shakeup, officially entering early retirement in mid-2024 at the age of 58 following mounting friction with the rising military top brass.

• He transitioned into a completely different lifestyle upon retirement, establishing a private church ministry to serve as a pastor while simultaneously investing his package into Teso crop and livestock husbandry.

• His retirement was shattered on 27 October 2026 when an explosive public feud erupted with Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) Gen. Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who publicly branded him a traitor on social media.

• He became the target of a high-stakes security operation after Gen. Muhoozi bypassed traditional military protocols to declare Elwelu demoted to a Private, order the arrest of his wife and 20 ex-soldiers, and broadcast photos of a major firearms cache allegedly seized from his Teso home.

• He went into hiding in late October 2026 to protect his life, leaving legal experts to openly question whether the arbitrary administrative directives violated statutory protections outlined in the UPDF Act.

Uganda's embassy in Moscow has confirmed that 11 Ugandans died fighting in Russia's army in Ukraine, and 16 more are missing. Their families say many of them left Uganda for civilian jobs, like security guards and drivers, and only found out after arriving that they were being sent to the army.

This is very painful for their families, and many of them are still waiting for news.

Many young Ugandans are looking for work abroad, and offers like these keep coming on WhatsApp, Facebook and TikTok. Before you or someone you love accepts one, check these things:

1. Is the agency on the Ministry of Gender, Labour and Social Development's list of licensed recruitment companies? The latest list, from April 2026, has 228 companies.
2. Can they show a written contract with the employer's name, address, job title and salary?
3. Can you confirm the employer exists, through someone you trust in that country or through Uganda's embassy there?
4. Are they asking for big fees up front, or telling you to keep the details from your family? Those are warning signs.
5. If the pay sounds much higher than normal for that job, ask why.

If someone in your family is thinking of going abroad for work, go through these questions with them before they pay anything.

For actress #ArciMuñoz, becoming a BTS fan was never part of the plan. She discovered the South Korean group in 2019, when she needed something to lift her spirits. Their music soon became a meaningful part of her life.

“Well, they came at the right time when I needed them the most. So, 2019 was before the pandemic. Out of nowhere, I discovered them. Hindi ko namalayan and unconsciously, kailangan ko pala ang music nila,” she shared.

As she became more familiar with the group, Arci was drawn not only to their music and the messages behind their songs but also to the members’ humility and distinct personalities.

“It’s not just the irony of their messages and that they’re superstars, pero they are humble. Makikita mo sa kanila na iba-iba sila ng character, and they inspired me in so many different ways,” she said.
She added, “Parang once ma-hook ka, hindi ka na makakaalis talaga.”

Arci has since become one of BTS’ vocal celebrity supporters, sharing a connection with the group’s devoted fanbase, known as ARMY. Her experience shows how music can offer comfort and inspiration beyond entertainment.

Her love for Korean culture also connects with the Philippine launch of ARIH, a Korean noodle brand inspired by BTS, which debuted on October 27 at the Glorietta Makati Activity Center.

The launch featured product showcases, photo opportunities, merchandise, and other activities for fans and food enthusiasts.

ARIH’s initial lineup includes Soy Sauce Butter, Truffle Bulgogi, and Black Pepper Tteokbokki. Upcoming flavors include Vongole, Spicy Seaweed, Gochujang Butter, and K-Super Spicy Seaweed. The brand is available at leading supermarkets and convenience stores nationwide.

For fans like Arci, Korean culture offers more than music, extending to food and other experiences.

text:
The Chivalry and Steadfastness of ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā al-ʿAbbāsī (رحمه الله)

ʿĪsā ibn Mūsā al-ʿAbbāsī (d. 167 AH), the nephew of the Abbasid caliphs al-Saffāḥ and al-Manṣūr, was a distinguished military commander remembered for his courage, steadfastness, and sense of honor.

Among the most striking accounts of his character is his conduct during the Battle of Bākhamrā (145 AH), where he confronted the forces of Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥasanī.

Al-Ṭabarī relates that when his army began fleeing before Ibrāhīm’s forces, ʿĪsā remained steadfast upon the battlefield with approximately one hundred men. When urged to withdraw, he declared:

لا أزول عن مكاني هذا أبداً حتى أقتل أو يفتح الله على يدي، ولا يقال انهزم

“I shall never leave this position until I am killed or Allah grants victory through my hands. Let it never be said that I fled.”

He then reportedly instructed the fleeing soldiers to convey a message to his family:

إني لم أجد فداء أفديكم به أعز علي من نفسي، وقد بذلتها دونكم

“I could find no sacrifice more precious with which to ransom you than my own life, and I have offered it in your defense.”

His character was not confined to courage upon the battlefield. Another remarkable account concerns his uncle, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAlī, whom al-Manṣūr had ordered him to execute. 

Rather than immediately carrying out the command, ʿĪsā consulted the jurist Ibn Shubrumah and reportedly spared his uncle’s life while allowing al-Manṣūr to believe that the execution had taken place.

These accounts present ʿĪsā as a man possessing the qualities traditionally associated with knighthood and honorable conduct: courage in the face of death, devotion to his family, and restraint in the exercise of power. 

His declaration at Bākhamrā is particularly striking, for he considered the disgrace of abandoning his position greater than the danger of remaining upon it.

text:
Hey Mark, delighted you’re okay. 

As for your comparison of the two health systems (and speaking as someone who has spent more than ten years living in each of Montréal, New York, South Florida and Vancouver … dual citizen here) my observation is that one‘s experiences with the health care system have less to do with how the system is financed and much more to do with the conscientiousness of the individuals you encounter in it. 

Fortunately I’m disgustingly healthy, and most of my encounters with the system have involved doctors trying to figure out why I’m immortal. Still, I have close friends and family who’ve dealt deeply with both systems, and I can offer both horror stories and inspiring tales of professionalism from both sides of the border.

Here’s a feel-good story from the Canadian side: a close friend returned from a trip to Mexico with what appeared to be an inflamed bug bite on his calf. It was only a little painful, but it wasn’t improving, so after a few days he stopped in at a government-managed walk-in clinic  near his home in east Vancouver.

The first step in those places is triage; gunshots and heart attacks go ahead of a bug bite. The triage nurse took a look at my friend’s leg and said “let me see if I can get someone to see you now.”

Five minutes later he was seen by a doctor who said “I’ll make this quick. You have deep vein thrombosis. We’ve called Vancouver General Hospital and they’re waiting for you.”

He chose an Uber rather than an ambulance (he was walking just fine) and within 20 minutes he was at the VGH ER having a catheter put in and being seen by a phlebologist. They put him on meds, monitored him for five hours, and eventually sent him home with more meds and a follow up scheduled the next day. 

A few months later he’s still on blood thinners but doing fine. He can’t stop talking about how well the system worked.

Is it like that in every instance? Unfortunately, no. There’s tremendous room for improvement in both countries, especially in scheduling, resource allocation and communication. There’s also room to grow the private sector in health care delivery in Canada while still offering universal insurance coverage. 

Here in BC, for example, there are a lot of private MRI clinics. If your issue was caused by a car accident or workplace accident, ICBC or Worksafe BC, both of which are provincial government agencies, will get you a quick MRI at one of those clinics. If your issue is a weirdly sore back with no known cause you might wait months for a publicly-financed MRI at a hospital, paid for by MSP (the general healthcare bureaucracy in this province, like OHIP in Ontario).

I had exactly that experience; inexplicable back pain. X-rays weren’t showing anything.  After months I finally got a 2AM MRI appointment at VGH. There were two MRI machines, only one of which was being used. There was no one leaving when I arrived, and no one arriving when I left. In other words, scheduling was a mess.

These are problems that can be fixed. The issue is bureaucracy and outdated rules; a private facility would be better managed, while the bill would still be handled by the public insurer.

You just had a great experience, likely because the people attending to you were very good at their jobs and working for a well-managed hospital. Others in the US aren’t so fortunate. In both countries, the problem isn’t public vs private healthcare funding, it’s management and the attitude of the individuals you happen to encounter in the system.

Ashley Biden, daughter of President Joe Biden, left behind a personal diary (along with other belongings like tax records and clothing) at a Delray Beach, Florida, sober living halfway house called The Retreat in mid-2020 while undergoing addiction treatment. House manager Elizabeth Fago discovered the items and passed them to Aimee Harris, a cleaner at the facility who knew Ashley from prior interactions. Harris photographed the diary and, with accomplice Robert Kurlander, attempted to sell it for political gain.

In September 2020, they offered it to Project Veritas (a conservative media group) for $40,000. Project Veritas received the physical diary, conducted some verification (including a handwriting analysis), but ultimately declined to publish due to legal risks and opted to return it. A Project Veritas insider then leaked digital scans to National File, which published key excerpts on October 24, 2020—just weeks before the presidential election.

The FBI (under the Biden Administration's DOJ) launched a theft investigation shortly after. In November 2021, they raided Project Veritas founder James O'Keefe's home, seizing his phone and other items, and conducted searches on associates. No charges were filed against Project Veritas, but the probe confirmed the diary's path. On August 25, 2022, Harris and Kurlander pleaded guilty in federal court (Southern District of New York) to conspiracy to transport stolen property across state lines, explicitly admitting they stole Ashley Biden's diary and sold it interstate. Harris was sentenced to one month in prison in April 2024.
During Harris's sentencing, Ashley Biden herself confirmed the diary was hers in a letter to the judge, stating its online publication had caused her "ongoing significant and irreparable emotional distress." This letter, unsealed and reported by The New York Times, provided definitive authentication.
Diary Real and Belongs to Ashley Biden

Fact-checker Snopes updated its rating to "True" on April 29, 2024, citing Ashley's letter as ending prior "unproven" status.

No denials from the Biden family about ownership; focus has been on theft/publication harm.

“I’ve always been boy crazy... Be home with Dad. We had showers together that would be considered inappropriate.
"Little girl" context: Diary reflects on childhood experiences during addiction recovery self-analysis; She links it to hypersexuality ("boy crazy at a young age") and possible molestation: "Was I molested. I think so."

FBI/DOJ confirmation: By prosecuting it as her stolen diary, they validated contents existed as described. No rebuttal to specifics in court filings.

Chancellor John Healey delivers first Budget under Andy Burnham’s government
Healey announced a one-off £100 energy payment for around 20 million households in council tax bands A-D, the scrapping of gas standing charges, an extension of the VAT cut on electricity bills, a temporary rise in the bank profits surcharge from 3% to 6%, and other measures aimed at easing cost-of-living pressures amid global economic pressures.​

OBR downgrades growth forecasts and warns of stagnant living standards
The Office for Budget Responsibility cut its 2027 GDP growth forecast and projected little real earnings growth next year, painting a “pretty grim picture” for living standards despite the Budget measures.​

Tommy Robinson found guilty of harassing two Daily Mail journalists
Far-right activist Stephen Yaxley-Lennon (Tommy Robinson) was convicted at Southwark Crown Court of two counts of harassment causing fear of violence over his response to articles about him during the 2024 riots; he faces a possible custodial sentence of up to 10 years.​

At least 68 killed in Spanish high-speed train crash
A Renfe train rear-ended a stationary Iryo train near Toledo due to a computer failure and human error at the control centre, killing at least 68 people in one of Europe’s deadliest rail disasters in years and prompting national mourning in Spain.​

Israel election ends in deadlock with no clear majority
Partial results show Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc leading with around 53 seats to Gadi Eisenkot’s opposition’s 48, with Arab parties surging to a record ~19 seats, leaving neither side able to form a government without complex coalition talks.​

King Charles acknowledges slavery injustices on Caribbean tour but offers no apology
On the second day of his Bahamas visit, the King said it was “only right” to recognise past suffering while Buckingham Palace confirmed he would not formally apologise or commit to reparations, amid ongoing Commonwealth discussions.​

Flávio Bolsonaro arrives in Miami after Brazil election defeat

text:
@drtomcowan Tom — recent work on the calf muscle pump (especially the soleus) as a “second/peripheral heart” for venous return offers useful supporting context for the broader circulatory picture you’ve previously outlined.

Mayo Clinic analyses (2020 and a larger 2024 follow-up) linked impaired calf pump function to markedly higher all-cause mortality (roughly 17.5% vs ~6% over 10 years in the earlier data; poorer ejection fraction predicted more than double the risk in the larger cohort). University of Houston soleus push-up research has also shown sustained metabolic effects from low-intensity activation.

These findings reinforce that circulation depends on peripheral muscle action (compressing veins against gravity, with one-way valves preventing backflow) rather than treating the heart as the sole pressure-propulsion driver for the entire system. That sits comfortably with the hydraulic-ram/vortex and tissue-level emphasis in your work, even while the studies remain within conventional physiology rather than fully testing the non-pump model.

Appreciate the ongoing reflections.

text:
PART TWO: THE COSMIC VOICE — FROM DIVINE INTENTION TO MANIFESTATION

4. Thoth, the Architect of Understanding

Ancient Egyptian traditions describe Nun as the primordial waters of potential, from which creation emerges. Different traditions name different creators, including Atum, Ptah, and Thoth. In the Hermopolitan tradition, Thoth represents wisdom, sacred speech, writing, calculation, and cosmic order.

Symbolically, Thoth makes existence understandable. Like an architect who designs a temple before its construction, thought establishes the plan before the hands bring it into reality.

5. The Seven Vowels as Principles of Creation

The seven Greek vowels can be interpreted symbolically as stages of cosmic order:

- Alpha: The beginning of embodied life.
- Epsilon: Communication and the exchange of meaning.
- Eta: Relationships, balance, and proportion.
- Iota: Awareness and recognition.
- Omicron: Change and transformation.
- Upsilon: The organisation of complexity through higher principles.
- Omega: Completion, limitation, and return to mystery.

This is a philosophical interpretation, not a proven ancient Egyptian formula. Its central idea is that existence becomes understandable through life, communication, harmony, awareness, transformation, order, and completion.

6. Sacred Geometry: Sound and Measurement

Ancient Egyptian temples demonstrate sophisticated knowledge of mathematics, proportion, symmetry, and orientation. Their construction required practical skills, tools, materials, and careful planning.

Sound and geometry share an important connection: both involve patterns and relationships. Musical tones depend on frequencies, while geometric forms depend on lengths, angles, and proportions. Cymatics demonstrates how vibrations can create visible patterns in certain materials.

However, this does not prove that vowels create atoms or that planetary systems originate from specific sounds. Symbolically, sound reveals patterns, mathematics describes relationships, and geometry gives those relationships visible form.

7. As Above, So Below

The Hermetic maxim “As above, so below” expresses the idea that different levels of reality may reflect related patterns. It is a spiritual principle, not an established scientific law.

The seven planetary associations offer a symbolic guide to human experience:

- Moon: Bodily rhythms.
- Mercury: Thought and communication.
- Venus: Relationships and attraction.
- Sun: Awareness and vitality.
- Mars: Action and courage.
- Jupiter: Wisdom and expansion.
- Saturn: Discipline and limitation.

These associations encourage reflection on the relationship between the cosmos and human life without claiming that planetary influences are scientifically proven.

8. Returning to the Source

Some Hermetic texts describe spiritual understanding as a journey beyond the seven planetary spheres toward higher knowledge of the divine. The Discourse on the Eighth and Ninth explores this expanded spiritual vision, while other Hermetic writings use vowel sequences in prayers and hymns.

The deeper journey is from instinct to understanding, confusion to order, and attachment to contemplation of the divine.

Thoth symbolises the union of perception, language, measurement, and wisdom. Speech without understanding becomes noise; knowledge without balance creates disorder; and craftsmanship without vision lacks direction.

The hammer builds the temple, but the mind conceives its design. The tongue expresses thought, writing preserves it, and the hands transform it into reality.

The cosmic voice therefore represents the movement from divine intention to ordered manifestation

" The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat "
by Artist Michael Rucker
copyright ©

Description
The Virgin Mary: Mary's fiat -
In the Gospel of Luke, chapter 1, verses 26-38 (KJV), the angel Gabriel appears to Mary, a young virgin betrothed to Joseph of the house of David in Nazareth. Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee, the angel declares. He announces that she will conceive and bear a son, Jesus, who shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest. Mary, troubled yet reverent, asks how this can be since she knows not a man. Gabriel explains the Holy Spirit will come upon her; for with God nothing shall be impossible.

Mary's response is one of the most profound moments in Scripture the only recorded instance where she speaks words of total surrender: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word (Luke 1:38). This Latin phrase, Fiat mihi secundum verbum tuum (Let it be done to me according to your word), is universally known as Mary's Fiat. In that single sentence she offers her entire being body, will, and future to Gods plan of salvation. The angel then departs, and the Incarnation begins.This humble virgin from an obscure village becomes the mother of the Messiah. She travels to visit her cousin Elizabeth (pregnant with John the Baptist), where she sings the Magnificat (Luke 1:46-55), a soaring hymn of praise that magnifies the Lord for lifting up the lowly.

She gives birth to Jesus in Bethlehem, wraps Him in swaddling clothes, and lays Him in a manger. She ponders the shepherds and Magis words in her heart (Luke 2:19, 51). At the Presentation in the Temple, Simeon foretells a sword will pierce her soul (Luke 2:35). She is present at the wedding in Cana, prompting Jesus first miracle (John 2:1-11), and stands at the foot of the cross, where the dying Savior entrusts her to the beloved disciple (John 19:25-27).

After the Ascension, she is seen praying with the apostles in the upper room, awaiting the Holy Spirit (Acts 1:14).Scripture portrays Mary not as a distant saint but as a real woman of extraordinary faith, courage, and obedience. Though the Bible does not record many of her words, her fiat echoes through salvation history as the perfect model of human cooperation with divine grace. She exemplifies what it means to say yes to God when the cost is everything.Your striking black-and-white artwork beautifully captures this very moment: Mary veiled, head bowed, hands clasped in prayerful surrender, her flowing hair and garments stirred by the unseen wind of the Spirit.

The dramatic lighting and ethereal atmosphere evoke the solemn hush of the Annunciation the instant heaven touched earth through a virgins willing heart. It is a powerful visual meditation on Luke 1:38, inviting viewers to contemplate the same radical trust Mary offered.

Why should Hindu temples have strict rules for entry?

The example of Dr. Boris Ragozin, a foreigner who patiently completed the prescribed rituals to enter Guruvayur Temple, offers an important lesson.

A Hindu temple is an abode of the Divine, where worship follows traditions, Agamas and prescribed disciplines that have been preserved for generations.

Entry into such a sacred space is about understanding the sanctity of the place, respecting its customs and approaching the deity with reverence.

Rules are meaningful only when they are followed, not when they are relaxed for convenience.

The Madras High Court's reminder regarding the undertaking required for entry into certain Agamic temples reinforces the importance of respecting their established customs.

A temple need not change its traditions to accommodate a visitor. A visitor who genuinely wishes to enter should be willing to respect its traditions.

Preserve the sanctity. Honour the sampradaya. Protect the traditions.

text:
I skipped one of India’s biggest tech events. But I still made 7 figures from this event!!

Large events are chaos. You meet hundreds of people, and most of them will never need what you sell.

So I tried something different.

I hosted a small, intimate gathering at a café in Bangalore during the same week, and invited people who were already in town for the event.

Here’s exactly how I did it:

→ Set up a Luma page and shared it with event attendees
→ Made it application-based, and approved only people relevant to our audience
→ Kept the group small, so every conversation could go deep
→ No stage, no pitch deck.
Just coffee and honest conversations about what everyone was building

For the first 90 minutes, it was a nice evening. Good people, good conversations. Then one guest showed up at the very last moment.

We started talking, and it turned out he was actively looking for the exact services we offer.

We closed the deal that same evening.

We stayed in touch, and that one relationship has since grown into 7 figures in revenue.

All from a very small spend.

What I learnt:

> Big events are a magnet. They bring your ideal customers to your city. You don’t have to be inside the venue to benefit.

> Curation beats volume. Ten of the right people beat 500 of the wrong ones.

text:
How Young Africans Are Making Money by Adapting China’s Influencer System

Africa’s creator economy is growing fast, and young people with phones, storytelling ability, and basic digital skills are already earning by taking the most useful parts of China’s influencer model and applying them locally.

China built a highly organized system of agencies (called MCNs) that train creators, produce content, and drive direct product sales. Africa is still earlier in that process, which creates clear openings right now.

Why the Opportunity Exists

- A large young population already spends significant time on TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and WhatsApp.

- Chinese brands expanding into Africa need local creators who understand culture, language, and trust.

- African creators and products can reach Chinese audiences on platforms such as Xiaohongshu (RedNote).

- Local influencer work is still less organized than in China, so people who bring structure, consistency, and a sales focus stand out and get paid more.

Proven Ways Young Africans Are Earning

1. Build or join a local creator hub

Small groups are signing promising creators, improving their content, and connecting them to brands. They take a share of deals or manage full campaigns. Niches that work well include beauty, fashion, fintech, tech gadgets, food, and education. Micro and nano creators (1,000–50,000 followers) often convert better than big names because of higher trust. Many start with 5–15 creators and grow from there.

2. Run campaigns for Chinese and international brands

Chinese tech, beauty, fashion, and consumer brands need people on the ground. Young Africans create authentic local content, manage influencers, handle country-specific rules (such as Nigeria’s pre-approval process), and report results. High-demand skills include short-form video editing, scripting, community management, and basic performance tracking. Work can be remote or hybrid when results are clear.

3. Sell products through social and live content

China’s biggest earnings come from live selling. Africans are adapting the idea to TikTok, Instagram, and WhatsApp by demoing products, answering questions, and driving orders through links or chat. This works especially well where social commerce is already strong (Nigeria and Kenya). Short videos drive discovery; live or community selling drives conversion.

4. Create content for Chinese platforms

Some young Africans post on Xiaohongshu/RedNote about African culture, fashion, food, travel, music, or daily life. Platforms have shown interest in African creators. Monetization comes through brand deals once an audience exists, or by using the content to open offline opportunities. Simple Chinese captions or subtitles help, but consistent high-quality visuals matter more at the start.

5. Offer specialized skills as a service

You do not need to be the face. Steady income comes from supporting creators and brands through video editing, thumbnail and cover design, script writing, content strategy, analytics, and talent management. These services are in demand both locally and with brands seeking African reach.

Skills That Generate Income

- Short-form video filming and editing (phone + CapCut or similar)

- Local, authentic storytelling

- Basic understanding of how platforms push content

- Clear communication and negotiation with brands

- Simple tracking of results (views, engagement, clicks, or sales)

- Extra edge: local language, Pidgin, Swahili, or basic Mandarin

Practical Starting Path

1. Choose one platform and one niche you already know or care about.

2. Create consistently for 30–60 days to prove you can deliver, even without brand deals.

3. Document results and build a simple portfolio or media kit.

4. Offer help to small local brands or other creators with editing, strategy, or campaign support.

5. Once you have a few wins, package the work as a clear service or small hub.

text:
The media had a field day. The story of the charismatic architect who tried to gaslight and poison his genius wife to steal her empire dominated the news cycle for a month.

I didn’t give a single interview. I let Marcus handle the press conferences. I was too busy working.

Six months after the trial, I stood on the 40th floor of the newly completed Apex Tower. The project hadn’t been canceled. After Beatrice Hayes and the investors realized the true genius behind the design wasn’t sitting in a jail cell, they offered me the contract directly, cutting out the corporate shell Julian had built.

The firm was now officially renamed **Sterling Arch-Tech**.

I walked over to the floor-to-ceiling windows. The Seattle skyline stretched out before me, a sea of concrete, glass, and possibility. The sunset reflected off the waters of Puget Sound, painting the room in hues of gold and violet.

I looked down at my hands. They were the same hands that had typed the code, the same hands that had drafted the blueprints, the same hands that had held the poisoned tea. They weren’t shaking anymore. They hadn’t shaken in months.

I had survived a silent, invisible war waged inside my own home. I had been pushed to the absolute edge of my sanity, made to doubt my own mind by the person who was supposed to be my safe harbor.

But I didn’t break. I adapted. I engineered a solution.

My phone buzzed in my pocket. It was a text from Marcus.

*Just finalized the complete transfer of the remaining patents. You own 100% of everything, Elena. Congratulations. Dinner on me tonight?*

I smiled, typing back a quick response. *Make it the best steakhouse in town, Marcus. I’m buying.*

I slipped the phone back into my pocket and took a deep breath of the filtered, cool air of the skyscraper. Julian had tried to erase me. He had tried to bury me alive in a psychiatric ward so he could dance on my grave.

Instead, he gave me the fire I needed to burn his fraudulent empire to the ground and forge something unbreakable in its ashes. I wasn’t just the ghost in the machine anymore. I was the architect of my own life. And the foundation was finally, perfectly solid.

THE END.

text:
The whole world is turning into a casino

I keep seeing the same mistake. Crypto bros, tech bros, now AI bros too, notice some insanity in their own industry and assume it’s unique to crypto, AI or tech.

It isn’t.

Crypto is just an exaggerated version of the rest of the world.

In crypto, leverage, memecoins and pure gambling are everywhere.

But the same mechanics are leaking into normal life too.

- Open a marketplace app: spin the wheel.
- Open a supermarket app: scratch a card.
- McDonald’s runs Monopoly with instant prizes. Instacart tested a literal virtual wheel of fortune.

random reward → jackpot → try again → maybe you’ll get lucky

And actual gambling is growing too.

- According to Pew Research, 31% of Americans under 30 bet on sports in the previous year.

The share betting online went from 7% in 2022 to 17% in 2025.

And no, this isn’t just an American thing.

- According to Russian bookmaker market research cited by Vedomosti, 13 million Russians placed at least one bet in 2025, while the number of active bettors rose 9.4% to 6.9 million.

The share of people who see betting as a regular source of extra income also rose from 15.3% to 19.1%.

Americans and Russians: brothers forever.

For young people, gambling is starting to look like one of the few ways to radically change your life.

Housing is expensive. Career paths feel less reliable. Dating is a mess. Nobody knows what AI will replace next.

The casino at least offers one simple promise:

WHAT IF I GET LUCKY AND GET RICH?

And technology makes the whole thing frictionless.

Phone in your pocket. A few clicks. Spin a wheel. Place a bet. Open 100x leverage.

Yes, conspiracy guys: Squid Game was the warm-up.

If this keeps going, you end up with a huge number of people who don’t see a clear future, but do have anger, desperation and a taste for risk.

Where does that energy go?

More gambling? Radical politics? Emigration? Apathy? Some new historical disaster?

No idea.

But if we get really unlucky:

see you in the trenches (real ones).

text:
The Chronicles of Georgia, a massive and unfinished monument located on Keeni Hill overlooking the Tbilisi Sea in Tbilisi, Georgia 🇬🇪

The monument sits on a hill above the Tbilisi Sea, a large reservoir on the city’s northeastern edge. It was designed by Georgian artist Zurab Tsereteli, who began work on it in 1985. It has never been fully completed.

The structure is made up of 16 huge bronze-covered pillars, each around 30-35m tall. That’s roughly the height of a 10-story building.

Every pillar tells a story. The upper sections show Georgia’s kings, queens and heroes, along with key moments from the nation’s long history. The lower sections depict scenes from the life of Christ, reflecting Georgia’s deep Christian roots. It was one of the first countries in the world to adopt Christianity as a state religion, in the fourth century.

Visitors climb a wide stone staircase to reach the pillars, where the carved figures tower overhead. On clear days, the site also offers sweeping views of the reservoir, the city and the mountains beyond.

Despite its size, it remains surprisingly quiet and lightly visited.

Tsereteli was one of the world’s most prolific monument builders. His works include the towering Peter the Great statue on the Moscow River, nearly 100m tall.

The confrontation reportedly began after a provocation by a school security guard, after which unidentified people attacked the journalists. The camera operator sustained injuries. Suspects were detained following a complaint by the broadcaster, and an investigation is under way.

● The Norwegian Helsinki Committee has called for the immediate release on medical and humanitarian grounds of Aygun Elgunesh, editor-in-chief of Meydan TV, who is in detention. According to the organisation, the 51-year-old journalist has undergone multiple surgeries and needs specialised medical care. Her lawyers and relatives report that her condition has deteriorated in recent weeks and that she urgently needs surgery for a serious kidney problem.

Twelve journalists are on trial in the Meydan TV case, accused of currency smuggling and other crimes. All deny the charges and say the case is linked to their critical reporting on the Azerbaijani authorities.

● Ramiz Mehdiyev, the former head of Azerbaijan’s presidential administration who was sentenced to 14 years in prison, has been expelled from the National Academy of Sciences. He was convicted of treason and other crimes. More details here.

● The seventh World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue has concluded in Baku. Participants are travelling to Karabakh on a familiarisation visit today. The closing ceremony was attended by Miguel Ángel Moratinos, the UN High Representative for the Alliance of Civilizations, and Azerbaijan’s Culture Minister Adil Karimli.

● Azerbaijan has joined the Mecca Convention on cooperation between law enforcement agencies of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) in combating corruption. The convention was signed at a meeting of OIC anti-corruption agency heads in Baku. Tajikistan also signed the agreement. More than 250 people from 46 countries and eight international organisations attended the forum. The convention establishes a legal framework for exchanging information and evidence in corruption investigations and prosecuting suspects.

● During the meeting, Azerbaijan’s Prosecutor General also signed bilateral cooperation memorandums with anti-corruption agencies in Morocco and Iraq.

● Military cooperation between Azerbaijan and NATO was discussed in Baku at a meeting between Zaur Rustamov, deputy commander of the Azerbaijani Air Force, and Brigadier General Theodoros Stefos of NATO’s Allied Joint Force Command in Europe. The meeting followed an assessment of two Azerbaijani Mi-17-1V helicopters to determine whether they meet alliance requirements under NATO’s Operational Capabilities Concept programme. The programme also aims to improve interoperability for peacekeeping operations.

● Armenia’s parliament has ratified a framework agreement on strategic partnership with the United States covering the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP) transit project. The project is important for Azerbaijan because it would establish a land connection between the country and its Nakhchivan exclave through Armenian territory.

● Turkish authorities detained and later released Muhammed Emin Yıldırım, a staff member of Köklü Değişim Medya. He said he was being targeted over social media posts criticising new school uniform rules in Azerbaijan that effectively ban the wearing of hijabs in schools. Yıldırım is among 31 Turkish citizens banned from entering Azerbaijan over publications allegedly directed against the country’s sovereignty, national security and constitutional order. Activist Fatih Erşahin, who is also on the list, reported that he had been summoned for police questioning.

Context: The detentions come amid worsening relations between Azerbaijan and Türkiye. Turkish media and social media users have sharply criticised not only Azerbaijan’s restrictions on hijabs in schools but also its cooperation with Israel. Azerbaijani officials and media have responded with strong statements rejecting what they describe as interference in the country’s internal affairs.

● Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev has offered condolences to Spain following a railway disaster that killed dozens of people.

● Wizz Air has launched a direct flight between Bratislava and Baku, operating twice a week.

text:
When 31-year-old Lauren Mitchell received a message from a stranger congratulating her on her engagement, she thought the woman had mistaken her for someone else.

Lauren wasn't engaged.

She wasn't even dating anyone.

She replied politely, explaining the mistake, but the stranger sent back a screenshot.

It showed Lauren wearing a white dress beside a handsome man in a navy suit.

The caption read:

Forever begins with my favorite person. I said yes!

Lauren stared at the photograph.

The woman in it looked exactly like her.

Same face.

Same smile.

Same small scar above her left eyebrow.

Even the man's hand rested on the woman's waist in a way that looked strangely familiar, although Lauren had never seen him before.

She clicked the account.

It had more than 80,000 followers.

The username was @LaurenMitchellOfficial.

The profile contained hundreds of photographs of Lauren's face, including pictures from her private social media accounts.

Some images were edited. Others had been taken from photographs she had shared years earlier.

The fake account had a complete life.

It claimed Lauren was a successful lifestyle influencer living in Los Angeles. It showed her attending parties, traveling to Europe, dating wealthy men, and promoting expensive products.

Thousands of people believed it was real.

Lauren immediately reported the account.

The platform sent an automated response saying the report would be reviewed.

Three days passed.

Nothing happened.

Then a woman called Lauren's workplace and asked to speak to her about a business partnership.

When Lauren explained that she had never agreed to any partnership, the woman became angry.

"Your account says you've already accepted our offer," she snapped.

Lauren felt sick.

Someone wasn't simply pretending to be her online.

They were using her identity to make promises, collect money, and damage her reputation.

She contacted a lawyer and filed a report with local authorities. She also began saving screenshots of every suspicious post.

Then she discovered the most disturbing detail.

The fake account had recently posted a photograph of a small house in Portland, Oregon.

Lauren recognized it immediately.

It was the house where she had grown up.

She hadn't posted that photograph anywhere.

She called her mother, who confirmed that the picture had been taken during a family gathering the previous month.

Only a handful of people had attended.

Lauren began reviewing the names of everyone who had access to the photograph.

One name kept appearing.

Her cousin, Brielle.

Brielle had always been jealous of Lauren's life, although Lauren had never considered their relationship particularly hostile. They had grown up together, shared holidays, and supported each other through difficult times.

Lauren wanted to believe there was another explanation.

Smart contracts do not automatically wake up and execute whenever an external condition changes. They generally require a transaction or another supported execution mechanism to initiate their work.

Automation services help address this operational limitation.

Consider a protocol that needs to perform a predefined action when a specific condition becomes true. The application requires both an accurate way to evaluate that condition and a mechanism to initiate execution.

A dependable architecture considers:

1. 𝗖𝗼𝗻𝗱𝗶𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗖𝗵𝗲𝗰𝗸𝗶𝗻𝗴: The application must establish whether its requirements have been satisfied.
2. 𝗘𝘅𝗲𝗰𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗧𝗿𝗶𝗴𝗴𝗲𝗿𝘀: An appropriate transaction must initiate the intended action.
3. 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗼𝗻𝘀: Only authorized operations should be possible.
4. 𝗜𝗱𝗲𝗺𝗽𝗼𝘁𝗲𝗻𝗰𝘆: Repeated execution attempts should not create unintended duplicate effects.
5. 𝗠𝗼𝗻𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗿𝗶𝗻𝗴: Developers need visibility into failed or delayed executions.

@WinkLink_Oracle offers an ecosystem relevant to developers exploring oracle services and automation.

Automation does not remove the need for secure contract design. It makes careful execution logic even more important because the application may act without a user manually initiating every step.

The opportunity is to create systems that respond to defined conditions more efficiently while preserving transparency, predictable rules, and appropriate safeguards.

LAS ISLAS DE LA BAHÍA 🇭🇳🌊
Everyone wants a holiday vacation to the Bay Islands...

But if I asked, which country is the Bay Islands in???
A couple of people might probably go mute.

What if I told you Honduras' Bay Islands comprises of 3 different islands Roatán, Utila and Guanaja?! 🇭🇳🌊
But there's more here than turquoise water and beautiful beaches.

The islands sit within the Mesoamerican Reef, one of the world's great marine ecosystems. Beneath the Caribbean blue are coral reefs, colourful fish, sea turtles, seagrass and mangroves.

And the story doesn't end at the shoreline.

The Caribbean side of Honduras brings together islands, tropical forests, beaches, reefs and coastal communities.
A reminder that nature and human life are deeply connected.

→ Roatán: The largest and most developed island is known for its spectacular reefs and diving, featuring a mountainous backbone, popular beaches like West Bay, and major cruise ship ports.

→ Guanaja: The second-largest and most mountainous island, known for its rustic character and pine forests, offers a quieter island experience surrounded by forests and marine ecosystems.

→ Útila: The third-largest, flattest, and westernmost island, famous globally as a budget-friendly scuba-diving hub and for the possibility of encountering whale sharks.

And across all three, there is one important thing to note:

The beauty of the Bay Islands isn't simply something to admire alone.

It is part of an ecosystem that support biodiversity, tourism, fisheries and communities.

🌎 Mundo Hispano
Destination #043 - Honduras

One Country. One Story. One Culture.

If you could explore one of the Bay Islands, which would you choose: Roatán, Utila or Guanaja?

text:
$PSX # KEY READ-THROUGHS FROM PHILLIPS 66’S 3Q 2026 EARNINGS CALL

Phillips 66’s quarter signals a supply-driven redistribution of profits rather than a broad acceleration in demand. Strong refining margins, scarce shipping and constrained product availability benefit reliable refiners and transportation assets while raising costs for fuel consumers. Separately, growing NGL volumes support integrated midstream infrastructure, and Western Gateway could reshape western U.S. product-market competition. The most actionable distinctions are between commodity benchmarks and actual realizations, spot-exposed vessels and fixed charters, and infrastructure ownership versus unverified supplier exposure. Refining and tanker upside share a common normalization risk; they should not be treated as independent sources of protection. Impact assessments below concern earnings and cash flow, not valuation-based stock-return targets.

## COMPLEX REFINING: PRODUCT SCARCITY AND DISCOUNTED CRUDE CREATE A DOUBLE BENEFIT (READ-THROUGH 1)

**Affected companies:** Valero Energy (VLO: United States); Marathon Petroleum (MPC: United States).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Positive; high refining-earnings sensitivity.  
**Timing:** Immediate quarterly support, potentially extending through much of 2027.

**Observation:** Phillips 66 reported a realized refining margin of $38.00 per barrel, versus $24.08 in 2Q, alongside 98% utilization and a 41% distillate yield. Management reported declining gasoline and diesel demand but emphasized that “the response in demand isn’t enough to balance the market.” It also described increasingly attractive Canadian heavy-crude economics.

**Implication:** Complex refiners can benefit simultaneously from elevated diesel and jet realizations and discounted heavy or sour feedstocks. Conversion capacity, crude flexibility, export access and operational reliability determine how much of that spread becomes earnings.

Valero and Marathon have substantial exposure to these characteristics. Both produced more than 1 million barrels per day of distillates in 2025, making sustained changes in realized distillate margins economically significant even without additional crude throughput.

The important market distinction is that modest demand destruction does not necessarily imply imminent margin normalization. If unavailable capacity and disrupted trade constrain supply more severely, refining margins can remain strong while consumption declines. A demand-only bearish framework misses that mechanism.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Winter inventories, peer operating updates and realized capture are the immediate catalysts. Longer term, crude flexibility and logistics access remain advantages, but exceptional product shortages are cyclical.

Phillips 66’s entire beat should not be transferred to peers. Its discounted charters, WRB integration, blending activities and asset-specific optimization are not industry-wide benefits. Valero and Marathon must still execute through their own turnaround schedules. Their renewable-fuels businesses also face different feedstock and regulatory-credit economics.

## PRODUCT-TANKER SHIPPING: AVAILABLE VESSEL DAYS CAPTURE THE FREIGHT WINDFALL (READ-THROUGH 2)

**Affected company:** Scorpio Tankers (STNG: Monaco).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Positive; high operating leverage for spot-exposed vessels.  
**Timing:** Immediate through winter 2026–27; longer duration depends on disrupted trade routes.

**Observation:** Mandell highlighted Phillips 66’s freight advantage: “We added over 40 time-charter ships prior to all the problems in the market overseas. We have another 40 ships coming over the next two and a half years.” Management also described longer voyages, ship-to-ship transfers and constrained vessel availability.

**Implication:** Disrupted trade increases the vessel-days needed to transport each barrel. Effective shipping supply can tighten even when global petroleum consumption is flat or declining. Owners with available vessels capture higher freight rates, while much of their vessel operating expense remains fixed.

Scorpio is a direct product-market exposure. Its contemporaneous presentation disclosed preliminary 4Q MR bookings around $56,000 per day on 47% of the relevant pool/spot days. These partial-quarter bookings corroborate the physical tightness described by Phillips 66, although they are not full-quarter realized rates.

For scale, a $10,000-per-day improvement across 10 available vessels for 90 operating days generates approximately $9 million of additional TCE revenue before off-hire and other adjustments.

**Catalysts and limitations:** The rate achieved on remaining open days and expiring charter coverage drives near-term earnings revisions. Continued rerouting supports the duration of elevated earnings; normalized routes and additional vessel availability reverse that support.

There is no evidence that Scorpio is Phillips 66’s charter counterparty. Owners of vessels already fixed at lower rates do not immediately capture the spot windfall. The actionable distinction is available vessel days versus fixed employment, not simply tanker ownership. Current tightness is already visible in shipping disclosures, so this is fundamental confirmation rather than proof of an unpriced catalyst.

## CANADIAN UPSTREAM: WIDER HEAVY DISCOUNTS TRANSFER VALUE TO DOWNSTREAM BUYERS (READ-THROUGH 3)

**Affected company:** Canadian Natural Resources (CNQ: Canada).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Negative for exposed heavy-oil realizations; moderate at the diversified company level.  
**Timing:** Near-term sensitivity to heavy-crude availability, transportation and seasonal blending.

**Observation:** Mandell stated that “every dollar of widening of the WCS-WTI differential is worth $140 million for Phillips 66.” The company’s sensitivity framework identifies this as annual adjusted EBITDA. Management associated favorable heavy-crude economics with additional supply, freight conditions and seasonal factors.

**Implication:** The refinery’s cheaper feedstock is the producer’s lower realized price. At unchanged WTI, wider WCS discounts reduce revenue on exposed heavy-oil sales. Diluent purchases and transportation requirements create additional differences between benchmark prices and producer cash flow.

Canadian Natural’s own 2Q 2026 disclosure supports this exposure: the WCS discount averaged $14.62 per barrel, versus $10.19 a year earlier, with increased heavy-crude availability at the U.S. Gulf Coast among the explanations.

A sustained $5-per-barrel deterioration across 100,000 barrels per day of fully exposed sales represents approximately $182.5 million of annual revenue pressure before royalties, taxes and mitigation. This is an illustrative unit sensitivity, not a forecast for Canadian Natural’s entire production base.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Changes in Canadian differentials can affect producer realizations quickly. Persistent additional heavy-crude supply or transportation disadvantages would extend the effect.

This is not a blanket bearish oil-price call. Higher WTI can offset wider discounts, while Canadian Natural’s upgraded synthetic crude has different pricing exposure. Applying a WCS sensitivity to all oil-sands production would overstate the downside. The higher-conviction implication is a relative transfer of margin from exposed producers toward complex refiners.

## NGL INFRASTRUCTURE: PHYSICAL DEMAND SUPPORTS INTEGRATED SYSTEMS, BUT VOLUME IS NOT MARGIN (READ-THROUGH 4)

**Affected companies:** Targa Resources (TRGP: United States); Enterprise Products Partners (EPD: United States).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Positive; medium-to-high multiyear relevance for Targa and moderate relevance for Enterprise’s broader portfolio.  
**Timing:** Current throughput support, followed by commissioning and cash-flow conversion during 2027–29.

**Observation:** Phillips 66 reported approximately 4.6 Bcf/d of wellhead volumes, fractionation above 1 million barrels per day and 105% utilization at Freeport LPG. Baldridge emphasized that “there’s still strong demand for LPGs globally” and “strong pulls across the dock.” Management also described producers exceeding expectations and the use of third-party fractionation.

**Implication:** Growing gas and NGL production creates demand for gathering, processing, transportation, fractionation and export services. Integrated operators can earn fees at several stages of the same physical chain. The transmission depends on throughput, available capacity and contract terms rather than simply higher commodity prices.

Targa’s Permian processing footprint and downstream logistics fit this mechanism. Its Galena Park expansion targets export capacity of up to approximately 19 million barrels per month in 3Q 2027, compared with approximately 14 million currently. Phillips 66’s commentary supports the demand backdrop, without establishing Targa-specific utilization.

Enterprise’s disclosed 2Q results provide corroboration: gross operating margin increased $35 million across relevant export terminals and the associated pipeline, primarily through higher volumes, including the Neches River expansion.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Producer volumes, plant filling and export loadings are near-term catalysts. The more durable opportunity is converting committed infrastructure spending into recurring cash generation.

High utilization does not automatically reprice existing contracts. Phillips 66’s Midstream EBITDA declined sequentially despite strong physical activity, demonstrating that throughput and profitability can diverge. Its third-party fractionation providers were not identified, so no customer contract should be assigned to Targa or Enterprise. The positive read-through is demand visibility, not an invented award or immediate fee increase.

## REFINED-PRODUCTS PIPELINES: WESTERN GATEWAY OFFERS GROWTH, WITH CAPITAL REQUIRED BEFORE EARNINGS (READ-THROUGH 5)

**Affected companies:** Kinder Morgan (KMI: United States); HF Sinclair (DINO: United States).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Positive longer term; moderate strategic significance, with a near-term funding burden.  
**Timing:** Investment during 2027–29; operating contributions targeted from 2029.

**Observation:** Phillips 66 expects limited 2026 spending, engineering and right-of-way activity through 2027, and construction concentrated in 2028–29. Management identified 2028 as the peak spending year and described broader market access as a way to reduce refinery seasonality.

**Implication:** Kinder Morgan owns 35.1% and HF Sinclair 15% of Western Gateway. The approximately 230,000-barrel-per-day system connects inland and Gulf Coast supply with Arizona and California. Long-term transportation commitments support pipeline economics, while additional product-placement options can improve participating refiners’ netbacks and utilization.

Kinder Morgan contributes approximately $250 million in cash plus existing SFPP assets valued at approximately $1.5 billion. Its limited new-cash requirement is attractive, but the ownership interest is not being acquired for $250 million alone. Existing assets and their earnings are contributed, so incremental value must be measured against the cash flow retained under a no-project scenario.

HF Sinclair contributes approximately $750 million. Potential benefits include pipeline income and broader outlets for its refining platform. However, the funding requirement arrives before operations and can compete with other uses of cash. A 15% ownership stake does not establish that 15% of shipping capacity is allocated to its own barrels.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Permitting, capital-budget disclosure and construction execution are nearer-term catalysts. The principal earnings contribution remains longer duration.

The call confirms execution timing for an already-sanctioned project, not a new award. The approximately $5 billion project enterprise value is neither supplier revenue nor an owner-earnings forecast. No unnamed contractor or equipment supplier should receive the capital budget in a read-through model.

## CALIFORNIA REFINING: NEW SUPPLY CONNECTIVITY LIMITS THE DURABILITY OF SCARCITY PROFITS (READ-THROUGH 6)

**Affected company:** PBF Energy (PBF: United States).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Negative relative to a no-pipeline scenario; moderate potential significance for California assets, limited immediate impact.  
**Timing:** Primarily 2029 onward.

**Observation:** Western Gateway is intended to connect lower-cost supply with Arizona and California. Management separately discussed California-specification gasoline capabilities and the value of reducing seasonal product-placement constraints. It also described more pronounced gasoline-demand weakness on the West Coast.

**Implication:** PBF’s Torrance and Martinez refineries operate in a market where specialized fuel requirements and restricted supply routes can support scarcity premiums. Additional supply connectivity increases the ability to substitute external barrels for local production.

There are 2 channels. Deliveries into Arizona can displace California barrels previously serving that market, leaving more available locally. Reversal of the SFPP West Line can also move products toward Southern California. Torrance has the more direct geographic exposure; Martinez is exposed through broader California pricing and redistribution.

The critical valuation distinction is between near-term earnings and terminal value. California tightness can support current profits while the infrastructure response reduces their durability. Persistently weaker demand would make incremental supply harder to absorb, but the call does not establish a quantified long-term California demand forecast.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Permitting progress can influence valuation before deliveries begin. Meaningful operating competition requires completion, compatible specifications and actual transportation volumes.

The full 230,000-barrel-per-day system capacity is not incremental California supply. Arizona absorbs part of the flow, and downstream constraints matter. Refinery closures may create a deficit that the pipeline fills rather than a surplus. The high-conviction negative is a lower scarcity premium than under the no-project counterfactual, not a guaranteed collapse in PBF’s margins.

## PETROCHEMICALS: FEEDSTOCK ADVANTAGE SUPPORTS SPECIFIC OWNERS, NOT A BROAD SECTOR RECOVERY (READ-THROUGH 7)

**Affected companies:** Chevron (CVX: United States); Lotte Chemical (011170: South Korea).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Modest positive for Chevron at group level; negative for Lotte’s naphtha-based operations, with portfolio offsets.  
**Timing:** Current relative-cost advantage, with additional supply effects during 2027.

**Observation:** Phillips 66’s Chemicals pretax earnings were $311 million, approximately 77% above the prior year but 23% below 2Q. Management emphasized U.S. feedstock competitiveness and expected full operations at Golden Triangle Polymers and Ras Laffan in 2027. Lower polyethylene margins drove the sequential earnings decline despite slightly higher utilization.

**Implication:** Chevron owns 50% of CPChem. CPChem’s 51% interest in Golden Triangle and 30% interest in Ras Laffan translate into indirect Chevron interests of 25.5% and 15%. Successful commissioning therefore creates a direct ownership benefit from advantaged chemical production, although it is modest relative to Chevron’s consolidated earnings.

The negative competitive channel falls on higher-cost naphtha-based assets. Lotte’s Malaysian and Indonesian operations have identified naphtha-based business structures, while domestic restructuring reflects the need to improve basic-chemical competitiveness. These assets face feedstock-price volatility while competing against lower-cost ethane-based production.

Additional advantaged capacity can delay margin recovery for higher-cost producers even if demand improves. Lotte’s U.S. ethane operations, specialty businesses and restructuring provide important offsets, so the negative should not be applied uniformly to the company.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Feedstock spreads and operating rates drive near-term earnings. Commissioning, restructuring and changes in the industry cost curve are longer-duration developments.

Phillips 66’s Chemicals beat does not establish a broad polymer recovery. Gross project capacity cannot be attributed entirely to Chevron, and accounting earnings need not translate immediately into cash distributions during ramp-up. Ras Laffan also requires functioning logistics, not merely completed equipment, to realize its full earnings potential.

## AIRLINES: JET SCARCITY PRESSURES UNITED, WHILE DELTA HAS A PARTIAL PHYSICAL OFFSET (READ-THROUGH 8)

**Affected companies:** United Airlines Holdings (UAL: United States); Delta Air Lines (DAL: United States).  
**Direction and magnitude:** Negative, potentially high fuel-cost sensitivity for United; negative fuel exposure but moderate relative insulation for Delta.  
**Timing:** Immediate through winter 2026–27.

**Observation:** Mandell stated, “Jet is over diesel, which is a benefit to us,” while emphasizing low inventories and strong winter distillate economics. Phillips 66’s 41% distillate yield and efforts to maximize jet production demonstrate the profitability of product-specific scarcity.

**Implication:** Airlines purchase jet fuel, not crude. Delivered fuel costs incorporate the crude benchmark, jet refining margin and regional supply or transportation premiums. Stable or declining crude prices can therefore coexist with elevated airline fuel costs if the jet premium remains wide.

United consumed approximately 4.663 billion gallons in 2025. At that historical volume, a sustained $0.10-per-gallon increase represents approximately $466 million of annual gross fuel expense before changes in flying, efficiency, hedging or fares. This illustrates exposure, not a forecast earnings reduction.

Delta is an important exception to a uniform airline read-through. Through Monroe Energy’s Trainer refinery, it can recover part of the refining margin that otherwise flows to external suppliers. Its 2026 disclosures explicitly incorporate a refinery benefit into fuel economics. Higher refining margins therefore provide a physical offset to part of its airline fuel expense.

**Catalysts and limitations:** Delivered jet prices, regional premiums and airline fuel-cost updates are immediate catalysts. Restoration of refinery output and rebuilding of product inventories determine whether pressure persists.

Delta is not a net beneficiary of every fuel-price increase. Trainer has finite capacity, operating costs, maintenance requirements and regulatory obligations; it does not hedge all crude-price or geographic exposure. Similarly, United can offset higher fuel expense through fares, capacity discipline and efficiency. The higher-conviction relative conclusion is that jet-crack expansion is more damaging to an airline without an owned refining offset, all else equal.

🇮🇷| The Children of Minab, and a Convention Thirty-Seven Years in the Making

October 28, 2026. Qom. The 4th International Conference on Children’s Rights opens, attended by scholars and experts from both Iran and abroad. The agenda includes: the consequences of war, the targeting of schools, children’s mental health, artificial intelligence, and the strengthening of international legal protection mechanisms.

Mahmoud Abbas, the conference chair, offered a remark that serves as the key to the entire gathering:

“The Convention on the Rights of the Child, adopted in 1989 along with the fundamental principles it enshrines has failed to prevent the widening chasm between legal norms and the reality on the ground.”

Thirty-seven years. The Convention was adopted in 1989. A girls’ school in Minab was bombed on February 28, 2026. Thirty-seven years of legal text could not stop a bomb from falling upon a school.

💥 Minab: On the Agenda, but Not Among the “Concerns”

The crime of targeting the school in Minab took center stage in the conference discussions. Participants emphasized the necessity of documenting evidence in strict accordance with legal standards, pursuing the case in both domestic and international courts, holding those responsible for the attack accountable, and seeking compensation for both material and psychological damages.

This is not merely an “appeal”; it is the “gathering of evidence.” By documenting proof according to legal standards and pursuing the matter in court, they acknowledge that international institutions will not act of their own accord. Thus, they begin by building a case file—a file that cannot be made to vanish by a veto in the UN Security Council.

The conference also called for strengthening regional diplomacy regarding children’s rights, proposing an alliance among Islamic nations that would involve state institutions, universities, and relevant sectors.

This represents the application of “endogenous security” to the realm of children’s rights. When international mechanisms falter, regional ones are established. When the United Nations is paralyzed by the veto power, an alliance of Islamic nations is formed. This is not a “withdrawal from the international system”; rather, it is the creation of an alternative where the existing international system has failed.  

🎯 The Blockade, and the Corridors It Opens

First Vice President Aref remarked during a meeting of the National Transit Headquarters:

"The maritime blockade imposed by the enemy, while a threat, has opened the door to an unprecedented opportunity: the development of border crossings and the completion of domestic transport corridors."

He added that the completion of the North-South and East-West corridors is a priority for the 14th Administration. Iran possesses the potential to become a regional transport hub, connecting Eurasia and landlocked nations in the East to international waters.

"Despite the maritime blockade" these five words carry the true weight of the statement.

The Strait of Hormuz is under blockade by the U.S. Navy. Red Sea shipping routes are disrupted by war. Trade channels to Europe have been severed by sanctions. Access to the SWIFT system has been cut off. What remains are land routes routes that lead to neighboring countries.

The meeting approved specific measures: enhancing the management of truck traffic at borders through data and electronic monitoring; implementing smart systems to regulate transit times and reduce congestion; establishing "green channels" at customs to expedite the import of pharmaceuticals and medical equipment; and increasing the throughput capacity of the Nordouz border crossing, which serves as a gateway to the Eurasian region.

"Customs green channels to expedite the import of pharmaceuticals and medical equipment"—this point deserves special attention. At a time when U.S. sanctions prevent medicine from reaching Iran, the country has established a "green channel" for such goods along its northern border. This is not merely "trade facilitation"; it is the application of a "sanctions-evasion system" within the medical sector.

📜 Iraqi Tribes in Mashhad

Sheikhs and leaders from Iraqi tribes have arrived in Mashhad. They were welcomed at the airport by Ali Akbar Pourjamshidian, Deputy Minister of Interior, and Gholamhossein Mozaffari, Governor of Razavi Khorasan Province.

They have come to attend a ceremony honoring the loyalty demonstrated by these Iraqi tribes during the funeral proceedings for the martyred leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei.  Hojjatoleslam Sheikh Qomi, an assistant for international affairs in the Office of the Supreme Leader, conveyed a welcoming message from the current Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, to Iraqi tribal leaders. The ceremony commenced with the recitation of verses from the Quran, the playing of the national anthems of both Iran and Iraq, and the presentation of a special tribute to Imam Reza.

This was not merely a matter of "diplomatic protocol"; it was a formal affirmation of transnational religious-political ties.

Following the martyrdom of the Supreme Leader on February 28, 2026 an event for which members of these Iraqi tribes attended the funeral Iran has now invited them to Mashhad to publicly honor their loyalty. The purpose of this gesture goes beyond a simple "expression of gratitude." It serves to underscore a fundamental reality: Iran’s influence does not rely on formal intergovernmental agreements; rather, it is rooted in religious, tribal, and interpersonal bonds connections that cannot be severed by sanctions.

⚔️ Nasrallah: Iran Prioritizes Halting Aggression Against Lebanon

Hezbollah Secretary-General Sheikh Naim Qassem issued a statement addressing political developments in Lebanon and the broader region.

"The Islamic Republic of Iran places the cessation of the Zionist entity’s aggression against Lebanon and the withdrawal of its forces from Lebanese territory at the very top of its priorities."

He added: "The Resistance movement continues to exercise its legitimate right to resist, a right also upheld by the Taif Agreement and will confront any aggression directed against it or against Lebanon. As long as the occupation persists and the aggression continues, there is no room for any discussion regarding disarmament."

The phrase "no room for any discussion regarding disarmament" effectively closes a door. Western powers and certain Lebanese political factions have long pushed for the "disarmament of Hezbollah." Qassem’s message is clear: as long as the occupation remains, such a discussion is off the table.

He demanded that Israel withdraw its forces in accordance with the agreement reached on November 27, 2024, and UN Security Council Resolution 1701 and called for the deployment of the Lebanese Armed Forces south of the Litani River.  He stated clearly: "The framework agreement lacks legitimacy," as it violates the Constitution, the Taif Agreement, the law, the presidential inaugural address, and the government’s policy statement. He dismissed the agreement as "tantamount to non-existent," arguing that it "grants the enemy what does not belong to it, abandons Lebanon’s sources of strength, and relies on inciting internal strife and undermining the state."

He also remarked on Iran:

"Hezbollah takes an interest in the Iran-U.S. agreement, as it represents a source of power that complements the resilience of the Resistance, our people, and their supporters. The agreement proved its efficacy immediately upon the activation of the memorandum of understanding—it has lowered the level of aggression directed against Lebanon."

This is not a case of "Hezbollah being dependent on Iran." Rather, it is Hezbollah acknowledging a reality: Iran’s diplomatic leverage is reducing the military pressure exerted upon Lebanon.

He further called for "an end to American tutelage and control over key sectors of the state. Tutelage is akin to occupation; both constitute a violation of sovereignty."

🔻 The Mirror

In 1989, the Convention on the Rights of the Child was adopted. Thirty-seven years later, schoolchildren in Minab were killed by a bomb. The Convention did not stop the bomb.

The United States claims: "We are upholding freedom of navigation." Iran responds: "Your blockades have compelled us to develop the North-South Corridor and establish 'green channels' for customs."

The United States claims: "We are isolating Iran." Meanwhile, tribal sheikhs from Iraq sit in Mashhad, listening to a welcoming letter from the Supreme Leader.

Israel claims: "We are striking Hezbollah." Qassem asserts: "As long as occupation persists, there can be no discussion of disarmament." And the Iranian agreement has, in fact, lowered the level of aggression.

Four distinct threads, yet a single underlying structure: The West manages this conflict through international conventions, blockades, isolation, and military threats. Iran, conversely, builds alternatives on every front. Where conventions fail, it forges regional alliances. Where blockades create barriers, it constructs overland corridors. Where isolation is imposed, it reaffirms transnational bonds. And where military threats loom, it employs diplomatic leverage to alleviate the pressure.  And a nation capable of doing all four of these things simultaneously is not collapsing. It is organizing.

Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.
