text:
YONKERS GOLFER: Doug Ford (born Douglas Michael Fortunato, August 6, 1922 – May 14, 2018) was a Hall of Fame American professional golfer, two-time major champion, and one of the strongest players from the New York metropolitan area—often linked to Yonkers.

Born in West Haven, Connecticut, he grew up in the New York area (including the Bronx/upper Manhattan), where his father and uncles were golf professionals. 

His family name was shortened to Ford so his father could get club-pro jobs (Italian and Irish pros faced discrimination at many clubs). 

He developed an excellent short game and putting stroke on public courses, served in the Coast Guard during WWII, and turned pro in 1949 at age 27 after making good money gambling in matches. 

His father advised him to stick with golf over a baseball offer from the Yankees because “you’ll last forever.” 

He later lived in the Yonkers area (his father was pro at Putnam Country Club), received a hometown parade after his 1955 PGA win, and is in the Yonkers Sports Hall of Fame. 

Local sources frequently call him a Yonkers native or the standout golfer from the city/region.

Ford won 19 PGA Tour events between 1952 and 1963, plus other titles (including the 1956 Met Open). Key achievements:

* 1955 PGA Championship (match-play era): Won in his first appearance, defeating Cary Middlecoff 4 & 3 in the final. Named PGA Player of the Year that season.

* 1957 Masters: Trailed Sam Snead by three shots entering the final round. Shot a then-record final-round 66 to win by three at 283 (−5). He famously holed out from a plugged lie in the greenside bunker on the 72nd hole for birdie (“the greatest shot I ever hit”). Earlier on the 15th he went for the green in two with a 3-wood against his caddie’s advice and made birdie.

*Four-time Ryder Cup player (1955, 1957, 1959, 1961), contributing to three U.S. wins.

* Played in a then-record 49 Masters (final appearance 2001 at age 78).

* World Golf Hall of Fame inductee (2011, veterans category), plus Connecticut, Met PGA, National Italian American Sports, and Yonkers honors.

He was known as a fast, aggressive player (“goes for broke”) with a looping swing who wasn’t the longest hitter but was exceptional with the wedge and putter. 

In an era dominated by Snead, Hogan, and the emerging Palmer, he was a consistent top performer and money-winner. 

A 1989 PGA Tour ranking study placed him 18th among all-time greats.

After Ford’s 1957 Masters victory, Bobby Jones (Augusta National co-founder and legendary amateur) congratulated him. 

There is a well-known archival photo of Jones congratulating the new champion, and later images show the two together in green jackets. 

Jack Burke Jr. (1956 winner) helped Ford into the green jacket in the traditional ceremony.

Ford died in Palm Beach Gardens, Florida, at 95—the oldest living major champion at the time. 

He remained active in golf for decades, including on the Legends/Champions events, and is remembered as a durable, respected pro who helped shape the modern Tour.

He is widely viewed as the greatest golfer associated with Yonkers (or among the very top from the broader New York metro area of his generation), given his two majors, Tour success, and local area ties.

-
CMAT, the Irish singer-songwriter, showcases her powerful vocals, sharp songwriting, chemistry with her band, and signature comedic timing in a Tiny Desk Concert packed with charm from start to finish.

Throughout the set, CMAT offers a refreshing perspective on country music. On the pop hit “Take A Sexy Picture of Me,” she uses humor to respond to the cruel comments she has received about her appearance. text:
France and India share a bond forged with sacrifice and courage. This bond is now building a brilliant future. Thales, the $24 billion French aerospace and defence giant, has sourced more than $1.2 billion in goods and services from Indian suppliers over the past five years.

Over a century ago Indian soldiers crossed oceans to liberate French soil in two world wars, writing chapters of shared sacrifice that still echo.

At Neuve-Chapelle in northern France stands the Indian Memorial, a circular sanctuary with an Ashoka pillar and carved tigers honouring more than 4,700 soldiers and labourers of undivided India who fell on the Western Front and have no known grave.

Unveiled in 1927, it marks where the Indian Corps fought its first major action as a single unit in March 1915, a place of eternal remembrance for courage given far from home.

At Mazargues War Cemetery in Marseille, another sacred ground holds the names of nearly 1,000 Indian soldiers from both world wars, where troops first set foot in France before facing the trenches.

Those same ties of sacrifice and trust now power a modern technological partnership that knows no bounds.

Thales CEO Patrice Caine confirms that “Indianising” now means transferring design authority itself, so Indian engineers can enhance radars, missiles and electronic warfare systems for global markets.

India’s industrial base, engineering talent and competitive pricing make it a critical hub, not merely a market.

Thales already employs more than 2,300 people in India, with headquarters in Noida, engineering competence centres in Bengaluru and Noida, plus offices and an avionics MRO facility in Delhi, Gurugram and Mumbai.

Bharat Electronics Limited has already delivered thousands of transmit/receive modules for the Thales RBE2 AESA radar on India’s Rafales under technology transfer, with production expanding to SPECTRA electronic warfare systems.

The Rafale fighter anchors this alliance: the original 36-aircraft deal of 2016 was worth $8 billion, followed by 26 Rafale-Marine jets for $7 billion.

France has formally offered 114 additional Rafales valued near $33 billion, with the majority to be built in India, embedding deep technology transfer from Dassault, Safran and Thales.

Beyond fighters, cooperation spans Scorpene submarines, nuclear energy including advanced modular reactors, space launches and aeronautics centres of excellence.

Bilateral trade has exceeded $14 billion annually, while France ranks among India’s top European investors in defence and high technology.

For France, India offers scale, skilled talent and a strategic partner in a multipolar world; for India, it delivers cutting-edge capabilities and global market access.

Indian private rocket startups are already positioned to fill the 2029 satellite launch gap as Western capacity tightens.

This is true co-development and innovation where design blueprints shared, precision suppliers locked into global programmes, and sovereign capacity is built together.

From the mud of Flanders to the skies of the Indian Ocean and the frontiers of space, the old bonds of sacrifice have become an unbounded engine of innovation.

India and France are not just partners. They are co-architects of a shared future where technology serves peace, prosperity and strategic autonomy.

The monuments remember the past. The factories, laboratories and launch pads write the next chapter with a deep sense of responsibility. 

Together they prove that the strongest alliances are those that honour history while inventing a better tomorrow.

The ratlines (German: Rattenlinien) were systems of escape routes used by Nazis and their collaborators to flee Europe from 1945 onwards in the aftermath of World War II. Two primary routes developed independently with their operators eventually collaborating, the first transferring through Spain and the second through Rome and Genoa. Some escapees settled at these locations or used them to flee elsewhere, with the majority settling in Argentina or other South American countries such as Brazil, Chile, and Paraguay.

The ratlines were supported by some clergy of the Catholic Church, such as Austrian bishop Alois Hudal and Croatian priest Krunoslav Draganović, as well as some outlets of the International Committee of the Red Cross. The Nazis paid Argentine officials (starting c. 1943) to shield their agents, bolstering the rise of Juan Perón, whose regime set up additional ratlines through Scandinavia and Switzerland.

A number of significant Nazis and their collaborators escaped, including Ustaše leader Ante Pavelić, as well as Schutzstaffel (SS) officers Adolf Eichmann and Josef Mengele, both perpetrators of the Holocaust. Starting in 1945, the United States utilized the ratlines to aid the escape of some Soviet defectors and informants, as well as Gestapo leader Klaus Barbie (who had traded intel with the U.S. Army while being held in Austria). Planetary protection rules exist specifically to prevent Earth organisms from being introduced to Mars (and vice versa), mainly to protect scientific investigation of any potential native Martian life.

Core reasons
Scientific contamination risk: If Mars has (or had) indigenous life—most likely microbial, possibly in subsurface ice, brines, or protected niches—Earth microbes could colonize, outcompete, or alter those organisms and their chemistry. That would make it extremely difficult or impossible to distinguish true Martian biology from Earth contamination later. Future missions looking for biosignatures (organic molecules, isotopic patterns, cellular structures, etc.) rely on the surface and subsurface remaining as uncontaminated as possible.
COSPAR / NASA planetary protection protocols: International guidelines (Committee on Space Research) and NASA policies categorize Mars missions by risk. Landers and rovers destined for special regions (areas with potential liquid water or ice) require rigorous sterilization. Spacecraft are cleaned, baked, and assembled in cleanrooms to reduce the bioburden of viable Earth microbes to very low levels (often orders of magnitude below what would freely travel). Deliberate introduction of organisms is prohibited.
Uncertainty about Mars life: No definitive evidence of current life on Mars has been found, but the planet is not sterile by assumption. Past evidence of liquid water, organics detected by Curiosity and Perseverance, seasonal methane variations, and subsurface ice keep the possibility open. Introducing Earth life would permanently compromise the ability to resolve that question.
Practical survival factors: Mars is harsh (intense radiation, extreme cold, thin CO₂ atmosphere, perchlorates, low pressure). Many Earth organisms would die quickly. However, some extremophiles (certain bacteria, archaea, or spores) can survive desiccation, radiation, and cold for long periods and might remain viable or even metabolize in protected microenvironments. Once introduced at scale, control or removal is effectively impossible.

Scientific contamination risk: If Mars has (or had) indigenous life—most likely microbial, possibly in subsurface ice, brines, or protected niches—Earth microbes could colonize, outcompete, or alter those organisms and their chemistry. The unusual exchange happened on October 26, 2026, during jury selection in Hillsborough County. Kessler, who is representing himself, is charged with first-degree murder and abuse of a dead body in connection with the 2021 death of 47-year-old Stephanie Crone-Overholt.

When Judge Nick Nazaretian explained that Kessler could enter an open plea and face life in prison, the defendant responded with his own unusual proposal. He specifically requested a cheesesteak with onions and mayonnaise, fries, and a Pepsi, claiming the deal would save taxpayers money by avoiding a trial.

But the judge immediately rejected the idea, explaining that offering food in exchange for a guilty plea would be inappropriate. He said he could guarantee Kessler would receive lunch, but not the specific meal he wanted.

Kessler later withdrew his offer and asked the court to proceed with jury selection, admitting he did not expect to get his cheesesteak.

Meanwhile, the serious criminal case continues. Investigators allege that Crone-Overholt’s dismembered remains were discovered by fishermen in McKay Bay in November 2021. Kessler denies no charges in this courtroom exchange, and the allegations must be determined through the legal process.

October 28–29, 2026. Yemen. Operations are advancing simultaneously on two fronts.

💥 Front One: Aden Airport

“More than four missiles were fired at Aden International Airport, triggering explosions. The Yemeni Armed Forces stated that they were targeting a large shipment of weapons transported by a Saudi cargo plane.”

Parts of southern Taiz and the area around Taiz University have now fallen under the control or within the firing range of Yemeni forces.”

“Ansarallah forces continue to employ short-range tactical missiles against Saudi-led coalition bases and troop concentrations in Aden, Lahj, and other areas.”

A market in the Al-Hazm district of Al-Jawf province was bombed, leaving 14 dead and 10 injured, including women and children.

Artillery shelling struck residential villages in the Razih district of Saada province.

A market. Mountains. A chemical factory. An island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Villages.

These were the targets Saudi Arabia chose to strike on the very same day its mercenaries fled from the Daiman hills, Al-Iqam, and Al-Maydan.

"The Iranian Army and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps have directly attacked U.S. military bases. Apart from Japan’s brief assault on the United States during World War II, no other major power has carried out such an attack against the U.S."

This is not mere "rhetoric." It is a "record."

Since the war began on February 28, 2026, Iranian missiles have struck U.S. bases in Qatar, Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Jordan. An E-3 airborne early warning aircraft was destroyed. Three U.S. service members were killed in their barracks in Jordan. The Pentagon is concealing the extent of the losses at these bases; five senators have demanded that the full account be made public.

And the Iranian Ambassador to Russia states: We have directly attacked U.S. bases something no other major power has done, with the sole exception of Japan’s brief attack on the U.S. during World War II.

The purpose of this statement is not "boasting." It is "positioning" placing Iran’s military actions within a historical frame of reference.  In 1941, Japan attacked Pearl Harbor. In 2026, Iran attacked U.S. bases in the Middle East and the United States was powerless to stop it.

📜 Cyberattacks

“Cyberattacks targeting the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting (IRIB) were detected this morning. Sources suggest these attacks may be a test run for a larger-scale operation, aimed at maximizing the impact on the IRIB.”

What is the IRIB? It is Iran’s state broadcasting organization. Its function goes beyond mere “entertainment”; it serves to maintain information sovereignty during wartime. It broadcasts news, analysis, and official state positions, acting as a critical node in countering Western media narratives.

The goal of these cyberattacks is not merely to “disable a website,” but to “silence a nation’s voice.” Iranian sources indicate that this could be a “test for a larger-scale operation” meaning the adversary is probing the vulnerabilities of Iran’s information infrastructure in preparation for a more significant strike.

Iraqi Prime Minister al-Zaidi and Syrian President al-Shara held expanded talks at the People’s Palace in Damascus. The discussions focused on strengthening cooperation between Iraq and Syria, including the potential export of Iraqi oil via the Baniyas pipeline, a conduit reportedly capable of transporting up to 2 million barrels per day.

The Baniyas pipeline runs from Iraq’s oil fields, through Syria, to the port of Baniyas on the Mediterranean coast. Its purpose is to allow Iraqi oil to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The Strait of Hormuz is currently blockaded by the U.S. Navy, and Red Sea shipping routes have been disrupted by the war. Iraq’s oil exports are currently dependent on the port of Basra which lies within the Persian Gulf, on the inner side of the Strait of Hormuz.

The Baniyas pipeline offers an export route that avoids the Strait of Hormuz entirely. By passing through Syria to the Mediterranean, it circumvents the blockade chain imposed by the United States.

Al-Zaidi’s discussions with al-Shara in Damascus are not merely a matter of “bilateral cooperation”; they represent the creation of an alternative route to bypass the U.S. blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia says: We are striking military targets.

Yemen says: You are bombing markets, chemical plants, and islands in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

Yemen says: Your mercenaries have fled from the Daiman hills, Al-Iqam, and Al-Maydan. Parts of Taiz University are now within our range of fire.

Two fronts. The same outcome: Saudi Arabia is bombing markets, while Yemen is liberating airports. The United States is concealing its losses, while Iran is documenting its strikes. The Strait of Hormuz is blockaded, and the Baniyas pipeline is under discussion.

Long live Yemen. Long live Iran. Long live the Resistance. Long live the Axis of Resistance.

Shri Ram and the Birth of Marukantara 🏹

Rama reached the southern ocean with the Vanara army to cross into Lanka and rescue Sita. He prayed to Varuna, the ocean god, for three days. Varuna never appeared.

Angered by the ocean's arrogance, Rama fixed the Brahmastra to his bow, ready to dry up the sea itself. Varuna emerged at once, bowed, and offered a way: the Vanaras could build the floating bridge, Ram Setu.

But a Brahmastra once aimed cannot be recalled. It had to be fired. Where? Varuna pointed to Dhrumkulya in the north, a land terrorised by the Abhira dacoits who poisoned its waters.

Rama released the arrow. Its fire dried every water body there. The scorched, barren land it left behind was named Marukantara, "the region of death."

A desert born from an arrow that could not be taken back. 🌵

text:
Goedemorgen. Geschiedenis.
'The Raid on Déva
476 years ago, in October 1550, an angry young man, barely twenty-one years old, by the name of János Török, son of Bálint Török of Enying, took revenge on the Turks for his father's death. The raid on Déva was so spectacularly successful that the Pasha of Buda decided it would be wiser to abandon his campaign in Transylvania and turn back…
In 1550, Bálint Török, a Hungarian nobleman and Ban of Nándorfehérvár (Belgrade), died in Ottoman captivity. He had been captured by the Turks back in 1541, through trickery—the same way they had seized Buda Castle. The Janissaries of the Ottoman "relief army" simply walked through the open castle gates, and once enough of them were inside, out came the swords!
Buda was lost.
As for Bálint Török, he believed that he and several others had been invited to visit Sultan Suleiman as guests. The others were eventually allowed to leave, but Suleiman had taken such a "liking" to Lord Bálint that he insisted on keeping him close.
Until the day he died.
Despite every effort made by his family, the Sultan refused to part with his "beloved" prisoner. Perhaps he saw in him a dangerous adversary…
Understandably, Bálint's son, János Török—yes, we may also know him from Eclipse of the Crescent Moon—was hardly an admirer of the Turks after all this.
As Sebestyén Tinódi Lantos wrote in his historical ballad The Valor of János Török of Enying:

Let us now recall the deeds of János Török,
In the year fifteen hundred and fifty, as it is written,
When he was but twenty-one years of age,
János stood at the court of the Queen.
He declared before Her Majesty
That he would remain her faithful servant,
Yet never would he fight alongside the Turks;
Rather, for his father's sake, he would oppose them until death.
The trouble was that by 1550, Queen Isabella and Friar George (György Fráter), who had jointly—enthusiastically or perhaps somewhat less enthusiastically—struck a bargain with the Sultan back in 1541, had fallen out with each other.
The Queen still regarded the Turks as the guarantors of her power, ensuring that her son, the ten-year-old John Sigismund, the first Prince of Transylvania, could retain his position.
Friar George, meanwhile—as he had done so many times throughout his life—had switched sides and now saw King Ferdinand as the key to Transylvania's future.
And in those days, disagreements of this sort provided more than enough justification for a good old-fashioned civil war.
Naturally, Isabella played her Turkish card and appealed for help to Kasim (or Kason, according to other sources), the Pasha of Buda. The plan was for the Ottoman forces to join up near Gyulafehérvár (Alba Iulia) with the troops of the Wallachian and Moldavian voivodes, along with the forces loyal to the Queen.
And so, in October 1550, the Turks duly arrived. After all, they had been invited.
Of course, they could hardly be expected to travel through Transylvania without indulging in a little customary plundering along the way. For them, that was part of what war was all about…
One after another, they occupied the towns and castles along their route. At least, those that needed occupying.
Déva (Deva), for instance, was then held by supporters of the Szapolyai faction, who were allied with the Ottomans and gladly welcomed the Turkish advance troops.
As Ferenc Forgách recounts in his History of Martinuzzi and Isabella:

"Meanwhile, Kason sent 200 horsemen ahead under Feru Agha, who took up quarters in the suburb below Déva Castle, and then dispatched another 500.
When János Török learned of this—a young man thirsting for glory and revenge, who had never forgotten that his father, Bálint, had been taken prisoner in Buda and had languished to death in captivity in Constantinople; who possessed the mighty fortress of Hunyad and had many loyal followers near Déva—he resolved to offer, as it were, a funeral sacrifice to his father's memory through the bloody slaughter of the enemy.
Believing that this was no time for hesitation, he first sounded out the loyalty of the town magistrate and the townspeople. Then, with no more than 113 horsemen and 67 infantrymen, he set out under cover of darkness.
At the break of dawn, he ordered his infantry to force their way through the wattle fences, while he himself, leading the cavalry, had the bolts of the gates smashed—for the settlement had no walls or fortifications.
Bursting into the town, he put to flight those who were still half asleep or scrambling for their weapons. His men cut down the enemy inside the houses and struck down those they encountered in the streets.
The slaughter was all the more remarkable because Török's men had also occupied the roads and paths, leaving no possibility of escape. Those who scattered found armed men waiting for them, ready to cut them down.
János himself, fighting on horseback, engaged in a dangerous duel with one of Feru Agha's foot soldiers (...). After a prolonged struggle, and at great risk to his own life, he finally prevailed, stabbing his opponent through both sides with his dagger.
Feru Agha fell, together with almost all his men.
The victory and the revenge were far greater than the spoils, for in cutting down so many enemies (...) János evidently sought only to avenge his father's death.
When a few survivors eventually straggled back into the camp, they spoke of the enemy's strength and numbers (...), embellishing the truth with exaggerations.
Fearing that he might be surrounded, especially since his baggage train had become bogged down along the very road by which he had advanced, Kason was forced to return to Buda without accomplishing his mission."
— Ferenc Forgách, History of Martinuzzi and Isabella
In other words, a furious twenty-one-year-old young man, determined to avenge his father's death, managed in a single stroke to send an entire Ottoman intervention force fleeing.
Well, ladies and gentlemen, that's how things were done back in those days…

As Tinódi wrote:

Great terror seized the heathen host,
The fleeing Turks brought word to the five hundred,
Who hastened back to Kason, every one of them,
And great was the Pasha's grief upon hearing the news.
With his army he set out toward Buda,
Lest he suffer even greater shame.
Thus, for the death of Bálint Török,
Did the Turks fare at the hands of his valiant son, János Török.'

The Disinfo op - Khilji knew that the Yadava army was very strong and if even a fraction of it got into Deogiri, he was done for, so he left his main force behind and marched with 8,000 of his light cav. 

At this point he spread through his spy network the story that he was not seeking to wage war but he survived a civil war with his uncle, the Sultan and was marching south to be a mercenary to any Hindu king that would have him. 

The Senua (Yadava) King was away in the south waging war on the Hosyala (a 120 year long struggle from 1187 AD to the end of both empires), and while he was prepared to hasten back to his capital, the news that Khilji sought peace soothed him and he continued his campaign in the south. The main field army of the Senuas under the crown prince was in the south. 

Khilji in the meantime made an alliance with the Hosyala to attack Deogiri while the Hosyala pressed from the south. 

Once he entered Yadava territory, Khilji moved at a blistering pace, bypassing all other cities and forts till he reached the outskirts of Deogiri. 

The King who had stayed back in the capital, now realised how desperate his situation was, collapsed what little men he had into the citadel and locked it up tight while sending desperate summons to his son to return with his field army. 

He also spread rumours again that this 8,000 man force was the vanguard, the main army of 40,000 men was being personally lead by the Sultan and would be in Deogiri very soon. 

The citadel was unassailable even with 100,000 men but the problem was...food. 

And here Goddess Fortuna again cursed the Yadavas, before the siege the garrison hauled what they thought was a 10000 sacks of grain. Except it was salt. Yes, due to some error by some logistical clerk, the garisson had 100's of tonnes of salt but no food. 

Within weeks the King sued for peace and offered to pay an obscene sum in cash, gold and gems to Khilji. 

While this was on, the main force unde the crown prince returned, saw what was happening and lined up for battle. 

Massively outnumbered, Khilji drew up 7,000 horse to face the Yadava army while he left 1,000 at the foot of the citadel to act as a screen. 

While the 7,000 cavalry and the Yadava army fought, the 1000 men under Gen Nusrat Khan just waited, but riders from the main group reached Nusrat Khan and begged him to help as the battle was lost... abandoning his post the 1000 horse rushed to aid their general. 

The Yadava army saw all the dust being raised and assumed that this was the main army under the Sultan and simply lost all morale and fled. 

The King now having no hope, abandoned the defense, the ransom was paid in full to Khilji. Who took the money back to Delhi, used it to first bribe the mleccha nobility, had his uncle assassinated and came back as Sultan to finish the job. 

This time the Yadavas were a shell of their former selves but with Khilji offered an alliance to end the Hosyala, they took it!

With the Hosyala threat ended, Khilji turned on the Yadavas and ended them! 

And thus ended the empires of the Hosyala and Yadavas!

Google reports new AI capabilities and computing demand, Meta expands research and agent access, and Anthropic proposes court oversight.

TRANSCRIPT
Finding and repairing software flaws is a major focus of Google’s new Gemini 4 Carbon AI model. Google reports scores of eighty-eight point two percent for vulnerability discovery, fifty-four point eight percent for exploitation and seventy-one percent for patching on three security benchmarks. Those are company-reported evaluations. Access begins with selected cyber defenders, then trusted partners as Google gathers feedback and adjusts safeguards. Wider developer, business and consumer access is planned, rather than generally available.

AI research into infant monitoring, medical reporting and dementia communication is getting support at five American universities. Meta says it is supplying model access, researcher collaboration and two million dollars in grants. Projects include chest X-ray reporting and Alzheimer’s diagnosis research at Ohio State, infant monitoring at Louisiana State, and dementia communication at Indiana University. These are research efforts, not established clinical benefits. Meta says universities run the models in their own environments and retain patient-data control; the data is not made available to Meta.

Meta’s Muse AI agent offers Singapore users a way to delegate tasks across everyday services. Meta says its local partners span shopping, grocery delivery and travel, including Shopee, Grab and Singapore Airlines. The company says Muse asks before sensitive actions such as sending email or buying something, and keeps connected-service credentials outside the agent’s view. Singapore availability has been announced, but connector features are rolling out progressively. That does not establish that every connection is already operational.

Interactive AI-generated worlds could provide training environments for robots and software agents, according to Google. The company says Genie 4 generates real-time environments with native sound that users can change through natural-language prompts. Gemini 3.8 Flash guides generation and checks multi-step events. Genie 4 remains an early research preview for trusted testers. Google lists visual drift, complex interactions and spatial accuracy among its limitations. Training uses are potential applications, rather than demonstrated broad results.

Anthropic wants courts to have a role in stopping release of AI models assessed as a serious public risk. Reuters reports that the company’s October fifteenth letter to California Governor Gavin Newsom proposed letting officials seek judicial orders to block release after a risk review. Anthropic also argued that disabling a problematic agent or cutting a customer’s access could work better than a model-wide kill switch. Anthropic confirmed the letter’s authenticity to Reuters. This is a company recommendation, echoing earlier proposals, rather than an enacted California rule.

Google says demand for AI infrastructure is very strong while computing capacity remains constrained. The company says it is bringing more capacity online and sees strong demand across customers for its tensor processing units, its AI accelerator systems. Google also reports that Gemini 4 Argon developer-platform usage ramped three and a half times faster in its first week than Gemini 3, despite capacity constraints. These are Google’s reported adoption and demand measures; they do not quantify how many customers remain unserved.

text:
OpenAI is planning to buy Google's AI chips, according to reports from The Information and Bloomberg. The amount and the deal terms haven't been confirmed.

The chips are called TPUs, short for tensor processing units. Google started building them more than ten years ago to make search faster, and they turned out to be good at the kind of math AI models run on. For years, if you wanted that kind of computing, the default answer was an Nvidia GPU. OpenAI is one of Nvidia's most important customers.

One small detail makes it feel real. OpenAI has posted job listings for engineers to optimize its models for TPUs, with training or inference experience both welcome. The Information read that as a sign the work is still early. Signing for hardware is the easy part. Getting a giant model to run well on a different chip takes people, time, and a lot of patience.

OpenAI also isn't the first to shop at Google. The same week, Anthropic disclosed a five-year, $161 billion agreement to lease Google TPU-based equipment through Broadcom, and Oracle said it will offer TPUs on its cloud starting next year, the first time Google has supplied them to a major cloud outside its own.

Nvidia is hardly being dropped, though. In August it agreed to provide up to $105 billion in credit support for an Ohio data center OpenAI plans to lease, and Jensen Huang has said OpenAI committed to deploying a lot of Nvidia infrastructure through 2030. OpenAI is also getting its own chip ready, Jalapeño, co-developed with Broadcom and led by Richard Ho, who used to work on TPUs at Google.

So the best-known AI company is buying from Nvidia, buying from Google, and building its own. In most businesses that's just called not wanting to depend on one supplier. In AI the purchase orders have more digits.

Will anyone typing into ChatGPT ever notice which chip answered them? Probably not, and that's sort of the point of having more than one.

I’m 31, and until recently, I was earning about $57,000 a year as an operations supervisor at a hotel in Pennsylvania. The work was demanding, the pay was average, and every time a management position opened up, someone with more experience seemed to get it.

So when I applied for a resort operations director position and made it through three rounds of interviews, I was already surprised.

Then the offer came.

$98,000 a year, free accommodation on the property, and a title that would finally put me on the management track I had been chasing.

I nearly accepted on the spot.

During the final interview, however, the owner explained something the job listing had barely mentioned.

The resort operated beside a large lake in a remote part of northern Michigan. It welcomed guests from spring through autumn, but closed completely for four months during winter.

During that period, I would be expected to remain on the property to monitor the buildings, oversee maintenance, inspect storm damage, and coordinate contractors whenever problems arose.

There would be no regular staff living there with me.

I asked whether I could leave on weekends.

The owner hesitated before answering.

“You can, technically. But if a major storm hits or a pipe bursts, you're the person responsible for responding.”

He explained that the previous manager had resigned halfway through the winter season. Apparently, the isolation had affected him more than he expected.

I drove home thinking about the money, the title, and the possibility of finally getting ahead financially.

Then I told my family.

My mother immediately called it a terrible idea. My older brother laughed and said I was about to become a caretaker with an executive salary.

I thought they were being dramatic.

After all, I would still have electricity, internet, a furnished apartment, and a job that could transform my career.

At least, that was what I believed before I visited the property.

text:
That supports the broad observation that political views are much more complex than a left–right binary. It does not establish the video’s proposed relationship between ideological intensity and freedom. Pew Research Center +1

3. The video confuses opposition to a behavior with opposition to freedom itself

This is especially important in its AI, fandom, and vaccination examples.

The video repeatedly treats one side as saying let me do something and the other as saying stop doing that.

But many political disputes involve an additional question: Does one person’s exercise of freedom infringe upon another person’s rights or interests?

An artist defending copyright protections may believe they’re defending their creative freedom. Someone supporting vaccination requirements may believe they’re protecting vulnerable people’s health and ability to participate safely in public life.

That doesn’t mean either position is automatically justified. It means that the video cannot determine who is defending freedom merely by identifying which party wants a restriction.

What I think the creator gets genuinely right

The claim about political power is probably the most insightful part.

Political actors can be committed to civil liberties in opposition and become more comfortable with coercive policies when governing. Political loyalty can also influence how people perceive threats to freedom.

The video is therefore pointing toward an important distinction between principled liberty and selective liberty: whether someone defends a right even when its exercise benefits people they dislike.

That is a much stronger way to test the video’s intuition than plotting ideology inside a triangle.

Final judgment

As political philosophy, the video offers a worthwhile argument about the dangers of coercive ideological certainty.

As a mathematical representation of politics, it is underdeveloped. As empirical political science, it is largely unsupported.

The strongest version of its thesis would be:

The most meaningful political distinction is not always between left and right, but between people who defend liberties consistently and those who defend them selectively.

That proposition is worth investigating. It avoids the video’s central mistake of assuming ideological moderation is equivalent to freedom.

And it offers a demanding standard: someone who truly values liberty must be prepared to defend it even when doing so protects choices, expressions, or people they fundamentally oppose.

text:
On doubts and fears

Question: “How does the person of Nembutsu, who has received shinjin, deal with the ‘demon’ of doubt that resurfaces after the believer has received and experienced the blessings of true entrusting from Amida Buddha?

As foolish beings, our Saha world minds are prone to delusion and ‘doubt’. That is part of our hopeless condition as bonbu. Perhaps those who have doubt after receiving shinjin are loved all the more by Amida Nyorai, because Amida recognizes the great need to embrace these hopeless, helpless beings in their delusional state of doubt. A Chinese Pure Land Master once said, “You may not ever doubt Buddha Amitabha (Amida), but you will doubt yourself.” (I realize that those who have shinjin have Amida’s own faith through His merit transference to us, and that Amida Buddha cannot doubt himself).

At some level, most Westerners, who are converts from some form of Christianity, know they are ‘risking their very eternal lives’ (souls?) to receive, and possibly transmit, the Dharma of our school of Buddhism.

Could it be that ‘all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas praise the person of Nembutsu,’ because of that person’s stubborn reliance on the Great Vow and belief in the sutras preached by Shakyamuni at a ‘fundamental’ level? Are people of shinjin heroes to all the beings of all the worlds?

Are these children of Amida Buddha recipients of the ‘Present Benefits’ because they recognize their stupidity and know, beyond any doubt, that the one thing they cannot do is save themselves from birth and death?”

Answer: A person who has received shinjin (faith) cannot doubt Amida’s salvation. To have shinjin means, in the words of Shinran, to hear the Primal Vow of Amida without any doubt. So, doubt and shinjin cannot coexist with one another.

Of course, in terms of his personal daily life, the follower can have doubts related to many things, like his family, his friends, even his own self, but he never doubts his own birth in the Pure Land and subsequent attainment of Buddhahood.

Generally speaking, the follower who has faith in Amida should not expect to feel special things, acquire qualities that he hasn’t had until then, or to overcome his ordinary problems and fears. I do not deny that various changes may occur in a person of faith, but he should not think that shinjin is a means to change his personality or purify himself of illusions and blind passions. Simply stated, he can remain an ordinary person filled with delusions and attachments even after receiving shinjin. However, there is one big difference – he knows that from now on (from the moment of his first thought of entrusting) a great burden has indeed been taken off his shoulders, which is the burden of becoming a Buddha. He certainly knows, without any doubt, that he has become assured of birth and Buddhahood in Amida’s Pure Land at the end of this life.
He knows all this, but at the same time, fears of various kinds, delusions and difficulties might continue to coexist with this faith, just like in any ordinary person. Shinjin or faith is an “outside element” in the heart of the believer because it is not his creation but rather what Amida has planted inside him.
Shinjin is also like the big and warm arms of the mother who carries the frightened child across the turbulent waters of a flooded river. The child continues to cry, being afraid of various things he sees and hears around him, but he is safely kept in his mother’s embrace.
Fears of many types are present but there is also entrusting in the mother. For example, he might be scared when he sees a big wave coming toward him or hears a thunderbolt in the sky or the rain pouring over his face, but he knows he is safely carried away by his mother to the other shore.

Fear is an instinctual habit which cannot completely disappear from our hearts and minds until we have become Enlightened. For example, even when we are in a big and solid house we might fear for a moment when we hear powerful thunder. In the same way, we continue to fear death even if we know that when we die, we go to the Pure Land and become Buddhas. Fear of death is the manifestation of our powerful attachment and identification with our bodies. It is the same with fear from being injured, but I would not call these fears the same as doubting Amida’s salvation.

If we were asked to have no fear in our daily lives in order to be saved by Amida, then who would be saved? Who can say that he is completely free of fear? We even fear a tooth extraction because we don’t like to feel pain, even though we know we are safe! So, Amida Buddha does not require us to be without fear (without attachment to our bodies) as there is no mention in His Primal Vow of anything like this. If we read the Primal Vow, we see that He only asks us to entrust in Him (saying of the Name and aspiring to be born being the same as entrusting).

In the ultimate sense, faith in Amida is not the product of our unenlightened minds. It is said that in a forest filled with poisonous trees, there cannot appear any tree with good fruits. So, in the hearts filled with illusions and attachments, faith in Amida cannot appear unless Amida causes it to appear. It is the same as the love of the mother who makes the child entrust to her. Without the love of the mother, the child can do nothing. The calling of the mother echoes in the child’s heart and makes him respond with faith, just as it is with Namo Amida Bu which is the expression of faith. It is the mother’s love that works inside the child and makes him entrust to her. This is how I explain in limited verbal terms the impossible to understand concept that shinjin comes from Amida and is not our creation.

Because shinjin (faith) comes from Amida, it is called the diamond-like shinjin, which means it cannot be destroyed by anybody, be it a demon or a person from a different religion. Even if we hear other people telling us that because we left a monotheistic religion we’ll go to hell, it is like hearing thunderbolts and heavy rain from inside a big, strong and safe house. The thunderbolts and heavy rain might sound frightful for a moment, because we are used to hearing many threats all our life since childhood, but we remember that we are safe in the house, which is a metaphor for Amida’s embrace.
It is the same when watching a horror movie. We can become scared, but in the end we know we are safe and that it is only a movie. After all, the reality is that we are safe with Amida Buddha and carried to His Pure Land where we’ll too become Buddhas.

I repeat, in matters related to the salvation offered by Amida Buddha there can be no doubts for one who has shinjin. No matter what happens or how he feels, sometimes good and sometimes bad or scared by various things, he knows deep inside him, due to his faith, that he is saved by Amida and destined to become a Buddha in the Pure Land.

There is nothing that we, ordinary people, can do with our fears, attachments and problems, so there is no need to worry that they may remain with us for the rest of our lives. The most important thing is that we rely on Amida and that we have a simple faith in Him, being sure that this is our last life as non-Buddhas.

Please do not forget that fear, suffering and attachments are different and separated from shinjin. The former are the products of your own illusions and attachments, while the latter originates from Amida and is the assurance that He saves you and accepts you as you are.

People of Nembutsu are praised by all Buddhas and Enlightened Bodhisattvas not because they made something special through their own power, but because they follow the most important teaching of all Buddhas by entrusting themselves to Amida. All Buddhas know that the Amida Dharma is the supreme Dharma because it can save everybody, no matter how great or small their spiritual capacities are. The goal of all Buddhas’ appearance in the world is to save all beings, and what method is indeed capable of saving everybody and corresponds to this goal, if not the Nembutsu of faith in Amida? So, to be open to this Dharma, to accept it, to venerate it and to say the Nembutsu of faith is what all Buddhas praise even if the follower does not have anything special inside him.

It is due to Amida that persons of shinjin are praised by all Buddhas. We are not heroes, because without Amida we can do nothing but end up in hell or other lower realms. We can rather say that we are the children with the most important father or mother in the universe. If you have Amida as your Parent you can be certain that all Buddhas will praise you, even though you are nothing special by yourself.

Also it is one thing to know yourself by using the light of your own wisdom and another to realize your limitations while being illuminated by the infinite Light of Amida which enters your being through faith (shinjin). It is the difference between sitting in a dark room with a small candle and illuminating it with lots of modern electrical devices. Shinjin, or connecting to Amida’s Light, is what causes you to receive the ten benefits in this life and the praise of all Buddhas.

All one needs to do is listen deeply again and again to the teaching about the Primal Vow. Even if he doubts many times, he should continue to listen, ask questions, meditate on himself and on what he has heard, and one day he might become open to Amida and entrust to Him. Then he will be sure of his birth in the Pure Land no matter if his mind remains as ordinary as before.

I THINK THE WISE UNDERSTAND WHAT IS LEFT UNSAID.

On X, I believe anyone who is not SEBI-registered operates within certain limitations. 

There are things one may wish to communicate, yet regulatory boundaries demand restraint.

And sometimes, sir, a subtle indication is more than enough for those who know how to read between the lines.

Which stock deserves attention, why it deserves attention, where a potential opportunity may emerge,

How many points a move could offer, and what levels matter in NIFTY and BANK NIFTY - those who follow the analysis carefully often understand the underlying message without needing everything to be spelt out.

Beyond that, I have little more to say.

If a stock falls, there will be discussions. 

If it rises, there will be discussions. 

If the market trends, there will be discussions. 

If it refuses to move, there will still be discussions. 

Even a sideways market has a story to tell.

This is the stock market, sir.

Uncertainty is part of its nature; Interpretation is part of the process.

For me, the stock market is not merely a place to make money. 

It is a business that deserves discipline, patience, humility and respect.

A business is like a temple - you enter it with the right intentions, follow its principles and accept that the outcome is never entirely in your control.

So, approach the market with reverence, but never without reason. 

Analyse before acting. 
Respect risk before pursuing returns. 

And never mistake conviction for certainty.

The market does not reward our emotions;
 It tests our discipline.

Aurangzeb and India. History vs Bollywood Myth 

1. Banning the Burning of Widows (Sati)

Aurangzeb ordered that Sati be banned across Mughal territory. The Italian traveler Niccolao Manucci (1638–1717) recorded:

"The king issued an order that in all lands under Mogul control never again should the officials allow a woman to be burnt."
— Storia Do Mogor, Niccolao Manucci, p. 97

2. Temples: Politics, Not Just Piety

Historian Audrey Truschke notes that while Aurangzeb protected most of the temples and increased Hindu representation in the Mughal nobility. 
— Source: Daily Times, Feb 25, 2018 (LLF session)

It's worth remembering that temple destruction by various rulers across eras — including non-Muslim kings — was about power and control, not faith alone.

3. A Contemporary Account on Women's Treatment

French traveler Jean de Thévenot (1633–1667) wrote in detail about Sati and observed:

"To conclude, the Women are happy that the Mahometans are become the Masters in the Indies, to deliver them from the tyranny of the Bramens."
— Indian Travels of Thevenot, edited by Surendranath Sen, p. 120

4. The Execution of Sambhaji

Aurangzeb executed grapist sambhaji who graped even a bramen woman and mass graped Portuguese women in goa, Aurengzeb offered to spare Sambhaji's life if he surrendered his forts, disclosed his treasuries, and revealed which Mughal officers were secretly aiding the Marathas. He also offered him the chance to convert. Sambhaji refused and insulted both Aurangzeb and the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH). Scholars sentenced him to death; he was tortured and beheaded on 11 March 1689 at Koregaon.
— Pāṭīla, Śālinī (1987). Maharani Tarabai of Kolhapur, c. 1675–1761 A.D. S. Chand & Company, pp. 46–48; Johnston, Harry (1986). The Great Pioneer in India, Ceylon, Bhutan & Tibet. Mittal Publications, p. 252.

Conclusion: Nuance Over Narrative

During Aurangzeb's reign (1658–1707), Mughal India remained one of the world's major economic powers thriving textile industries, flourishing international trade, productive agriculture, and immense imperial revenues. Bengal's fine muslin and Surat's bustling port reflected India's global commercial importance, while the Badshahi Mosque in Lahore showcased Mughal architectural grandeur. History deserves nuance: Aurangzeb inherited much of this prosperity from earlier Mughal rulers, and his long military campaigns later strained imperial finances. Judge history by evidence, not just narratives acknowledge both the achievements and the controversies.

📜 THIS DAY IN DIPLOMATIC HISTORY
        October 29, 1907

Russia made two moves in the north of Europe on this date, two years apart, and they pointed in opposite directions. On October 29, 1905, it became the first power to recognise the new independence of Norway, a step that leaned toward Britain. On October 29, 1907, its foreign minister signed a secret protocol with Germany meant to keep Britain out of the Baltic. 

The quarrel went back half a century. By a convention of 1856, forced on a defeated Russia and attached to the Treaty of Paris, Russia had bound itself not to fortify the Åland Islands, the archipelago that commands the approaches to the Gulfs of Bothnia and Finland. Britain wanted that convention kept, because an unfortified Åland left the door open for the Western powers to involve themselves in Baltic affairs. Russia had long wanted it gone. When Izvolsky raised the question of scrapping it, Britain's foreign secretary, Edward Grey, answered coolly and proposed to discuss the matter among four powers, Sweden included, for Stockholm feared Russian naval bases on Åland so close to its own capital.

So Izvolsky changed tack. On the eve of concluding the Anglo-Russian Convention, he turned to a nervous Germany and offered it a secret protocol. Russia, he said, did not want Britain meddling in the Baltic, and to prevent it Russia would for now set aside its demand to abolish the 1856 convention and would settle the Åland question directly with Sweden. His draft proclaimed a common Russian and German policy in the Baltic: to preserve the existing territorial order, to keep out "all foreign influence," and to recognise only the four coastal states, Russia, Germany, Denmark and Sweden, as having any interest in the sea. By "foreign influence" he meant Britain.

The Germans suspected he wanted to lure Germany into signing something hostile to Britain so that he could then show it to the British and poison Anglo-German relations still further. So Berlin crossed out every anti-British line and kept the rest. Russia, caught out, accepted the German version without a word of protest. The protocol, signed on October 29, 1907, also carried a German assurance that a future lifting of the Åland restriction in Russia's favour would not clash with it. It was the most solid fruit of the brief Russo-German courtship that followed the Russo-Japanese War.

The northern game had a second theatre. In 1905 Norway broke away from its union with Sweden. Russia, far from resenting Norwegian independence, welcomed it. A free and neutral Norway suited Russia's interests in the Arctic and the safety of its remote northwestern frontier. And so Russia became the first power to recognise Norway as a fully independent state, on October 29, 1905.

Russia then pressed to replace the old anti-Russian treaty with a guarantee by the great powers, and Norway itself wanted one. But Britain would guarantee only Norway's territorial integrity, not its neutrality, because it meant to keep the option of using Norwegian ports against Germany in a future war. Russia accepted the British formula with some reluctance. On November 2, 1907, Russia, Britain, Germany, France and Norway signed a treaty guaranteeing Norway's independence and the integrity of its territory, with Norway bound to cede no part of its land to anyone. It was one more step drawing Russia and Britain together.

Two moves in the same north, in the same autumn, pointed in opposite directions. A secret pact with Germany against Britain in the Baltic, and a public guarantee alongside Britain over Norway. This was the real texture of diplomacy before the First World War.

#DiplomaticHistory #Russia #Germany #Baltic #Norway #Izvolsky #OnThisDay

text:
The gear in Metro Exodus has more choices than it first appears to have too. You don't just collect every upgrade and have all of them working at once.

You choose one upgrade in each of four categories at a workbench:

• Helmet/gas mask: Extended Filter, Reinforced Helmet, or Armored Glass.
• Electrical equipment: Battery Charge Controller, Extra Bright Flashlight, or NVD Amplifier.
• Vest: Ammo Pouches, Throwing Weapons Harness, or Consumables Carrier.
• Bracer: Compass, Metal Detector, or Motion Scanner.

Those are 12 selectable upgrades. The night-vision goggles themselves make up the 13 pickups normally counted in the full gear checklist. The goggles and the NVD Amplifier are not the same item.

Location spoilers below. These are base-game locations, not Sam's Story, and this is one route to each item rather than a list of every duplicate pickup.

In the Volga, look for these eight:

1. Compass
Search the cockpit of the crashed plane north of the Aurora. Once equipped on the bracer, it points toward the current main objective. It does not simply point north.

2. Extended Filter
In the central map area, find the enclosed container/safehouse full of fungus and webs, west of the bandit building holding captive villagers. The upgrade is inside. This makes filters last longer; it does not make the mask's glass harder to break.

3. Ammo Pouches
Search the main building of the central bandit camp where those villagers are being held. Look on a crate near the entrance. These increase how much ammunition you can carry.

Free the prisoners while you're there and collect the key one offers. That gives you an earlier way into the night-vision room in the Terminal.

4. Throwing Weapons Harness
Go to the bandit-held gas station on the eastern side of the large central landmass. Break the lock on the interior gate and check the shelving beyond it. This increases your capacity for throwing knives, grenades and Molotovs.

5. Reinforced Helmet
Search the bandit-held concrete ruins on the southeastern island, northwest of the teddy-bear location and connected to the Terminal area. The helmet is in the small surviving building. It improves ballistic protection, rather than filter life or mask-glass durability.

6. Battery Charge Controller
This one has a little puzzle. Go to the small island in the southern water with the ruined wooden house and generator shed. Find the fuel can behind the shed and start the generator.

Open the powered gate in the house, climb the boards and drop through the roof. Use the charger on the electrical panel, then go back through the red door and open the remaining powered room. Operate the switch beside the wired-up body and take the controller.

It helps the battery last longer. It doesn't replace the hand charger or mean that you never need to recharge anything again.

7. Metal Detector
Look for the little rusted, partly submerged shack west/southwest of the demon nest where you find the teddy bear, near the southern shore. Break the lock and check the desk among the clocks. This bracer attachment reacts to nearby crafting resources in the direction you're looking.

8. Night-Vision Goggles
These are on a table in the Terminal's confiscated-technology room. With the prisoners' key, you can enter early: after arriving by boat, take the ground-floor route left to the locked door.

There is also later access as you work through the Terminal. The key is a shortcut to getting them sooner, not the only possible way to obtain them.

Then there are five more in the Caspian:

9. Motion Scanner
Board the large slaver/bandit shipwreck along the western road and work up to the upper control area. Check the table. This uses the bracer slot and detects nearby enemies. Be careful not to hurt the captives while dealing with the people guarding them.

10. Extra Bright Flashlight
Search the smaller shipwreck safehouse below/west of the lighthouse, near the northwestern coastal road. Check for tripwires before walking in. You get a stronger beam, but it drains the battery faster. This replaces the battery controller or NVD amplifier in the electronics slot; those benefits don't all stack.

11. Armored Glass
Look for the bandit-occupied canyon west of the lighthouse, south of the northwestern water-source area. Clear the hostile occupants so the ladder lowers, then climb to the cave shelter and check the crate inside. This makes the gas mask harder to crack.

12. NVD Amplifier
Go to the abandoned airfield/helicopter base on the eastern side of the map. Climb the control tower to its top safehouse/control room and check the chair. It improves the night-vision picture. It is not a replacement for finding the goggles.

13. Consumables Carrier
Search the small cliffside cave/shelter north of the airfield, near the shoreline. Look beside the bed. This increases medkit and filter capacity, rather than ammunition or throwing-weapon capacity.

For Dressed for Success, collect all the suit modifications as you move through one continuous campaign. Don't assume that hopping between unrelated chapter saves will combine their equipment into one inventory.

The charging systems are worth separating too.

The flashlight and night-vision goggles use electrical power. Bring out the Universal Charger and operate it to recharge that equipment. If the flashlight starts getting weak, check the charge. You are not supposed to keep finding disposable batteries. The charger also powers certain electrical panels when the game gives you the interaction.

The Tikhar's usual pump is doing a different job. It restores air pressure in the weapon. Reloading bullets, pumping pressure and recharging your flashlight are separate actions. The late-game Railgun conversion changes the Tikhar's mechanism, not your suit's electronics upgrade.

Then there is the lighter. It provides a small light, burns away webs and can light suitable objects. You don't craft fuel for it or recharge it. It can help against spiderbugs, but holding up a flame also makes you more visible. Night vision is the better option when you want to see without lighting yourself up.

One thing not to bring over from earlier Metro guides: in Exodus, the lighter's smoke is not your objective pointer. Use the map or the compass upgrade for that.

The gas mask is another separate system. Filters handle the breathing supply; they don't repair cracked glass. A field patch is temporary. Use a workbench for a proper repair, and don't mistake wiping dirt off the visor for fixing damage.

💠Wagon revenue potential: 2,000 wagons a year gives ₹1,000 Cr+

💠Technology-sharing agreement with a Japanese company for refrigerated containers
💠Foundry for bogies, couplers and wheelsets: yet to commence

▫️1 lakh TEU plan (60 acres reserved):
💠~1 year and ~₹400 Cr
💠Scheme needs 1 lakh TEU for greenfield, 25,000 TEU for brownfield; 25,000 came as a “surprise”
💠Hoping for a large shipping line to partner with assured offtake
💠A government shipping line can be a customer, but a tie-up is uncertain

▫️Special containers: more than 50% of the ₹133 Cr order book
💠100 stainless steel containers recently given to JSW
💠Wheat container: 400 supplied, ~400 more expected within weeks
💠Salt container orders expected soon
💠Two-wheeler container appreciated by the Railway Minister

▫️New products:
💠Open-top dwarf container for steel: ~₹12–14 Cr revenue potential, volumes targeted at ~60,000 tons/month
💠Stainless steel container for salt: ~33.5 tons per box, Railways gave special rates
💠Super high volume 20 ft openable-roof container: ~400 supplied; wheat 33 T vs 26–27 T
💠40 ft super high cube for cotton bales: 200 bales per box
💠Triple-deck two-wheeler container: 72/90 bikes, tested with a major two-wheeler maker, orders expected soon
💠Foldable container and timber-log trials; no price disclosed

▫️New customers:
💠JSW Ports: ~1,500 containers this FY
💠Central Warehousing Corporation: ~₹30 Cr recent orders
💠Indian Navy: new customer
💠Western Carrier: 50 foldable containers supplied

👉Q&A :
▫️Competition and moat:
💠Container is low-tech and big companies avoid it, margins held by very low overheads
💠In wagons, moat is own patented design, not general-purpose wagons

▫️Demand outlook for containers:
💠Highly unpredictable, "yo-yo" cycle with no study on demand: "Bahut hi mushkil hai ye kaam karna"

▫️Risk view: order flow and margin delivery
💠Mitigation by growing capex with revenue and avoiding debt

▫️Quarterly reporting: not decided, will follow statutory requirement
💠Mainboard migration will bring quarterly results

▫️Railways' push for loading: "Unless you milk the cow fully, it will fall sick" (the Lalu Yadav line, on filling wagons to capacity)

▫️Copycats: “Nobody can beat the original”
💠Plants located in both the northern and western container regions
💠Open to others entering: “If somebody can do it in a better way let them also chalane do”
▫️Patent: the MOU with RDSO means RDSO cannot give the wagon design to anyone else without the company’s permission

▫️Import market:
💠Containers are international equipment owned by shipping lines
💠95–97% are made in China, which also gets cargo and zero empty repositioning cost
💠Scheme offers a ~$500 handicap per container
💠Company made ~5,500 domestic containers last year, ~60% share

▫️Overdue receivable: payments from one client’s ~₹4.7 Cr dues have started

👉 Others :
▫️FY26: revenue ₹149.99 Cr (+7.7% YoY), PAT ₹17.06 Cr (+19.8%), EPS ₹23.76 (+19.8%)
💠Company calls itself India's largest container manufacturer

▫️Padma Shri remark: when an investor praised the company for building this without an industrial house behind it, the MD replied “Toh Padma Shri dilwa dijiye ab”

▫️On hiring more managers: “Yeh aapko kya pata hai ki hamare paas nahi hai?”
💠Talking to stakeholders is “my prerogative”

text:
A new JED Foundation study dropped last week and the numbers should rattle every parent with a kid who has a phone. They surveyed more than 5,500 American middle and high school students across 21 schools, and what they found cuts through the usual "screen time bad" noise. It's a specific pattern of harm that most adults are missing entirely.

Fifty-seven percent of teens are using AI chatbots when they feel sad, stressed, lonely, or overwhelmed. That's more than half. And the outcomes get worse the more dependent they become on these systems. Twelve percent use AI for friendship or companionship, and that group shows significantly higher rates of anxiety, depression, loneliness, and history of suicidal thoughts and attempts. The same goes for the 28 percent seeking relationship advice from a bot. AI amplifies existing distress. It replaces human connection with something that simulates listening without caring.

The demographic breakdown matters too. Middle schoolers, girls, and kids from historically marginalised groups are more likely to turn to AI when they're struggling emotionally. That means the most vulnerable kids end up with a tool that makes them feel heard while giving them nothing that helps.

Dr Kayla Anderson, who led the study, said: "While AI may offer youth an immediate and accessible outlet, it cannot replicate the developmental, protective, and necessary benefits of human connection." That's the line that should be on every tech CEO's wall. We're building a generation that is learning to outsource its hardest moments to algorithms designed for engagement, not wellbeing.

WHAT I'M WATCHING TODAY — THURSDAY, OCTOBER 29
Good morning.
A major session ahead for U.S. economic data and corporate earnings.
After yesterday's Microsoft and Alphabet results, attention shifts to Amazon $AMZN, Intel $INTC, Eli Lilly $LLY, Coinbase $COIN and several major industrial companies.
The question I'm watching: Can economic growth remain resilient while inflation stays elevated, and are companies delivering the earnings and cash flow investors expect?
U.S. MACRO — ET
8:30 AM — MAIN EVENT: GDP + PCE INFLATION
🔹 Q3 GDP: 3.2% expected vs 2.2% previous
🔹 Core PCE MoM: 0.3% expected vs 0.2%
🔹 Core PCE YoY: 3.1% expected vs 3.0%
🔹 Headline PCE MoM: 0.5% expected vs 0.3%
🔹 Headline PCE YoY: 3.6% expected vs 3.4%
🔹 Personal Spending: +0.6% expected vs +0.9%
🔹 Personal Income: +0.3% expected vs +0.2%
🔹 Initial Jobless Claims: 199K expected vs 194K
🔹 Continuing Claims: 1.720M expected vs 1.728M
WHAT MATTERS
GDP is expected to accelerate, but inflation is also expected to move higher.
Stronger growth supports corporate earnings. Persistent inflation could limit the Fed's room to ease monetary policy.
I'll be watching the reaction in Treasury yields and equity valuations.
ADDITIONAL U.S. EVENTS
🔹 10:30 AM — EIA Natural Gas Inventories: +75 Bcf expected
🔹 1:00 PM — U.S. 7-Year Treasury Auction
EARNINGS — BEFORE THE BELL
🔹 $LLY Eli Lilly — Obesity drugs, demand and guidance
🔹 $MA Mastercard — Consumer spending and payments
🔹 $CAT Caterpillar — Industrial demand and margins
🔹 $MRK Merck — Pharmaceutical sales and pipeline
🔹 $MO Altria — Pricing, volumes and cash flow
🔹 $SHEL Shell — Energy, LNG and shareholder returns
🔹 $LIN Linde — Industrial demand and pricing
🔹 $BMY Bristol Myers — Drug sales and pipeline
🔹 $PGY Pagaya — Lending and credit performance
🔹 $CROX Crocs — Consumer demand and margins
🔹 $PWR Quanta Services — Grid investment and backlog
EARNINGS — AFTER THE CLOSE
🔹 $AMZN Amazon — AWS, AI CapEx and free cash flow
🔹 $INTC Intel — Foundry execution and profitability
🔹 $COIN Coinbase — Trading activity and crypto demand
🔹 $MSTR Strategy — Bitcoin exposure and financing
🔹 $RDDT Reddit — Advertising and monetisation
🔹 $SBUX Starbucks — Consumer traffic and turnaround
🔹 $SNDK Sandisk — NAND pricing and storage demand
🔹 $RIVN Rivian — Deliveries, margins and cash burn
🔹 $RBLX Roblox — Bookings and engagement
🔹 $FSLR First Solar — Manufacturing and margins
🔹 $PINS Pinterest — Advertising and engagement
MY MAIN FOCUS
1. GDP + CORE PCE — 8:30 AM ET
This could set the tone for the session.
Growth → Inflation → Fed expectations → Treasury yields → Equity valuations.
Strong growth is encouraging, but sticky inflation could keep borrowing costs elevated.
2. ELI LILLY $LLY
I'll be watching obesity treatment demand, pricing, manufacturing capacity and whether revenue growth is translating into stronger profitability.
3. CATERPILLAR $CAT + QUANTA SERVICES $PWR
Two useful indicators of physical infrastructure investment.
Caterpillar provides insight into industrial demand, while Quanta offers a view of grid modernisation and power infrastructure.
Both matter as AI infrastructure investment expands.
4. AMAZON $AMZN — MY BIGGEST EARNINGS FOCUS
AWS growth, AI infrastructure spending, advertising, operating margins and free cash flow.
Amazon has multiple growth engines, but its capital requirements are substantial.
Can AWS acceleration and operating leverage eventually translate into stronger free cash flow despite elevated investment?
5. INTEL $INTC
Foundry execution, manufacturing costs, product competitiveness and profitability.
The question is whether Intel can improve execution enough to generate sustainable returns on its manufacturing investment.
6. COINBASE $COIN + STRATEGY $MSTR
Two different exposures to cryptocurrency markets.
Coinbase provides insight into trading activity and transaction economics.
Strategy is more directly exposed to Bitcoin prices, financing and balance-sheet risks.
7. SANDISK $SNDK
NAND pricing, enterprise storage demand and profitability.
I'll be watching whether AI-related storage demand is supporting margins alongside the broader memory cycle.
8. REDDIT $RDDT + PINTEREST $PINS
Digital advertising, engagement and monetisation.
Both offer insight into advertising spending beyond the largest technology platforms.
MY TAKE
Three things matter today.
🔹 Macro: Can growth remain resilient without reigniting inflation?
🔹 AI infrastructure: Are companies converting demand into profitable growth and cash flow?
🔹 Corporate spending: Are businesses maintaining pricing power and margins?
Amazon will be particularly important for understanding AI infrastructure economics.
But GDP and PCE come first.
Strong economic growth alongside persistent inflation could support earnings expectations while keeping pressure on valuations through higher interest rates.
That's the tension I'm watching.

Operating EBITDA margin: 29.3%, versus 29.7%
PAT: ₹160.2 crore, up only 5.4%
Q1 FY27 (Apr–Jun 2026): revenue ₹133.9 crore, PAT only ₹1.5 crore, operating EBITDA margin 7.4%
The business is seasonal: 86% of wastewater revenue comes in the second half of the year.

✅ WHAT WORKS IN ITS FAVOUR

Market leader with its own technology: 80%+ SBR market share and 20 years of experience.

High margins: operating EBITDA margin has stayed around 29% for three years.

It looks cheap against peers: 20.9× FY26 EPS, against Ion Exchange at 31.34× and Thermax at 52.01×.

Strong anchor book: mutual funds took 89% of it.

Smart money bought above the IPO price. The Gogri family bought ₹69 crore of shares at ₹343 on 12–13 Oct 2026, above the ₹330 cap.

Structural demand from water scarcity, waste mandates and the CBG blending push.

⚠️ WHAT HOLDS ME BACK

Profit is not turning into cash. From FY24 to Q1 FY27, PAT was ₹458 crore but operating cash flow was only ₹6.7 crore. Operating cash flow was negative in FY24, FY26 and Q1 FY27.

Customers pay very slowly. Receivable days went from 197 (FY24) to 262 to 282, and reached 443 days in June 2026. ₹660 crore was uncollected at March 2026, about 82% of the year’s revenue.

Government dependence: 92% of wastewater revenue and 100% of solid waste revenue is linked to government. When the government pays late, SFC waits.

Mostly an OFS. ₹517.5 crore of the ₹667.5 crore goes to sellers, whose average cost is ₹36.72, about 9× below the issue price. Promoter Dhandoriya is selling 44% of his stake.

Low promoter holding: promoters and the promoter group hold only about 41% after the IPO.

Debt is rising. Borrowings went from ₹84 crore to ₹205 crore in 15 months. Most of the fresh issue goes to working capital and repaying debt, not growth.

Legal risk: a Portuguese municipality is claiming €5.6 million (₹59.75 crore, 37% of FY26 PAT) against its Austrian subsidiary. There are also Goa pollution board notices.

The order book includes MoUs and LoIs, so not all of it is firm. EPS grew only 4.4% a year from FY24 to FY26.

💰 VALUATION

At ₹330, market capitalisation is about ₹3,233 crore. That is 20.9× FY26 EPS.

The RHP’s peer average is 101.38×, inflated by Praj at 220.77×. Ion Exchange, the closest peer, is at 31.34×.

Price to book after the issue is about 3.4×.

My fair value range: ₹146–561. My base case is about ₹310, roughly 6% below the IPO price. The P/E looks cheap, but the cash flow risk removes the margin of safety.

🏛️ ANCHOR BOOK

₹200.26 crore was allocated across 17 anchor allocations at ₹330, the top of the band.

SBI Infrastructure Fund: ₹37.50 crore
Nippon India MF (2 schemes): ₹37.50 crore
ICICI Prudential MF (3 schemes): ₹34.25 crore
Quant MF (2 long-short funds): ₹34.25 crore
Sundaram Small Cap Fund: ₹10 crore
Edelweiss Life Insurance: ₹10 crore
Norway’s Government Pension Fund Global: ₹6.75 crore

Mutual funds took 89.14% across 8 AMCs and 14 schemes. Insurers took 4.99%. Société Générale came in through an ODI (₹5 crore).

📊 SUBSCRIPTION (Day 3, 1:15 PM)

QIB: 0.61× 🚨
NII: 1.23×
Retail: 0.54× 🚨
Total: 0.71×

The issue is still not fully covered on the last day. Retail has bid for only about half its quota. A strong anchor book did not turn into demand in the main QIB portion.

📈 GMP

GMP is ₹6 (1.82%) as of 29 Oct, 1:02 PM, pointing to a listing near ₹336.

It has fallen at every update since its peak: ₹32 (24–25 Oct) → ₹20 (26 Oct) → ₹17 (27 Oct) → ₹10 (28 Oct) → ₹6 (29 Oct). That is down 81% from the peak.

⚠️ GMP is unofficial and can fall anytime before listing. Don’t apply only because of GMP.

📝 MY VIEW

I am not applying.

SFC is a good business at a fair-looking P/E. But profit is not turning into cash, receivables are at 443 days, and 77.5% of the issue is promoters and investors selling. There is no listing gain and no margin of safety.

Not SEBI registered. Educational purposes only. Do your own research. GMP is unofficial and listing gains are not assured.

text:
She was only three months old when she disappeared in broad daylight. More than two decades later, her family is still waiting for answers.

On May 6, 2001, 18-year-old Olivia Castaneda took her two young daughters to a swap meet near 123rd Avenue and Buckeye Road in Avondale, Arizona.

Her youngest daughter, Jacqueline Vasquez, was just three months old. Her older sister, Nayeli, was two.

At around 11:15 a.m., the family arrived after being dropped off by Olivia’s husband, 21-year-old Jorge Vasquez.

Olivia carried Jacqueline in her infant carrier and held Nayeli’s hand as they walked into the busy market. Before meeting her mother at a booth, Olivia needed to use a portable restroom.

Worried that Nayeli might wander away in the cramped space, Olivia made a decision she would never stop thinking about. She left Jacqueline, still in her carrier, on the ground just outside while she took Nayeli inside.

It took only about a minute.

When Olivia came back out, Jacqueline and her carrier had vanished.

At first, Olivia rushed to her mother’s booth, hoping she had taken the baby. When she discovered Jacqueline wasn’t there, the two women desperately searched the market, asking vendors and shoppers whether anyone had seen her.

About 20 minutes later, police were called.

Officers sealed off the swap meet, monitored the exits, and checked vehicles leaving the area. But Jacqueline was nowhere to be found.

Witnesses reported seeing a woman behaving suspiciously near the portable restrooms. One vendor recalled a woman approaching her booth and affectionately touching her own infant while commenting on how beautiful the baby was. Another witness described a woman lingering near the bathrooms.

Sketches were created, but neither woman was conclusively identified.

Investigators later examined footage recorded by a television cameraman showing a woman leaving the market with an infant. Olivia believed the baby might be Jacqueline. However, police located and questioned the woman and determined that she was not connected to the disappearance.

Authorities also sought information about an unidentified red pickup truck seen near the swap meet. Whether it was connected to Jacqueline’s disappearance remains unknown.

Investigators ruled out Jacqueline’s parents as suspects and considered the possibility that she had been abducted by a woman who wanted to raise a child of her own. They believed the abductor might not have intended to harm her, although the motive has never been established.

The disappearance brought Olivia into contact with Colleen Nick, whose daughter Morgan had vanished in Arkansas in 1995. Through the Morgan Nick Foundation, Colleen helped distribute information about Jacqueline and offered emotional support to her family.

For Olivia, speaking with someone who understood the pain of having a child disappear offered a kind of comfort that few others could provide.

But comfort could never replace the little girl who was missing.

Jacqueline has black hair, brown eyes, and a distinctive heart-shaped birthmark on her upper right arm. The FBI and the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children became involved in efforts to find her.

Jacqueline was only three months old. She could not call for help, tell anyone her name, or find her way home. She depended entirely on the adults around her.

Somewhere, there may be someone who remembers something about that day. Someone who knows what happened to a baby who disappeared from a crowded public place in less than a minute.

More than two decades have passed, but Jacqueline’s story remains unresolved.

Her family deserves answers. Jacqueline deserves to know who she is and where she came from.

She was not forgotten when she disappeared. And she must not be forgotten now.
