ethereum:0xb31561f0e2aac72406103b1926356d756f07a481 — VOOI

Everyone is watching $HYPE, $ASTER, and $LIT.

But one much smaller project is building the trading infrastructure that connects them.

Over $33 BILLION in cumulative perpetual trading volume.

Its market cap? Approximately $3 million.

Its fully diluted valuation? Around $9 million.

Sounds ridiculously undervalued?

Here's the catch: Billions in trading volume don't necessarily mean millions in revenue for token holders.

NO.1 WHAT IS VOOI?

VOOI is a self-custodial DeFi trading aggregator backed by YZi Labs.

Instead of building another perpetual exchange, it connects existing trading venues through one interface.

Its products include:

Perpetual futures aggregation
Cross-chain trading
Unified trading balances
Funding-rate arbitrage tools
Developer execution APIs

VOOI isn't trying to replace every perpetual DEX. It's trying to become the interface connecting them.

NO.2 WHERE DOES THE DEMAND COME FROM?

Perpetual traders want better liquidity, lower fees, and simpler execution.

Developers want access to multiple exchanges without building separate integrations.

VOOI serves both.

More traders → More routed volume → Potentially more platform revenue.

But the critical question is how much of that volume VOOI actually monetizes.

NO.3 THE BIG NARRATIVE

VOOI combines three narratives:

Perpetual DEX aggregation
Chain abstraction
AI-powered trading infrastructure

As liquidity spreads across Hyperliquid, Lighter, Aster, and other venues, trading becomes increasingly fragmented.

The next big opportunity may not be another exchange. It may be the infrastructure that connects all of them.

NO.4 THE REAL COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE

VOOI already has functioning products and substantial historical trading activity.

Its platform reports:

$30B+ cumulative trading volume
140K+ traders
500+ supported crypto and RWA perpetual markets
Multiple integrated trading venues

Its developer infrastructure also supports automated execution and cross-venue strategies.

But there's a weakness.

Aggregators depend on the liquidity and infrastructure of the exchanges they connect.

And competing interfaces can offer similar functionality.

NO.5 THE NUMBERS THAT MATTER

Market Snapshot — October 29, 2026

Price: ~$0.0087
Market cap: ~$3M
FDV: ~$8.7M
Circulating supply: ~344.9M VOOI
Maximum supply: 1B VOOI
Circulating ratio: ~34.5%
24H token trading volume: ~$436K
Decline from ATH: ~95.7%

Protocol Activity

Cumulative perpetual aggregator volume: ~$33.6B
30-day perpetual aggregator volume: ~$420M
7-day volume: ~$116M
Verified 30-day protocol revenue: Unavailable
Verified token-holder revenue: Unavailable

Here's the striking comparison.

A $3M token market cap against more than $400M in monthly routed trading volume.

That's a remarkable activity-to-valuation ratio.

But routed volume isn't revenue, and revenue isn't automatically token-holder value.

NO.6 THE TOKENOMICS TRAP

Maximum supply: 1 billion VOOI.

Approximately 34.5% is circulating.

Original allocations include:

Community growth and marketing: 27.82%
Foundation: 31%
Contributors: 17%
Strategic investors: 13.65%
Airdrops and community sale: 10.53%

That's a substantial amount of future supply.

The $3M market cap looks tiny. But roughly 65.5% of maximum supply remains outside circulation.

The token is fixed-supply, but not fully distributed.

NO.7 THE NEXT BIG UNLOCK

VOOI launched on December 18, 2025.

Its official vesting terms include:

Contributors: 12-month cliff, then 24-month linear vesting
Strategic investors: 6–12-month cliff, then 12–18-month vesting
Foundation: 36-month linear vesting
Community growth: 36-month linear vesting

The next exact aggregate unlock date and amount could not be independently verified.

But one important milestone is approaching.

The contributor cliff reaches its 12-month anniversary in December 2026.

That doesn't mean the entire contributor allocation unlocks at once.

It means investors should closely monitor the transition into team vesting.

NO.8 THE VALUE CAPTURE QUESTION

VOOI's documented token utility includes:

Governance
Trading fee discounts
Staking rewards
Yield boosts
Ecosystem incentives

The project also allows governance to authorize token buybacks.

But there's a distinction.

Potential buybacks are not the same as a guaranteed recurring buyback program.

And staking rewards paid in VOOI don't necessarily represent external business revenue.

I couldn't verify a recurring fee-sharing mechanism that distributes platform profits directly to holders.

VOOI can route billions in trades while the token captures relatively little of that economic activity.

NO.9 THE FINAL VERDICT

I'm interested in VOOI's business positioning.

It has a real product, substantial historical trading volume, and exposure to the growing perpetual DEX ecosystem.

Its valuation is also dramatically smaller than many competing crypto trading projects.

But the token investment thesis remains speculative.

My verdict: Impressive trading distribution. Tiny valuation. Unproven revenue capture and significant dilution risk.

I'd become more bullish if VOOI demonstrated recurring platform revenue, stronger paid API adoption, and a transparent mechanism connecting that revenue to VOOI demand.

$33 billion in cumulative trading volume is impressive. But the real opportunity begins when that activity becomes sustainable economic value for the token.

Bookmark this before the next perpetual DEX rotation.

text:
hive:native — Hive Blockchain
ㅤ
Everyone is watching solana:So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112, $TON, and near:native compete for the future of consumer blockchain applications.
ㅤ
But what about a blockchain that has processed more than 4 billion transactions, supports over 150 applications, and still trades almost 99% below its all-time high?
ㅤ
Meet hive:native — Hive Blockchain.
ㅤ
A decentralized network built around social media, digital ownership, gaming, and community-driven applications.
ㅤ
The project isn't new.
ㅤ
It launched in March 2020 following a community-led fork of Steem.
ㅤ
And unlike many cryptocurrencies promising future adoption, Hive already has functioning applications and a long operational history.
ㅤ
But there's a major problem.
ㅤ
Billions of transactions haven't translated into sustained token price appreciation.
ㅤ
Save this checklist:
ㅤ
-> Where the demand comes from
ㅤ
Traditional social media platforms control much of the infrastructure behind online communities.
ㅤ
User accounts.
Content distribution.
Monetization.
Platform rules.
Access to audiences.
ㅤ
Creators build communities on platforms they don't own.
ㅤ
Hive takes a different approach.
ㅤ
It provides an open blockchain where users can publish content, interact with communities, transfer value, and earn cryptocurrency rewards.
ㅤ
Applications can share the same underlying social and financial infrastructure.
ㅤ
The opportunity is straightforward.
ㅤ
More creators.
More communities.
More applications.
More demand for blockchain resources.
ㅤ
But user activity doesn't automatically translate into token price appreciation.
ㅤ
-> Main narrative
ㅤ
Decentralized Social Media.
Web3 Infrastructure.
Creator Economy.
SocialFi.
Blockchain Gaming.
Digital Ownership.
Community Governance.
ㅤ
hive:native sits at the intersection of several crypto narratives.
ㅤ
But its strongest argument isn't speculation.
ㅤ
It's that the network already exists and operates.
ㅤ
-> The real advantage
ㅤ
Hive was designed to make blockchain applications accessible to ordinary users.
ㅤ
Zero Transaction Fees — Users spend Resource Credits rather than paying conventional gas fees.
ㅤ
Three-Second Blocks — Fast transaction processing.
ㅤ
Hive Power — Staked HIVE used for governance, influence, and network resources.
ㅤ
Delegated Proof of Stake — Stakeholder-elected witnesses secure the blockchain.
ㅤ
Decentralized Social Infrastructure — Multiple applications can use shared accounts and content.
ㅤ
Hive Backed Dollars — HBD provides a separate stable-value asset within the ecosystem.
ㅤ
The Resource Credits model is particularly interesting.
ㅤ
Users who stake HIVE gain access to transaction capacity.
ㅤ
That creates a connection between network resource demand and token staking.
ㅤ
But there is a tradeoff.
ㅤ
Zero-fee transactions don't generate conventional gas-fee revenue.
ㅤ
And a functioning network doesn't automatically generate profits for tokenholders.
ㅤ
-> The numbers are interesting
ㅤ
As of October 29, 2026:
ㅤ
~$0.049 — HIVE price.
~$29M — Reported market capitalization.
~593M — Circulating supply under CoinMarketCap's methodology.
No fixed maximum supply.
~$3.42 — Historical all-time high.
~98.6% — Decline from ATH.
ㅤ
Official Hive ecosystem statistics:
ㅤ
4.2B+ — Cumulative blockchain transactions.
158 — Listed ecosystem applications.
248 — Listed communities.
3 seconds — Target block interval.
ㅤ
These numbers tell two very different stories.
ㅤ
The network has processed substantial historical activity.
ㅤ
But the token trades at a small fraction of its previous valuation.
ㅤ
That's an important contradiction.
ㅤ
And investors need to understand why.
ㅤ
-> The adoption reality check
ㅤ
Four billion transactions sounds enormous.
ㅤ
But not every blockchain transaction represents a financial payment.
ㅤ
Hive records social interactions.
ㅤ
Posts.
Comments.
Votes.
Transfers.
Reward-related operations.
ㅤ
That means transaction count cannot be directly compared with financial settlement volume on other blockchains.
ㅤ
A social media vote and a $10,000 financial transfer are economically different activities.
ㅤ
And cumulative transactions don't reveal how many users remain active today.
ㅤ
The important questions are:
ㅤ
How many people actively use Hive applications?
ㅤ
How many creators earn sustainable income?
ㅤ
How much capital is actually moving through the ecosystem?
ㅤ
And how many users need to acquire or stake HIVE?
ㅤ
Those metrics matter more than historical transaction totals.
ㅤ
-> The ecosystem advantage
ㅤ
Hive supports several established Web3 applications.
ㅤ
PeakD — Decentralized publishing and community interaction.
ㅤ
Ecency — Social media applications built on Hive.
ㅤ
https://t.co/x7wnDnxPr0 — Blockchain-powered blogging and content rewards.
ㅤ
Splinterlands — Blockchain-based trading card gaming.
ㅤ
These applications demonstrate that Hive is more than a theoretical infrastructure project.
ㅤ
Real products have been built around its technology.
ㅤ
But the competitive challenge is enormous.
ㅤ
Traditional social platforms already have massive audiences.
ㅤ
And crypto-native social platforms continue evolving.
ㅤ
Hive needs more than functioning applications.
ㅤ
It needs sustained user growth and stronger economic demand.
ㅤ
-> The HIVE and HBD relationship
ㅤ
This is one of the most interesting parts of the ecosystem.
ㅤ
Hive uses a dual-token economic model.
ㅤ
HIVE — The native asset used for network participation, governance, and staking.
ㅤ
HBD — Hive Backed Dollars, a blockchain-native stablecoin designed to maintain a value around $1.
ㅤ
HBD supports transfers, savings, and financial activity within the ecosystem.
ㅤ
HIVE provides the underlying economic and governance infrastructure.
ㅤ
But there's an important risk.
ㅤ
HBD is not the same as a fully cash-reserve-backed stablecoin.
ㅤ
Its stability depends on blockchain mechanisms, market conditions, and the relationship with HIVE.
ㅤ
Severe market stress could challenge that stability.
ㅤ
And attractive HBD savings yields should not be confused with risk-free returns.
ㅤ
-> The tokenomics problem
ㅤ
Unlike many newer altcoins, HIVE doesn't face a large conventional venture-capital vesting schedule.
ㅤ
But that doesn't mean the token is free from dilution.
ㅤ
HIVE has no fixed maximum supply.
ㅤ
New tokens are created through network inflation.
ㅤ
Historically, the protocol's issuance schedule began at 9.5% annually, declining by approximately 0.5 percentage points per year toward a long-term floor of 0.95%.
ㅤ
New issuance supports:
ㅤ
Content creator rewards.
Curation rewards.
Staking-related rewards.
Block producers.
Ecosystem funding.
ㅤ
This is central to Hive's economic model.
ㅤ
The network uses newly created tokens to incentivize participation.
ㅤ
But newly issued rewards can also become selling pressure.
ㅤ
If creators and participants consistently sell their rewards, external demand must absorb that supply.
ㅤ
That's the challenge.
ㅤ
A network can have active users and still struggle to support its token price.
ㅤ
-> The staking angle
ㅤ
Hive Power is created by staking HIVE.
ㅤ
It provides influence over content rewards, governance participation, and access to network resources.
ㅤ
This gives HIVE practical utility.
ㅤ
More users requiring Resource Credits could create demand for staked HIVE.
ㅤ
More community participation could increase demand for governance influence.
ㅤ
But staking is not automatically equivalent to economic profit.
ㅤ
Some rewards come from newly issued tokens.
ㅤ
And increased staking participation doesn't guarantee a rising market price.
ㅤ
Investors need to monitor net demand after inflation.
ㅤ
-> The valuation reality check
ㅤ
Using approximately $29M in market capitalization:
ㅤ
2x — ~$58M.
5x — ~$145M.
10x — ~$290M.
ㅤ
These are valuation scenarios, not price predictions.
ㅤ
A relatively small market capitalization creates speculative upside potential.
ㅤ
But HIVE's supply is not fixed.
ㅤ
Future token issuance means market capitalization and token-price returns may not grow proportionally.
ㅤ
A 10x increase in market capitalization does not necessarily mean a 10x increase in token price if circulating supply expands.
ㅤ
And a historical price near $3.42 is not automatically a reasonable recovery target.
ㅤ
-> The competitive landscape
ㅤ
$TON — Consumer applications and Telegram ecosystem connectivity.
ㅤ
near:native — Blockchain infrastructure and user-friendly applications.
ㅤ
solana:So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112 — High-throughput applications and consumer crypto activity.
ㅤ
hive:native — Decentralized social media and community-owned content infrastructure.
ㅤ
Hive's biggest competition also comes from outside crypto.
ㅤ
X.
Reddit.
YouTube.
Traditional creator platforms.
ㅤ
Those platforms already have enormous network effects.
ㅤ
Hive needs to offer compelling reasons for users and creators to migrate.
ㅤ
Token rewards alone may not be enough.
ㅤ
-> The biggest investment question
ㅤ
Can Hive become a major decentralized social platform while HIVE remains undervalued?
ㅤ
Possibly.
ㅤ
But investors need to separate three things.
ㅤ
Blockchain activity.
ㅤ
Application adoption.
ㅤ
Token demand.
ㅤ
They are connected, but they are not identical.
ㅤ
More posts don't automatically create more token purchases.
ㅤ
More transactions don't automatically generate protocol revenue.
ㅤ
And more token rewards can increase circulating supply.
ㅤ
The strongest long-term investment thesis would require growing organic demand for HIVE that exceeds ongoing issuance and selling pressure.
ㅤ
-> Bull case
ㅤ
If decentralized social media adoption accelerates, Hive could benefit.
ㅤ
More active creators.
More community applications.
Higher demand for Resource Credits.
Greater HIVE staking participation.
More HBD financial activity.
Stronger gaming and SocialFi integrations.
ㅤ
Its existing infrastructure could become an advantage if Web3 social adoption expands.
ㅤ
At a relatively small market capitalization, meaningful growth could attract renewed speculative interest.
ㅤ
But that growth needs to be measurable.
ㅤ
-> Bear case
ㅤ
The risks are substantial.
ㅤ
Competition from established social platforms.
ㅤ
Limited mainstream adoption.
ㅤ
Ongoing token inflation.
ㅤ
Reward-driven selling pressure.
ㅤ
Uncertain direct tokenholder value capture.
ㅤ
HBD stability risks.
ㅤ
Governance concentration among large stakeholders.
ㅤ
And a 98% price decline doesn't guarantee recovery.
ㅤ
The blockchain could remain operational for years without delivering strong token returns.
ㅤ
-> What to watch
ㅤ
Daily active accounts.
ㅤ
Monthly active social users.
ㅤ
Organic transaction growth.
ㅤ
HIVE Power staking participation.
ㅤ
Net token issuance.
ㅤ
Creator reward selling pressure.
ㅤ
HBD market stability.
ㅤ
New application adoption.
ㅤ
Gaming ecosystem activity.
ㅤ
Demand for Resource Credits.
ㅤ
My view:
ㅤ
Narrative: 7/10
Utility: 7/10
Adoption: 6/10
Tokenomics: 5/10
Risk: Very High
Long-Term Outlook: Cautiously Speculative
ㅤ
Hive is an interesting example of a cryptocurrency with real infrastructure and a long operating history.
ㅤ
It has functioning applications.
ㅤ
An established community.
ㅤ
A native stablecoin.
ㅤ
And billions of recorded blockchain operations.
ㅤ
Those are meaningful achievements.
ㅤ
But the biggest weakness is obvious.
ㅤ
Historical network activity hasn't translated into sustainable long-term token appreciation.
ㅤ
The economic model continuously distributes newly issued tokens.
ㅤ
And organic buying demand must be strong enough to absorb that supply.
ㅤ
I like the decentralized social media concept.
ㅤ
I like the network's operating history.
ㅤ
But I want stronger evidence of growing active users, productive staking demand, and sustainable economic activity before becoming more bullish on HIVE long term.
ㅤ
A blockchain can have billions of transactions and still be a weak investment.
ㅤ
Usage matters.
ㅤ
But value capture matters even more.
ㅤ
Save this for your Web3 and SocialFi watchlist.
ㅤ

ㅤ

ethereum:0x75231f58b43240c9718dd58b4967c5114342a86c has OKX.

ethereum:0x61ec85ab89377db65762e234c946b5c25a56e99e has the HTX exchange ecosystem.

But there's a critical difference.

An exchange can generate billions in trading volume without creating equivalent value for its token holders.

HTX DAO has a token-burning model designed to connect exchange activity to token supply.

The opportunity is straightforward: benefit from exchange growth and a shrinking token supply.

The risk? Exchange dependence, governance concentration, and whether the burn mechanism delivers meaningful long-term value.

NO.1 WHAT IS HTX DAO?

HTX DAO is a decentralized autonomous organization associated with the HTX exchange ecosystem.

Its token, ethereum:0x61ec85ab89377db65762e234c946b5c25a56e99e, supports governance and ecosystem participation.

The project aims to connect exchange activity, community incentives, and token economics.

But owning HTX does not mean owning equity in the HTX exchange.

NO.2 WHERE DOES THE DEMAND COME FROM?

Potential demand comes from:

Exchange ecosystem participation
Governance and community incentives
Promotional and utility programs
Speculation on future token burns

The central thesis is that continued exchange activity can support the token's economics.

But trading volume alone isn't enough.

What matters is how much economic value actually reaches HTX holders.

NO.3 THE BIG NARRATIVE

HTX belongs to the exchange-token sector alongside $BNB and ethereum:0x75231f58b43240c9718dd58b4967c5114342a86c.

Exchange tokens offer exposure to the growth of crypto trading infrastructure.

But they're not interchangeable.

Their utility, ownership structures, fee mechanisms, and regulatory risks differ significantly.

The strongest exchange token isn't necessarily attached to the largest exchange. It's the one with the most durable token demand.

NO.4 THE REAL COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE

HTX benefits from an established exchange ecosystem rather than starting with no distribution.

Its advantages include existing exchange users, liquidity, branding, and a token-burning framework.

But its dependence on one exchange ecosystem is also a weakness.

If exchange competitiveness deteriorates, the token's investment narrative can weaken with it.

Total pledged and burned, as reported by HTX DAO: ~$235M

Over $71M in tokens were burned across the four reported 2026 quarterly events.

That's meaningful relative to a $1.44B market cap.

But the reported cumulative pledge-and-burn total also includes liquidity-related mechanisms. It shouldn't be treated entirely as direct token repurchases.

NO.6 THE TOKENOMICS TRAP

HTX launched with a maximum supply of approximately 1 quadrillion tokens.

The reported circulating supply is now close to 89% of that figure.

Its tokenomics are unusual because the primary supply narrative is deflation rather than conventional staking emissions.

But investors should distinguish three things:

Tokens circulating
Tokens permanently burned
Tokens still controlled by large holders

A shrinking total supply doesn't eliminate concentration risk.

And a token with hundreds of trillions of units isn't cheap simply because its unit price has many zeros.

NO.7 THE NEXT BIG UNLOCK

I couldn't verify a reliable upcoming dated team or investor vesting cliff.

That doesn't prove every remaining token is permanently locked or unavailable.

The more important scheduled catalyst is the quarterly burn program.

For HTX, the next burn announcement matters more than an unverified unlock countdown.

Investors should monitor the amount burned, the funding mechanism, and whether burns remain consistent as trading conditions change.

NO.8 THE VALUE CAPTURE QUESTION

This is HTX's strongest argument.

Its published tokenomics describe allocating 50% of platform revenue toward quarterly HTX buybacks and burns.

The official burn history confirms substantial token destruction during 2026.

That creates a clearer economic link than governance-only tokens with no fee-based value capture.

But there's a distinction.

Burning tokens is not the same as distributing cash to holders.

Token holders benefit only if reduced supply contributes to sustained demand relative to available supply.

And the burn model depends on the exchange's continued financial performance and execution of its policy.

NO.9 THE FINAL VERDICT

I'm more interested in HTX's token economics than its extremely low unit price.

A functioning quarterly burn program is a legitimate advantage over tokens with no meaningful value-accrual mechanism.

But this isn't an undiscovered microcap.

At approximately $1.44B market cap, investors are already paying for substantial expectations.

My verdict: Real burns. Established exchange distribution. Significant dependence on centralized exchange performance.

I'd become more bullish if HTX maintained substantial burns, strengthened transparent reporting, and demonstrated durable exchange market share.

🔴 Pentagon watchdog declines to investigate Starlink disruptions in Ukraine

The Pentagon’s inspector general has declined a bipartisan request from nine US senators to investigate recent disruptions affecting Starlink and its military-grade counterpart, Starshield, in #Ukraine, the Associated Press reports.

Ukrainian officials had reported connection speed restrictions that complicated efforts to intercept Russian attack drones. However, the #Pentagon watchdog said the US Air Force was better placed to address the lawmakers’ concerns.

Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen criticised the decision, noting that the Trump administration and SpaceX had offered conflicting explanations for the disruptions. She called for an independent review to establish accountability and prevent similar incidents in the future.

On October 24, Ukraine’s Defence Ministry reported that Starlink and Starshield speeds had been restored to their pre-restriction levels.

text:
MASS EFFECT 3: SOLDIER, ADEPT, AND ENGINEER

ME3 opens every weapon category to every class. The tradeoff is weight: a lighter loadout improves power recharge, while a heavy one slows it. Soldier can build the highest carrying capacity; Adept and Engineer have the lowest potential capacity.

Most cooldown-based powers still share a timer within a character, but the combo system is much broader. You prime a target, then use a compatible detonator. Biotic explosions, tech bursts, fire explosions, and cryo explosions all matter. Do not assume every pair of powers will combine, or that every protection type allows every setup.

SOLDIER

Pros: Excellent weapon flexibility, high carrying capacity, Adrenaline Rush, and several ammo powers. It also participates in combos: ammo effects can prime suitable targets, and Concussive Shot can detonate tech, fire, and cryo setups. The Amplification evolution adds further options.

Cons: All classes can now use the same weapon categories, so you are choosing Soldier for its bonuses and combat powers rather than exclusive access. Carrying a huge arsenal still has a recharge cost, and there is less native battlefield control than the specialist classes offer.

Choose Soldier if you want gunplay to stay central without ignoring ME3's power-combo system. It is more capable than the idea that Soldier means never using powers.

ADEPT

Pros: A strong self-contained biotic combo toolkit. Warp followed by Throw is a basic example, while Singularity and Pull control enemies that can be lifted. A light weapon loadout lets you keep setting up and detonating powers at a quick pace.

Cons: Shields still interfere with lifting effects, and the normal kit has no Overload. You need to distinguish between enemies you can control and enemies you should damage through combos. Heavy guns in your loadout can undermine the rapid casting that makes the class work so well.

Choose Adept if you want frequent biotic attacks and explosions. Do not judge it only by the restrictions that made ME2 Adept more demanding.

ENGINEER

Pros: Overload is useful against both shields and barriers here, Incinerate handles armor, and the expanded combo system turns tech powers into serious damage tools. Combat Drone and Sentry Turret offer distractions, while Sabotage adds more disruption.

Cons: Summons do not replace positioning, and investing in every available tool can spread your points thin. Like Adept, Engineer has a relatively low weight capacity, so a gun-heavy loadout can get in the way of a power-focused build.

Choose Engineer if you want tech combos, defense-stripping, and deployable support. You can lean into the constructs or emphasize direct powers instead of treating every Engineer as the same build.

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. The two companies would make excellent merger partners; amongst others things, their staff and senior people have similar cultures, they are co-operating on future Australian iron ore projects and they are copper joint venture partners in Chile and the US. Meanwhile, there are significance cultural differences between Rio Tinto and Glencore; there is little doubt that Rio Tinto's CEO Simon Trott would have had doubts about a merger once he understood these cultural differences. (RMS)

News/Snapshot

Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic expands

The value of Alphabet’s stake in the artificial intelligence start-up Anthropic has soared to around $US124 billion ($178 billion), making it one of the most lucrative bets in the company’s history.The Google parent disclosed in a filing on Thursday (Friday AEST) that the value of its investments in unidentified private companies totalled roughly $US124.3 billion as of June 30. The filing noted that this value is “primarily” driven by one investment, which is a reference to Alphabet’s stake in Anthropic, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified because the information is not public. The company said it recorded about $US77 billion in unrealised gains from its private investments in the second quarter, without providing further details in the filing. Google has emerged as one of Anthropic’s biggest backers over the past several years. The technology giant first invested $US3 billion in the start-up starting in 2023. Earlier this year, it agreed to invest as much as $US40 billion more, consisting of $US10 billion upfront and a potential $US30 billion in additional funding tied to operational and financial milestones through 2030.Alphabet’s filing on Thursday showed the remaining commitment has fallen to $US20 billion as of June 30 from $US30 billion at the end of the first quarter, suggesting that Google invested another $US10 billion in the start-up last quarter. Rio Tinto dodges merger bullet

Rio Tinto has dodged two 'bullets' due to Glencore's rejection of a merger proposal: a possible BHP takeover bid and a dangerous acquisition. BHP looked closely at whether to bid for Rio Tinto if the latter announced a merger with Glencore. Australian Mining

Global Commodity Rankings

Australia holds some of the world's largest reserves and is a leading producer of several key minerals.

#1 Producer: Iron Ore, Bauxite, Lithium, Rutile, and Zircon.

#1 Reserves: Iron Ore, Gold, Lead, Nickel, Rutile, Uranium, and Zinc.

#2 Producer: Gold, Alumina, and Manganese.

Key Mining Hubs & Major Projects

Western Australia: The nation's "engine room," producing 98% of Australia's iron ore and 60% of its gold. Major sites include the Pilbara (iron ore) and the Super Pit in Kalgoorlie (gold).

Queensland: A global leader in metallurgical coal (Bowen Basin) and silver/lead production (Cannington mine).

South Australia: Home to Olympic Dam, which contains the world's largest single uranium deposit and significant copper and gold reserves.

Major Players

The sector is dominated by several multinational giants and significant domestic players:

BHP: Often ranked as Australia's most valuable company; major interests in iron ore, copper, and coal.

Rio Tinto: A world leader in iron ore (Pilbara) and aluminum.

Fortescue (FMG): Primarily focused on iron ore and rapidly expanding into green energy.

Hancock Prospecting: Australia's largest private mining company, led by Gina Rinehart, the nation's wealthiest person.

South32: Spun out of BHP; manages a diversified portfolio including manganese, silver, and nickel.

2026 Trends & Developments

Critical Minerals Push: The government has introduced a $23 billion package to support domestic processing and manufacturing of critical minerals to reduce global reliance on single-country supply chains.

Uranium Rally: Prices exceeding US$100/lb have sparked renewed interest in Australian prospects like the Kalkaroo project.

M&A Activity: Major merger talks continue between giants like Rio Tinto and Glencore as they seek to consolidate copper exposure for the EV market.

Workforce Challenges: The Minerals Council of Australia is currently calling for migration reforms to address a significant "skills crunch" in the sector.

1. Iran says three tankers struck mines around Hormuz in the past 24 hours. The claim comes via Fars and hasn’t been independently confirmed. UKMTO continues to report elevated maritime-security risks across the region.

2. US-Iran diplomacy is still alive -- JD Vance has reached out to Iran’s Mohsen Rezaei about restarting negotiations, even as the possibility of renewed US military action remains in the background.

3. QatarEnergy has signed another major US LNG deal -- up to 3 mtpa for 20 years from Woodside’s Louisiana LNG project, starting with the project’s ramp from 2029. It follows the recent Cheniere agreement and reinforces QatarEnergy’s push to diversify supply outside the Gulf.

4. European gas #TTF briefly topped €100/MWh before easing back toward €97. The market remains tight heading into winter, while Germany is also locking in longer-term supply through a new Trafigura-SEFE arrangement.

5. China is opening the product-export valve further -- Beijing has reportedly issued another 5.7m tonnes of fuel-export quotas, taking 2026 allocations to their highest since 2021. More Chinese exports would offer some relief to still-tight global product markets.

6. Saudi Aramco raised LPG prices again -- November propane was set at $720/ton and butane at $780/ton, the fourth consecutive monthly increase.

7. Nigeria has sharply discounted Qua Iboe crude -- November pricing reportedly fell to around Dated Brent -14 cents/bbl, versus a premium above $4 in October, as freight economics weigh on West African competitiveness.

8. Bolivia is opening the door to gas imports -- a new decree allows companies to import natural gas and LNG for their own use or power generation as domestic production continues to decline. A striking reversal for a country that spent decades as a major regional gas exporter. #OOTT

text:
My Wife Asked Me to Stop Telling Her I Love Her, and the Reason Left Me Speechless.

Something happened in my marriage last week that I still don't know how to explain.

My wife and I have been married for four years. I'm not the most romantic man in the world, but I make an effort. I call her beautiful, tell her I love her before leaving for work, and try to make her feel wanted.

So imagine my surprise when she sat beside me one evening and said, Please, can you stop telling me you love me?

I laughed because I thought she was joking.

She wasn't.

I asked her what I had done wrong.

She said, Nothing. That is the problem. You keep telling me you love me, but I don't feel loved anymore.

I was confused.

I pay the bills. I come home after work. I don't cheat on her. Whenever she needs something, I try my best to provide it.

So I asked her what exactly she wanted from me.

She looked at me and said, You know my favourite food, but you don't know what I have been struggling with lately. You know when I need money, but you don't notice when I'm having a bad day. You kiss me before sleeping, but you haven't asked me how I have been feeling in weeks.

I didn't know what to say.

Then she told me something that hurt even more.

She said she had stopped telling me about certain things because whenever she tried, I would immediately start giving advice or explaining how she could solve the problem.

I don't always need you to fix everything, she said. Sometimes, I just want to talk to my husband and feel like he cares about what is happening inside my head.

I wanted to defend myself. I wanted to remind her of everything I had done for our family.

But as I sat there, I realised I could remember the last time I bought her something she needed. I could remember the last time we had sex. I could remember the last time we went out together.

What I couldn't remember was the last time I sat down and genuinely asked her how she was doing, then listened without checking my phone or trying to end the conversation.

That night, I didn't make any promises.

I simply asked her, Are you saying you don't feel loved by me anymore?

She held my hand and said, I know you love me. I am  just tired of having to convince myself that you still see me.

That sentence stayed with me.

The next morning, I made her breakfast and sat with her while she talked about something that had been bothering her at work. I didn't interrupt. I didn't offer solutions. I just listened.

Before I left, she kissed me and smiled.

It wasn't some magical moment that fixed our marriage. We still have things to work on.

But for the first time in a while, I understood that being a good husband wasn't only about what I could do for my wife. It was also about whether she felt she could be herself around me.

Now I am curious about something.

Men, when your woman says she doesn't feel loved, do you think she's overlooking everything you do for her, or could you be doing plenty for her while missing what she actually needs from you?

And women, what makes you feel loved beyond hearing the words I love you?

Comments by @ME_Beaumont 

ActionSA notes reports emanating from the City of Tshwane that its implicated Group Chief Financial Officer, Gareth Mnisi, left Tshwane House today accompanied by SARS officials following an operation involving search warrants at his office and residence.

This development is welcomed by ActionSA and serves as a timely reminder to the residents of Tshwane about what transpired during the disciplinary processes against Mnisi.

Mnisi’s return to work with merely a slap on the wrist in the wake of the damning evidence against him presented at the Madlanga Commission was entirely born of the actions and inactions of the ANC, EFF and DA.

The ANC and EFF were insistent that the charges against Mnisi should be deemed ‘minor in nature’ in order for them to result only in a warning, paving the way for his return to work in the City. This was in the face of serious findings against Mnisi from an independent forensic investigation. 

The ANC and EFF attempted to apply pressure on ActionSA to join them in this action, but ActionSA refused and voted in Council to classify the charges as serious in nature and warranting serious disciplinary action.

The DA, on the other hand, absented 19 of its councillors from Council on the day the matter was being addressed, citing party responsibilities as the reason for their absence. 

This was despite a previous Council meeting two weeks earlier setting up the Council meeting in question, leaving no ambiguity as to what it was about. After seven hours of the meeting, the DA attempted to withdraw their leave applications, and the Speaker refused – a decision that was later overturned in court as legally defective.

Unfortunately, the damage had been done. Under the applicable disciplinary regulations, a precautionary suspension automatically lapses if disciplinary proceedings have not commenced within three months. 

By voting to classify the allegations against Mnisi as minor in nature, rather than proceeding with serious disciplinary charges, Council failed to initiate the disciplinary proceedings necessary within that period. Consequently, Mnisi’s precautionary suspension lapsed, allowing him to return to work.
The DA may wish to claim its court victory, but nothing will change the fact that the disputed Council decision, which ultimately contributed to Mnisi’s return, would not have arisen in the same circumstances had its councillors done what they are paid to do and shown up for Council.

Why does this history matter? It offers a perspective on how political parties approach the work of accountability of implicated municipal officials. The ANC and EFF brazenly protect such officials for reasons South Africans can deduce, and the DA is too incompetent to give expression to its verbal stance against corruption.
This entire matter is now a timely reminder for the residents of Tshwane and beyond, because any further evidence or charges arising from the SARS investigation may provide grounds for the City of Tshwane to institute new disciplinary proceedings and address what failed before. 

The only question, between now and then, is what the numbers in Tshwane will look like arising from the local government elections next week.

If Tshwane residents who have previously voted ANC, EFF or DA want to see accountability for Mnisi, they need to make ActionSA the biggest party and return Nasiphi Moya to the mayoralty in our capital. If they want their city’s finances to be led by a financially implicated official, they should persist in their votes for the ANC, EFF or DA.
It is that simple.

text:
Amina found him on the fire escape again, knees drawn up, staring at the city like it owed him answers. She sat beside him without a word and passed him the last of her coffee. 

He took it, their fingers brushing the way they always did soft, automatic, still electric after three years. 
“They offered me the fellowship,” he said. 

“Two years in Nairobi, Real lab, real funding, the work I came here to do.”
She already knew. 

His advisor had called her that afternoon, half-congratulating, half-warning. 

Amina closed her eyes against the wind. 
“And I got the permanent contract at the clinic, the one with the loan forgiveness. The one that keeps my mother on her medication.”

They sat with it, below them traffic moved in steady lines. Somewhere a siren rose and faded.

“I love you,” Mason said,

 “I’ve loved you since the night you argued with me about water rights in that terrible bar. I still wake up and think about your laugh before I remember where I am.

”Amina turned her face into his shoulder. “I know, I love you like that too. Enough that I almost told them no.”

He went still. “Almost.”
 “Almost,” she repeated. “Then I thought about my mother’s hands. How they shake when the insurance runs out, and I thought about you in six months, hating the ceiling of this apartment because you stayed for me instead of the work that makes you make sense to yourself.”

Mason set the cup down, the metal grate pressed cold through their jeans. 
He wanted to promise he could do both fly back, split the years, invent a life that bent for both of them. The math had already failed every way they tried it.

“Sometimes it isn’t about wanting each other less,” he said quietly.

“I know.” Her voice cracked on the last word.

 “Sometimes the world just refuses to make room for the shape we make together.”

They stayed until the coffee went cold and the skyline blurred. 
When they finally stood, they didn’t kiss, they held on, hard, the way people hold the last thing they can still reach. 

Below them the city kept moving, indifferent to the fact that love, even the stubborn kind, could not stretch far enough to cover both of their necessary lives at once.

Supporting Rating-to-Officer Career Progression

A career at sea offers opportunities for professional growth and greater responsibilities. To encourage career advancement among rating seafarers, the Seamen’s Welfare Fund Society (SWFS) has introduced a scheme, effective from 1 January 2026, offering one-time financial assistance of ₹2,00,000 to eligible rating seafarers who obtain their first Indian Certificate of Competency (CoC) for Foreign-Going (FG) or Near Coastal Voyage (NCV) service and progress to officer-level positions.

Applications must be submitted in the prescribed format within 12 months of CoC issuance.

For detailed guidance, please refer to the relevant official circulars and orders issued by the Directorate General of Maritime Administration (DGMA) / Directorate General of Shipping (DGS):
- DGMA EAC Branch Circular No. 51 of 2026
- DGS Order No. 9 of 2024
- Merchant Shipping Notice No. 15 of 2024
- DGS Circular No. 26 of 2026

For queries or assistance, reach out through the 24×7 grievance redressal portal.

Your rank today does not have to define your destination tomorrow. Keep learning, keep progressing and build your future at sea.

The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) has launched three nationwide campaigns offering domestic flight discounts, transportation subsidies for organized tours, and special experiences for singles and solo travelers. Announced on October 29, the promotions are expected to generate at least 629 million baht in economic activity through early 2027, supporting TAT's tourism strategy, the Year of Transformation.

The first campaign, Fly Across Thailand, Heal Your Heart on Every Trip, offers a 500-baht discount on eligible domestic flights through seven airlines: Thai Airways, Thai AirAsia, Thai Vietjet, Bangkok Airways, Nok Air, Thai Lion Air, and Ezy Airlines. Travelers can use the promotional code FLYTODOM for bookings made through December 15, 2026, with travel permitted until January 15, 2027, subject to airline conditions.

The second campaign, Amazing Thailand: Explore Thailand with Organized Tours, provides transportation subsidies to eligible tour operators working with nine tourism organizations. Chartered buses carrying at least 30 tourists qualify for 10,000 baht per day, capped at 40,000 baht per trip, while vans carrying at least six tourists qualify for 2,500 baht per day, up to 10,000 baht per trip. Tours must last at least two days and one night, cross provincial boundaries, and include an overnight stay outside the departure province.

The third campaign, Single Journey 2026, features eight activities and 10 travel routes across Thailand's five regions for singles and solo travelers. Experiences include seaside movie screenings, underwater sound healing, nature excursions, train journeys, group runs, pet-friendly trips, coastal getaways, and coffee gatherings. Partners including https://t.co/CbUh2BFNwQ, Tinder, and Love Andaman will offer additional discounts and benefits, helping encourage domestic travel and support local tourism businesses.

Apollo Micro Systems Ltd - Q2 & H1 FY27 Concall Summary

Revenue Grew 72%;  Orderbook at ₹1,765 Cr expected to exceed ₹2k Cr by March;  MIGM, Pinaka and Torpedo Orders in the Pipeline;  FY27 Standalone Guidance of 35-45%, and Long-Term ₹25,000 Cr Revenue Ambition in Five Years 

1.  Financials

Consolidated Q2 revenue ₹388 Cr (+72% YoY); 
EBITDA ex other income ₹111 Cr (+88%), margin 29%; PAT ₹46 Cr (+40%)
Standalone Q2 revenue ₹306 Cr (+36% YoY); 
EBITDA ₹108 Cr (+82%), margin 35%; 
PAT ₹48 Cr (+46%)

Q2 margin rose on execution of production orders alongside development projects; management says quarterly margins vary with mix

2.  Milestones in the Quarter

CCI approved the Premier Explosives acquisition; the open offer follows (mgmt declined to comment further under the agreement)
Transfer of technology for a semi-active laser homing system was awarded

New group company for weapons and long-range systems, led by Dr VK Saraswat (Apollo holds ~33-34%); Apollo will produce what it develops
Ideal Explosives commissioned a 9,000 MT bulk silo near Asansol, with long-term coal subsidiary orders

3.  Orders & Programmes

Order book ₹1,765 Cr, standalone a little under ₹1,300 Cr; expected above ₹2,000 Cr by March, and ₹4,500-5,000 Cr by year end including MIGM
MIGM: quotation request expected next month; Navy wants to release the purchase order by Feb-Mar with a 20% advance; trials already done; Apollo is the sole source for its electronics

Pinaka rockets: 2,000-unit Army order negotiated and expected before December; 80 km range has three vendors, the 120 km production partner is not yet chosen
Heavyweight torpedoes: a 30-unit emergency order is expected in November (nine-month delivery); a larger 125-unit order later

QRSAM: MoD may split the first lot 50:50 between BDL and the private sector; Apollo supplies most onboard systems
100+ other programmes are under way; some cannot be disclosed

4.  Capacity & Subsidiaries

Unit 3 first phase operating; the full expansion (~12x present capacity) is due by March 2027; in-house EMI/EMC testing and calibration being installed to avoid weeks-long waits at DRDO labs
Ideal Explosives was loss-making; restructuring will take a couple more quarters, and Q2 was a lean off-season quarter
R&D ~8% of sales; large Ideal investment and 2,000 acres near Hyderabad planned

5.  Guidance

Standalone FY27 growth 35-45% (earlier guidance 45-50%; H1 was 29%)
Positive operating cash flow every quarter only from FY29 when production orders dominate
Group aspires to ₹25,000 Cr in five years; joint guidance after the Premier deal closes
Exports to start from next financial year; aims to be a global OEM in 5-6 years

6.  Key Risk

Order book rose only slightly QoQ; ordering delays on some programmes
Subsidiaries pull consolidated profit below standalone
Orders are lumpy and government-dependent

text:
I’m both sad and exhilarated about the Rays. It was an incredibly exciting season that was somewhat unexpected. The Rays were predicted to finish last in the division yet they not only won the East but advanced to the World Series, beating the rival Yankees along the way. The World Series didn’t go the way we wanted but it taught the Rays a lesson in how to build a champion. The Brewers were solid in all fronts and the Rays need to learn from them as they build upon what they already have — better bullpen, a healthy Shane, Simpson in leadoff. 

The Brewers fanbase also taught us in Tampa Bay what it means to be passionately connected to a franchise. While others around the nation — clowns like at @barstoolsports — will hate us for not always filling the Trop, they forget they have decades upon decades of a head start on us as a sports town. The “Brew Crew” that visited my bar were not only from Wisconsin but who traveled from states like Colorado, North Carolina, Texas, and New York who had been “lifelong fans who wouldn’t miss this for the world.” Some told me they paid over $5,000 to “experience something their grandparents never were able to.” Think about that: The Rays are a little pup of a franchise next to the baseball clubs that have had multiple generations grow up rooting for them.

In closing, I believe we will support the Rays even more so as the seasons mature, especially when they move to a new stadium. As much as I love the Trop and as much as I believe it has charm and encapsulates a grit having survived and recovered from a hurricane, the people of Tampa Bay will embrace a new stadium in Tampa. It will give people that shiny new car feel where people will be proud to show off. This is something else to think of: how many of y’all have your whole vibe change when you FINALLY trade that old reliable with the faded dash and torn seats in for a new ride with fresh leather and an elaborate console up front. You love taking it for a spin just to get milk and especially love offering to drive when you and your friends go out. That’s how the new stadium will be like. 

We forget to celebrate the good things anymore and just only care about winning but the 2026 iteration of the Rays was amazing this year. Let’s remember what 2026 had to offer: Junior Caminero rising to become a star, Chandler Simpson making a name for himself with his speed, Nick Martinez leading on and off the field, the new owners pushing the Rays new stadium across the finish line. Thank you @RaysBaseball for giving the region something incredible to root for, both today and for generations to come. #RaysUp

text:
Kissing a 10-Year-Old Not Enough to Prosecute? Questions Remain as Citywest Migrant Faces Deportation

On 23 October 2026, Dublin Circuit Criminal Court was told the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP) was withdrawing two sexual assault charges against a 27-year-old failed asylum seeker. The charges related to alleged incidents involving a 10-year-old girl near the Citywest IPAS centre in Saggart on 20 October 2025. 

Judge Martin Nolan ordered his release from remand and vacated the 2027 trial date. Within hours, he was rearrested by the Garda National Immigration Bureau under a May 2025 deportation order and remains in custody pending removal.

The girl was in Tusla care and had absconded during a recreational trip. When charged, the man reportedly told gardaí: “She sat beside me; you can check the CCTV. She started talking to me and I asked her her age, she told me she was 18. I just kissed her.”

His statement acknowledges kissing the child while claiming he believed she was an adult. The DPP has offered no public explanation for discontinuing the prosecution, and reports suggest considerable unhappiness within An Garda Síochána. The man has not been convicted, and the presumption of innocence remains. However, questions persist over whether any charge could have proceeded, even if more serious allegations could not be proved.

Tusla’s initial statement referred to the girl’s behavioural difficulties and her having absconded, prompting criticism that its wording risked victim-blaming. Its chief executive subsequently apologised. The episode has renewed concerns about the supervision and protection of vulnerable children in state care.

SnD Media covered the ensuing unrest at citywest last October (recap below), interviewing residents who expressed anger and fear about the incident, the child’s vulnerability and wider concerns surrounding the IPAS centre.

The case has also intensified debate about public warnings concerning sexual offending. Graham Carey, 42, from Finglas, received a two-year sentence, with the final year suspended, after being convicted of incitement to hatred over a 2023 livestream describing refugees as “rape-ugees”. Kirk Loco faces a charge concerning a June 2024 post about an international protection applicant allegedly exposing himself to a 14-year-old girl on a 133 bus. Loco is due to defend himself at Bray Court later today.

Other cases cited in the debate include Afghan nationals Ziaulhaq Safi, jailed for six years in 2026 for sexually assaulting a vulnerable 16-year-old in Sligo, and Akbar Moqadar, sentenced to an effective six years for the oral rape of a vulnerable woman.

Concerns extend beyond individual cases. Ruth Breslin has highlighted a recent High Court case involving the “horrifying” exploitation of a 14-year-old in Tusla care, warning that it was not isolated. Taoiseach Micheál Martin described the issue as “very serious and deeply worrying.”

Meanwhile, 24 Romanian men convicted of sexual offences and other crimes were deported on a single charter flight. Although Ireland’s non-Irish population is approximately 17 per cent, official statements caution against attributing crime trends to migration overall. That does not remove the need to explain specific protection failures or address public concerns about safety.

The child’s privacy must remain paramount. Nevertheless, the withdrawal of charges, the absence of a public explanation and the acknowledged shortcomings in protecting children in care leave serious questions unanswered.

When an adult admits kissing a 10-year-old irrespective of believing she was 18, should that admission be sufficient to pursue some form of charge if more serious allegations cannot be proved? Or if not,  does this set a dangerous precedent that 10-year-old girls are now fair game in Ireland?

⚠️ A WARNING THIS HALLOWEEN WEEKEND

As Halloween approaches here in Ireland, I want to share a warning, especially with anyone thinking of attending a tarot card reading, visiting a psychic or medium, having their fortune told, or taking part in séances or other occult practices.

Please do not mistake these things for harmless entertainment.

The Bible is very clear about witchcraft, divination, sorcery, consulting spirits and attempting to communicate with the dead.

Deuteronomy 18:10–12 specifically warns against these practices and describes them as an abomination to the Lord.

God does not give us these warnings without reason. As Christians, we are called to seek guidance from Him, not from mediums, spirits, tarot cards or fortune tellers.

And remember, something being popular, traditional or presented as entertainment does not mean it is pleasing to God.

“You shall be blameless before the LORD your God.” — Deuteronomy 18:13

This is not a message of condemnation. It is a message of love and warning. If you have participated in these things before, remember that Jesus Christ offers forgiveness and a new beginning to everyone who turns to Him.

You do not need a psychic to tell you your future when you can place your future in the hands of the One who created you.

This Halloween weekend, choose the light of Jesus Christ.

“I am the light of the world. He who follows Me shall not walk in darkness, but have the light of life.” — John 8:12

God bless you all. Stay safe, stay prayerful, and keep your eyes on Jesus.

👀 Today's horses we're following as we build towards Cheltenham 2027 and 2028.

🇫🇷 11:39 FONTAINEBLEAU | GRECIAN LIGHTNING
Finished second to Dino D'Or here earlier this month, with Don Dino just a head behind him in third. He now meets Yokozuna, who arrives with a runner-up finish in stronger Class 3 company. An interesting clash between two separate lines of French juvenile form.

🇫🇷 11:39 FONTAINEBLEAU | YOKOZUNA
Made much of the running in the Prix Richard d'Ayguevives before Le Brulhois caught him, finishing three lengths ahead. Nectar Des Dieux was another 14 lengths back in third. He returns to the same course and distance against Grecian Lightning, giving us a useful comparison.

🇫🇷 12:11 FONTAINEBLEAU | NO BED OF ROSES
Finished fourth behind It's Your Choice here on 3 October, beaten only a neck for third by Aquali Melody. That was her first appearance over hurdles after showing promise on the Flat. Today's fillies' contest offers another chance to put that opening effort into context.

🇬🇧 13:30 FFOS LAS | ARCADIAN STAR
His second at Leicester came on heavy ground, which makes today's conditions particularly interesting. He was still in contention when falling at Uttoxeter in March, so that run told us little about his finishing ability. This is a chance to revisit the Leicester form.

🇫🇷 13:47 BORDEAUX | AVAYA
Two hurdle victories from three starts make her one of the more accomplished juveniles on today's French programme. She now meets stablemate She Likestomove It in a Class 2 over 3,700 metres. Their contrasting experience should make this an informative race for the Lageneste and Macaire team.

🇫🇷 13:47 BORDEAUX | SHE LIKESTOMOVE IT
Won her second hurdle start in the spring after finishing fourth on debut. She returns against stablemate Avaya, who has already won twice. A particularly interesting comparison between a lightly raced filly returning from a break and one with more recent winning form.

🇬🇧 13:50 STRATFORD | RED METAL
Won over today's course and distance earlier this month and now carries a penalty. His experience makes him an important yardstick for Brecharnon, who arrives from bumpers. The result should help establish how much substance there is behind the newcomer's previous form.

🇬🇧 13:50 STRATFORD | BRECHARNON
Dan Skelton's bumper winner makes his hurdling debut against Red Metal, a recent winner over this very course and distance. Rather than facing a field of equally inexperienced newcomers, he has a proven hurdler to measure himself against immediately.

🇬🇧 14:00 FFOS LAS | PASSAGE GUENOT
Runner-up in an Irish point-to-point before joining Philip Hobbs and Johnson White. He makes his Rules debut over hurdles with Harry Cobden aboard and meets Kimai, a previous bumper winner. An interesting first look at how his point-to-point form translates to the racecourse.

🇬🇧 14:20 STRATFORD | FORTHFACTOR
Dan Skelton's Aintree Grade 2 bumper winner makes his hurdling debut. He beat Look Me by two and a half lengths in that 20-runner contest, with Merlin Allen third. Previously fifth behind Bass Hunter at Ascot, he brings a particularly useful bumper record into the novice-hurdling division.

The two British hurdling debuts and those French juvenile form comparisons are the races we'll be studying particularly closely today.

text:
Trump's plan to undermine the results of the midterm elections
Rebecca Crosby and Noel SimsOct 29Popular Information
Since President Trump entered national electoral politics in 2015, a core part of his political strategy has been undermining confidence in election results.
Before the 2016 election, for example, Trump posted on Twitter, “Of course there is large scale voter fraud happening on and before election day. Why do Republican leaders deny what is going on?” Trump has also repeatedly claimed that mail-in voting leads to rigged elections and that voter fraud by noncitizens is rampant.

This strategy allows Trump to either declare victory or, as with the 2020 election, declare the election was stolen.
The reality is that there is no evidence of widespread voter fraud in United States elections. Studies have also shown that noncitizen voting in the U.S. is “extremely rare.”

Nevertheless, when asked if he would respect the upcoming midterm election results regardless of the outcome, Trump responded, “I will, if they’re honest elections.”

Trump and Republicans seem particularly worried about a bad election result this year, as Republicans fight to retain control of both the House and the Senate. A recent PBS News/NPR/Marist poll found that “Democrats hold an 8-point lead among likely voters.” Trump’s approval rating has also plummeted. Earlier this month, Trump’s approval rating reached a record low of 31%, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll.

As a result, the Trump administration has made multiple moves to potentially cast doubt on the outcome of the midterm elections.

The Alaska lawsuit

Last week, Trump’s Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a lawsuit in federal court seeking to block certification of the results of a U.S. Senate election in Alaska if Democratic candidate Mary Peltola wins. The DOJ is taking issue with a Republican candidate, Daniel J. Sullivan, who shares the same name as the current Republican incumbent, who is also on the ballot. The DOJ’s lawsuit argues that “the sole purpose of his candidacy is to benefit the Peltola campaign.” The DOJ’s challenge was filed less than two weeks before the election.

Sullivan, a former teacher, has said that he is not running to confuse voters. The state has already made efforts to distinguish the two candidates on the ballot. For example, it lists Senator Dan Sullivan as a Republican incumbent, while the newcomer is listed without a party affiliation. Senator Sullivan is also listed as Dan, while his challenger is listed as Daniel. Each candidate is also listed with their middle initial. According to the AP, Alaska’s “Republican officials made the decisions about how to list him on the ballot.”

On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that operatives aligned with Peltola tried to recruit the new Sullivan to run. Peltola’s campaign has denied any involvement in the new Sullivan’s campaign. The Times reported that Peltola was “not directly involved,” but was “definitely aware.”

The results of the Alaska election could have a big impact on which party controls the Senate. The DOJ is asking that the results of the election not be certified if the incumbent Sullivan loses within a margin where he would have won with the inclusion of the votes for the other Sullivan.

Trump told reporters that he was the one that told the DOJ to file the lawsuit. Republicans attempted to remove the new Sullivan from the ballot earlier this year, but the efforts were rejected by the Alaska Supreme Court.

Experts have said that the DOJ’s lawsuit “has no merit.” A motion to dismiss the lawsuit was filed by lawyers for Peltola and Senate Democrats. The state has also asked the court to dismiss the lawsuit.

$1 million bounty

Trump is also encouraging people to come forward with claims of voter fraud. On Monday, Trump announced in a post on Truth Social that he would be offering a $1 million reward to people who successfully report voter fraud leading to an arrest and conviction. “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” Trump wrote.

Trump did not offer any additional information about the reward, including where the money for the rewards would come from.

Disqualifying tens of thousands of voters

Over the last year, the Trump administration has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia in an attempt to access their unredacted voter rolls and look for noncitizen voting. So far, the administration has lost in 27 of those cases — most recently in Utah, where the state’s Republican lieutenant governor has resisted sharing voter data.

Despite these losses, the Trump administration has continued to claim it identified noncitizen voters in some states. Over the summer, the administration told Nevada it found up to 16,000 noncitizens on the state voter rolls. A month later, the administration revised that number down to just 185. When Nevada officials looked into those voters, they found that all of them were citizens.

Earlier this month, the DOJ made similar claims in California, saying it had identified 20,000 noncitizen voters. The DOJ gave California election officials 48 hours to review the names, and when they refused, Trump threatened them with jail time. He wrote on social media that the officials “will all go to jail for a long period of time!!!” The Trump administration sued the state, demanding that a federal court prevent the state from counting the ballots of those voters. An appeals court ruled against the Trump administration on Monday.

Late last week, Attorney General Todd Blanche told reporters the DOJ was considering bringing similar cases against other states. “There’s a number of states that we’re looking at,” he said. On Monday, the DOJ asked the state of Washington to set aside the ballots of 400 voters it claims are noncitizens.

Threatening local election officials

Over the summer, the DOJ sent letters to election officials in all 50 states and Washington, D.C., warning that they “could face criminal charges for allowing noncitizens to remain on their lists of eligible voters.” The letters were sent by Harmeet Dhillon, who heads the DOJ’s Civil Rights Division.

“Any election officer, including the chief election officer of the state, who knowingly retains noncitizens on the state’s SVRL [state voter registration list] or facilitates noncitizens in receiving and casting ballots could be subject to criminal liability,” one letter said, according to Reuters.

The letters gave state election officials five days to say how they would comply with federal voter laws.

Filling the Department of Justice with election deniers

Trump has also stacked his administration with election deniers who could potentially validate conspiracies about election results. During the 2020 election, for example, Dhillon pushed for donations to Trump’s legal defense fund. “We’re waiting for the United States Supreme Court, of which the president has nominated three justices, to step in and do something,” Dhillon said in an interview on Fox Business after the election, Democracy Docket reported.

In August 2025, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) appointed election conspiracy theorist Heather Honey as Deputy Assistant Secretary for Election Integrity. After the 2020 election, Honey falsely claimed that she had discovered that, in Pennsylvania, more votes were reported than voters. Trump cited the false claim to justify his denial of the election results, and repeated the claim to the crowd on January 6, 2021.

Eric Neff, the acting chief of the Voting Section at the DOJ, was formerly a Los Angeles County prosecutor, and “was put on administrative leave in 2022 after he based a prosecution around tips from a right-wing group that has promoted election fraud conspiracy theories,” Mother Jones reported.

Gutting election security

The second Trump administration has also made major cuts to the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), which provides states with support for election security efforts. According to September reporting by the AP, the Trump administration “cut some 1,000 employees from CISA and slashed $10 million from two cybersecurity initiatives, including one dedicated to helping state and local election officials.”

The agency, which was created during the first Trump administration, did not release an election infrastructure security plan until 40 days before the midterms this year. Election officials in multiple states have said that the agency “provided them no assistance — and no explanation for its absence — during the most critical planning stages for the upcoming midterms,” ProPublica reported.

You must have heard about the soccer star kid who was unceremoniously walked out of a youth league in Winter Park, Florida by the police because he held the ball for too long.

If you’ve never heard or known that excellence can be a threat, this 3-year-old boy’s experience will teach you that. Being too good can be a threat to others.

But that’s not why I’m making this post.

I’m here to show you how pushing the right narrative (the one that favours you) and documenting your process when nobody is watching might be all you need to succeed in life and in business.

At 8 months, Nevada started walking and by the time he was 10 months old, he could fully dribble with football.

And at the age of 3, he made it into the global news. From the United States to Canada, from Canada to Europe and from Europe to Africa, everyone had something to say about him.

When he started trending, we all went back to watch his old videos.

His old content pointed to the fact that he didn’t start today. He had a track record.

But beyond that, when they tried to bully him, his parents pushed the “right” narrative that ended in his favour.

Imagine for a moment his mom didn’t record what happened.

Imagine for a moment he didn’t have any social media presence.

Jay-Z, Ye and 50cent wouldn’t have noticed and supported him.

ROC Nation Sports, owned by Jay-Z, wouldn’t have thrown their full support behind his football career.

Eddie Johnson wouldn’t have offered to be his personal coach.

He wouldn’t have raised $55,706 to support his career when his target was to raise $30,000.

Almost all top American content creators, especially the ones from the black community are fully in support of him.

All these things wouldn’t have happened if he didn’t:

*  Have an online presence 

*  Push the narrative that favours his brand

* Show his track record by documenting his training 

Don’t just sit around waiting for spotlight.

When nobody is clapping yet, focus on building your capacity.

Create content about what you do.

Blow your own trumpet 🎺 

And respond to any form of bully with a narrative that will favour you.
 
Indeed, God can use anything to bring the diligent into spotlight.

I hope this helps you.

A 3-year-old boy went to play football. He left with the whole world talking about him.

Nevada Pierre was playing against older children in Florida when a dispute broke out at a youth football match. 

His parents alleged he was being restricted because he was too good.

League officials offered a different explanation, raising concerns about the conduct of the adults involved.

Then someone called the police.

Videos of the incident went viral. People took sides. Former US footballer Eddie Johnson offered to train him, and Roc Nation Sports reportedly arranged a football development trip to Spain.

Gofund me raised $42,000 for him. 

One football match. 
One police call. 
Global attention. 
New opportunities.

It’s a reminder of how quickly life can change when the world notices you.

The goal now shouldn’t be give him the space and support to develop his talent and enjoy being a child.

text:
$IONQ New Mexico awards IonQ $160,951 to hire 3 trainees

On October 22, Economic Development New Mexico announced more than $12 million in job training grants for the quarter. IonQ, in Albuquerque, was awarded $160,951 in August for 3 trainees at an average hourly wage of $93. The state describes IonQ as focused on quantum computing, quantum networking and quantum sensing to support applications across national security, finance, healthcare, cybersecurity, logistics, materials science, aerospace and other high-impact sectors.

The state's Job Training Incentive Program reimburses a minimum of 50% of trainee wages for up to six months, for new full-time hires. Among the 33 companies funded this quarter, only Particle Labs had a higher average wage, at $96 an hour. Boeing's was $63.

IonQ is hiring more people in the state. Two Staff Scientists in Quantum Applications (Defense), who must reside in New Mexico, will be founding members of IonQ's new Customer Solutions team and build quantum algorithms for defense missions with national labs, government and industry. A Senior Staff Quantum Physicist, based in Albuquerque or Boulder, will work hands-on with IonQ's current hardware.

On September 29, IonQ was named among the first tenants of the Roadrunner Quantum Lab, a 35,000 square foot facility in Albuquerque's Innovation District and the anchor of the state's $450M commitment to quantum. Scott Millard, Chief Business Officer of IonQ: "IonQ is excited to deepen our presence in New Mexico."

New Mexico also offers matching grants of at least $1M to companies that perform their DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage C work in the state. IonQ is on DARPA's Stage C list. No application by IonQ has been announced.

On August 4, IonQ signed an MOU with Sandia National Laboratories to explore quantum co-design for national security at New Mexico's Quantum Demonstration Facility. Sandia and Los Alamos will help stand up and operate that facility at the Roadrunner Quantum Lab. IonQ plans to use both to support collaboration with the state's national laboratories, universities and research institutions.
