text:
A fox screams, and the internet goes quiet.
Not barks. Not yips. Screams. The kind of sound that makes you check whether a person is in trouble. The kind of sound that makes grown adults stop mid-scroll, turn the volume up, then immediately regret it.
I'm not going to tell you what happens in this video. That's the point.
Press play first. Then come back. Because what you're about to read will change how you see the animal on your screen, and I need you to feel the video before you understand it.
I'll be here. Go.
. . .
Still here? Good. Or you skipped ahead. Fine. Either way, you're about to find out why one small orange animal manages to wreck millions of people emotionally in under two minutes.
Let's start with the thing nobody tells you about foxes.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
1/ THE ANIMAL YOU THINK YOU KNOW IS NOT THE ANIMAL YOU KNOW
You think a fox is a cartoon. A sly trickster. A fluffy dog with better PR.
It's none of those things.
A red fox is a 10-to-15 pound predator with hollow bones, a nervous system wired like a hair trigger, and senses that make most of our technology look like a toy. It lives on every continent except Antarctica. It survives in forests, deserts, farmland, suburbs, and the middle of major capital cities. It eats beetles, berries, rabbits, birds, garbage, and whatever else the day offers.
It is, quite literally, one of the most successful mammals on Earth.
And it is built around one rule: never get caught.
Every muscle, every instinct, every reflex in that body exists to avoid one scenario. Being held. Being stuck. Being unable to move.
Keep that in your head. Because the entire video is about what happens when that rule fails.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
2/ A FOX CAN HEAR A MOUSE SQUEAK FROM ABOUT 100 YARDS AWAY
Read that again.
A mouse. Squeaking. Across a football field. Through grass.
Fox ears are enormous for a reason. They rotate independently, they funnel sound like satellite dishes, and they are especially sensitive to low-frequency noise, like the rustle of a rodent moving under snow or soil.
A fox can pinpoint a mouse under a foot of snow by sound alone, then leap high into the air and dive nose-first into the white to catch it.
This is an animal that lives inside an ocean of sound. Everything it knows about the world comes through those ears.
Now imagine what it does to that animal when the loudest thing in its world is its own fear.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
3/ FOXES MAY HUNT USING THE EARTH'S MAGNETIC FIELD
This one sounds fake. It isn't.
Researchers studying red foxes noticed something strange. When foxes pounced on hidden prey, they didn't jump randomly. They tended to leap in a north-easterly direction. And when they did, their success rate was dramatically higher. In the data, they hit their target about three quarters of the time when pouncing toward the north-east, and far less when they didn't.
The working theory: foxes can perceive the planet's magnetic field and use it like a rangefinder, a kind of invisible crosshair laid over their vision.
Think about that.
This is not a pet. Not a mascot. Not a meme. This is an animal that may literally see magnetism and uses it to calculate the perfect jump.
And there are situations where no amount of calculation matters.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
4/ THE FOX HAS ABOUT 40 DIFFERENT SOUNDS. ONE OF THEM IS THE REASON PEOPLE CALL THE POLICE.
Foxes are surprisingly vocal. Researchers have catalogued roughly 40 distinct vocalizations in red foxes: barks, whines, growls, yelps, a strange chattering laugh used during play, and a greeting call between mates.
But there's one sound that sits at the very top of the list.
The scream.
It's long, raspy, and disturbingly human. Every winter, in cities and villages across the world, people wake up at 2 a.m. convinced someone is being attacked outside their window. They call emergency services. Officers show up with flashlights and find nothing but a fox sitting in a hedge, looking mildly offended.
The scream is part of breeding season communication. It carries across huge distances. It's designed to be impossible to ignore.
Now here's what almost nobody knows: that's the happy version of the sound.
The distress version is different.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
5/ THERE IS A DIFFERENCE BETWEEN A SOUND AN ANIMAL MAKES AND A SOUND AN ANIMAL CAN'T HOLD BACK
Most wild animals do everything possible to stay silent when hurt.
Pain is weakness. Weakness is advertising. Predators listen.
A wounded animal that screams is a wounded animal that is about to be found. So evolution trained these creatures to suffer quietly. To freeze. To hide. To endure.
When a wild animal makes noise anyway, when it breaks that ancient rule, it means something has gone past the point of strategy. It means the fear has overridden the instinct to survive quietly.
In other words: when a fox cries out loud, it is out of options.
That is what makes the sound so hard to listen to. It isn't just loud. It's a confession.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
6/ A SHORT HISTORY OF THE MOST DANGEROUS FENCE EVER INVENTED
In 1874, an Illinois farmer named Joseph Glidden patented a simple idea: twist two strands of wire together and lock sharp barbs between them.
It was cheap. It was fast to build. It worked on cattle.
Within a few years it had spread across the American West and then across the world. People called it "the devil's rope." It ended the era of the open range. It reshaped borders, farms, wars, and entire economies.
And it did something else, quietly, for the next 150 years.
It turned countless landscapes into traps that animals were never evolved to understand.
A fox can read a forest. It can read a river. It can read the shadow of a hawk from half a mile away.
But thin metal, in the wrong light, at the wrong height, is a language it was never taught.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
7/ WILDLIFE RESCUERS HAVE A NAME FOR THIS SITUATION. THEY DON'T SAY IT OUT LOUD ON THE JOB.
Ask people who work in animal rescue what they dread most, and a surprising number give the same answer.
Not snakes. Not rabid-looking animals. Not floods.
Entanglement.
Because an entangled animal is the most dangerous patient in the world. It is terrified, it is in pain, it cannot flee, and every instinct it has tells it that the thing approaching is the end.
A calm, trusting animal can be helped in minutes.
A panicked wild animal with a mouth full of teeth, claws made for digging, and the adrenaline of a creature fighting for its life can hurt a rescuer badly. And it can hurt itself even worse by thrashing, because the more it struggles, the tighter everything gets.
That is the cruel math of being trapped: the instinct to fight is the thing that makes it worse.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
8/ THE SMARTEST WILD ANIMAL IN THE WORLD STILL CAN'T SOLVE ONE PROBLEM
Foxes are famous for intelligence. They open latches. They learn routines. They figure out garbage cans, bird feeders, and suburban schedules. In some cities they've learned to wait at crosswalks.
But intelligence has a limit when the problem is physical and the clock is running.
A fox can't call anyone. It can't explain itself. It can't understand that the shape approaching is trying to help.
It can only run the one program it has: escape.
So every rescue like this comes down to a single impossible question.
How do you convince a wild animal that you are not what it thinks you are?
You can't. Not with words. Not with patience alone. Not with good intentions.
You have to do something else.
I won't spoil what.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
9/ THE RUSSIAN EXPERIMENT THAT TURNED FOXES INTO DOGS
Here's a story that sounds like science fiction.
In 1959, a Soviet geneticist named Dmitri Belyaev began breeding silver foxes on a Siberian fur farm. His rule was simple. Out of every generation, he picked only the foxes that were least afraid of humans. Nothing else. Not size. Not color. Just tameness.
Within a handful of generations, something strange started happening.
The foxes began wagging their tails. They began licking hands. Their ears went floppy. Their coats developed patches. Their faces got rounder. They started whining for attention.
They were becoming dogs, in real time, in a single human lifetime, simply because fear was removed from the equation.
The lesson is staggering: the wall between a wild animal and a loving one is not intelligence, or species, or destiny.
It's fear.
That's it. That one emotion.
And in the video you're about to watch, fear is the only thing standing between a fox and a second chance.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
10/ WHY YOUR BRAIN CAN'T LOOK AWAY
There's a reason these videos get tens of millions of views. It isn't random. It's biology.
Humans are wired for what psychologists call empathic distress. When we see a creature in trouble, especially one that cries out, our brains light up regions linked to our own pain. Mirror neurons fire. Heart rate rises. Attention narrows.
We don't watch because we want to suffer.
We watch because some ancient part of us has decided that this situation is unfinished, and it will not release us until it knows how it ends.
This is called the Zeigarnik effect: the mind obsesses over incomplete tasks and unresolved situations far more than finished ones.
A trapped animal is the ultimate open loop.
You can't scroll past it. Your brain keeps the tab open.
So if you've ever seen a clip like this and thought about it three days later in the shower, that's why.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
11/ THE THING ABOUT SOUND
Watch this video on mute and it's one thing.
Watch it with sound and it's a completely different experience.
Because sound bypasses the part of your brain that analyzes. Sound goes straight to the part that reacts. A crying animal doesn't register as information. It registers as an emergency.
That's why film directors cut the music at the most intense moments. That's why horror relies on silence. That's why a single cry can hit harder than a thousand words.
So here's my advice.
Headphones in. Volume up. Alone if you can.
I'm serious. This is not a clip to half-watch while doing something else.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
12/ THE MOST UNDERRATED MOMENT IN ANY ANIMAL RESCUE
Everyone remembers the ending. The release. The animal running free.
But people who have done this work for years will tell you the real moment, the one that actually matters, happens earlier.
It's the moment the animal stops fighting.
Not because it's weak. Not because it's given up.
Because something has changed.
It's incredibly subtle. A breath. A shift in the eyes. A body that has been rigid for hours suddenly loosening by one degree.
And if you know how to look for it, you can see the exact second when terror turns into something that looks, impossibly, like trust.
Watch for it.
If you miss it, you've missed the whole video.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
13/ A FOX'S TAIL IS NOT A TAIL. IT'S A TOOL.
The bushy tail of a fox, called a brush, does about five jobs at once.
It works as a balance pole when the animal runs and turns at full speed. It works as a blanket in winter, wrapped around the nose and paws to hold in heat. It works as a signal flag, communicating mood to other foxes. It works as a rudder when leaping. It even helps carry scent.
And when an animal is in real trouble, it also tells you something.
The tail goes still.
A fox with a relaxed tail is a fox that feels safe. A fox with a tucked, frozen tail is a fox that thinks the world is ending.
Hold onto that detail. It becomes important later.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
14/ THE FOX FACT THAT SHOULD EMBARRASS EVERY HUMAN
A fox can jump a fence taller than a grown man. It can squeeze through gaps smaller than your head. It can cover miles at 30 miles per hour. It can climb. It can swim. It can survive on almost nothing.
This is an escape artist built over millions of years.
And yet.
A few strands of rusty wire, built by humans in a few minutes, can stop all of it.
There's an uncomfortable truth hiding in that.
We design a world with traps in it and then act surprised when wildlife walks into them. Fences, netting, litter, plastic rings, fishing line. Our world is full of invisible hazards that nature never prepared anyone for.
Every rescue video is, in a sense, a small repair of a mistake we made without noticing.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
15/ WHAT HAPPENS TO A WILD ANIMAL'S BODY IN A TRAP
This part is hard to read, but it matters.
When a wild animal is trapped, its body floods with stress hormones. Heart rate skyrockets. Breathing becomes shallow and fast. Muscles lock. The animal burns through energy at a terrifying rate.
In extreme cases, the stress alone can be dangerous. Wildlife veterinarians have a name for a related condition, capture myopathy, where the muscle damage and metabolic chaos from intense fear and struggle can cause serious harm, even after the animal is freed.
In other words: time matters.
Every minute stuck is a minute the body pays for.
So when you see someone move toward a trapped animal, and they do it slowly, quietly, with almost ridiculous calm, it isn't because they're not in a hurry.
It's because slow is the fastest way to help.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
16/ THE RESCUER'S PARADOX
Here is the strangest rule in wildlife rescue.
To save an animal that is screaming at you, you must become quiet.
You lower your voice. You lower your body. You avoid eye contact, because a direct stare reads as a threat in nearly every predator species on Earth. You move like the air is made of glass.
In a situation where adrenaline tells every human instinct to rush, the right move is to slow down until you're almost motionless.
It feels wrong.
It works.
The people who do this well all say the same thing: the animal is reading you far better than you're reading it. Your breathing. Your hands. Your confidence. Your fear.
You cannot fake calm in front of an animal.
You have to actually have it.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
17/ A BRIEF LIST OF THINGS YOU DO NOT KNOW ABOUT FOXES
Quick-fire round, because you deserve a break from the heavy stuff.
• Foxes have vertical, cat-like pupils, which is unusual among canines and helps them see well in low light. • Their whiskers aren't only on the face. They also have sensitive whiskers on the backs of their front legs. • They cache food, burying surplus meals in dozens of tiny hiding spots, and can remember where they put them. • Fox kits are born nearly black and gradually turn red as they grow. • Foxes are among the few canines that can partially retract their claws, which helps with climbing and stealth. • Their urine and scent marks carry coded information about who passed by, how recently, and in what condition. • In the wild, a red fox often lives only two to three years. In protected conditions, it can live over a decade.
That last one is the one to remember.
Because the gap between three years and thirteen years is often just one moment where someone showed up.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
18/ THE MOMENT YOU REALIZE YOU'RE HOLDING YOUR BREATH
Here's a test.
When you press play on this video, pay attention to your body.
Around a certain point, your shoulders will rise. Your jaw will tighten. Your breathing will get shallow without you deciding it.
You'll lean toward the screen.
You'll hear yourself say "come on" under your breath, to nobody, to an animal that can't hear you, to a stranger on a video recorded who knows where, who knows when.
That's not weakness. That's the most human reflex there is.
We are a species that evolved by caring about things that weren't us.
Every empathy circuit in your head is thousands of years of cooperation encoded in neurons.
And right now, it's about to be used on a fox.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
19/ WHY THESE VIDEOS HIT HARDER THAN MOST MOVIES
A film can make you cry with music, lighting, actors, a script, and a budget.
A rescue video has none of that.
No script. No score. No second take. No guarantee of a happy ending.
That's exactly why it works.
We've all developed a built-in detector for staged emotion. We can smell manufactured drama from a mile away. But raw, unplanned, uncontrolled reality disarms that filter completely.
Because when something is real, there's a possibility that it might not turn out okay.
And that possibility is the whole thing.
The tension isn't written. It's lived.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
20/ THE QUIET HEROES NOBODY WRITES ABOUT
Somewhere out there, right now, there's a person with a phone in one hand and a pair of gloves in the other, standing in a field at an inconvenient hour, deciding whether to get involved.
Nobody is paying them. Nobody is watching. There's no medal.
They could keep walking. Most people do.
They don't.
Wildlife rescue is built almost entirely on strangers who decided that a creature they will never see again was worth getting scratched, bitten, muddy, late, and exhausted.
That's not a small thing.
In a world where headlines tell us we're getting worse, these videos are evidence for the other side of the argument.
Look closely at what people do when nobody is asking them to.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
21/ IF YOU EVER FIND AN ANIMAL IN THIS SITUATION
Because one day you might.
The golden rules, in plain language:
• Do not rush in. Panic spreads from you to the animal in seconds. • Do not grab a wild animal with bare hands. A terrified fox can bite, and wildlife carries disease. • Call a local wildlife rescue organization, animal control, or a veterinarian who handles wildlife. They have the tools, the training, and often the legal authority. • Keep your distance, keep noise low, keep other people and pets away. • Take note of the exact location so help can find it. • If you must act and no help is available, protect your hands, move slowly, and never put your face near the animal.
Good intentions are not enough on their own. Good intentions plus the right method save lives.
Save this post. You may need it one day.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
22/ THE UGLY NUMBER BEHIND ALL OF THIS
Wildlife organizations around the world report huge numbers of animals injured by human-made hazards every year: fencing, netting, traffic, litter, discarded fishing gear.
The real count is unknowable. Most injured wild animals are never seen. They don't make videos. They don't get rescued. They don't have a person who stopped.
So every clip that does exist represents a tiny fraction of the story.
For each fox that gets filmed, how many never got found?
The honest answer is: far, far more.
Which means the video you're about to watch isn't just a rescue. It's a rare window into something that happens constantly, in the dark, without witnesses.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
23/ I'VE WATCHED THIS TYPE OF VIDEO HUNDREDS OF TIMES. HERE IS THE PATTERN.
There's a structure to every great rescue clip, and once you notice it, you can't unsee it.
Act one: the sound. Something is wrong, and you feel it before you understand it.
Act two: the standoff. Fear against kindness. Two creatures who don't speak the same language trying to figure each other out.
Act three: the turn. A tiny moment where everything shifts.
Act four: the release.
And then there's the part nobody plans, the part that makes people replay the video five, ten, twenty times.
The last second.
The fox does one thing at the very end.
I'm not telling you what.
But when you see it, you'll understand why this clip didn't stay in one corner of the internet.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
24/ A SMALL EXPERIMENT FOR YOU
Watch the video once, completely, from the beginning to the end.
Then pay attention to how you feel afterwards.
Not the sadness. Not the relief. Something underneath those.
The feeling that, just for a moment, the world was a little more sane than you thought it was.
That feeling has a name. Researchers call it "elevation," the warm, uplifting emotion we get when we witness unexpected goodness in others. Studies suggest it makes people more likely to be generous, to help strangers, and to treat the people around them better, for hours afterward.
Watching kindness doesn't just make you feel good.
It makes you kinder.
So in a very real sense, this video is not entertainment.
It's a small dose of something the internet badly needs.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
25/ WHAT THE FOX WILL NEVER KNOW
Here's what I can't stop thinking about.
The fox has no idea this video exists.
It doesn't know that millions of strangers watched it. It doesn't know that people cried. It doesn't know that a stranger's phone recorded the most frightening hour of its life and turned it into a story that crossed oceans.
It just knows that one day the world was terrifying, and then, somehow, it wasn't.
And then it ran.
That's the whole story, really. The rest is just how we choose to feel about it.
So here's mine.
I hope every animal that ever screamed in the dark gets someone like that.
I hope more of us become that someone.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
26/ NOW. THE ONLY QUESTION LEFT.
You've read 25 thousand characters about a fox.
You know what its ears can do. You know what its scream means. You know why it's afraid, why it fights, and why the quietest person in the field is usually the one who wins.
You know everything except the one thing that matters.
What happened.
Scroll up. Press play. Turn the sound on.
Don't skip. Don't speed it up. Don't read the comments first. Don't look at the replies.
Give it two minutes.
Then come back and tell me I was wrong about the ending.
I dare you.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
If this made you feel something:
→ Repost it so someone else gets to feel it too. → Reply with the exact moment that got you. → Follow for more stories from the wild side of the internet, the ones that remind you why people are still worth believing in.
And if you ever find a trapped animal, be the one who stops.
The fox in this video got lucky.
Let's make luck less necessary.

text:
Good Thursday morning, friends! ☀️

“I delight greatly in the LORD; my soul rejoices in my God. For he has clothed me with garments of salvation and arrayed me in a robe of his righteousness, as a bridegroom adorns his head like a priest, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.”  Isaiah 61:10 (NIV)🙏

As we welcome another Thursday morning, I want to share a beautiful reminder of just how much we have to be thankful for.

Sometimes we get so caught up in the everyday responsibilities of life that we forget to stop and appreciate the greatest gift we've ever been given: God's love and the salvation He offers us through Jesus Christ.

We wake up thinking about everything that needs to be done. There are appointments to keep, bills to pay, chores waiting for us, and people we love who may be going through difficult times.

Before we know it, our minds are filled with worries about the day ahead.

But Isaiah 61:10 invites us to turn our attention toward something far greater than our daily concerns.

It reminds us that we have a reason to rejoice simply because we belong to God.

Think about the beautiful picture this verse gives us. God doesn't just offer us a little encouragement or temporary comfort. Through His grace, He clothes us with salvation and covers us with His righteousness.

Not because we've earned it or because we've lived perfect lives, but because of His incredible love and mercy.

And isn't that something worth celebrating?

We all make mistakes. We have days when our patience runs thin, when we say something we wish we hadn't, or when we feel like we've fallen short of the person God wants us to be.

But God's love isn't reserved for people who never stumble.

He knows our weaknesses, understands our struggles, and still invites us to come to Him with open hearts.

Through Jesus Christ, we can receive forgiveness, find a fresh beginning, and live with the wonderful assurance that our hope rests in Him.

That's a joy the world cannot give us, and it's a joy that difficult circumstances cannot take away.

Now, that doesn't mean every morning will feel joyful. Some of us wake up facing pain, loneliness, disappointment, or worries that have followed us through the night.

And sometimes just getting out of bed and facing another day requires more strength than anyone realizes.

If that's where you are this morning, please remember that you don't have to manufacture happiness or pretend everything is wonderful.

You can bring your worries, your sadness, and your tired heart to God.

His love is still there. His grace is still sufficient. And His promises are still true.

So before this Thursday gets too busy, take a moment to thank Him for what He has already done in your life.

Thank Him for the prayers He's answered, the difficult seasons He's carried you through, and the blessings you might have overlooked along the way.

And most of all, thank Him for the gift of salvation through His Son.

We may not have everything we want in this life, but in Christ, we have a reason to rejoice that goes far beyond anything this world can offer. 

Let's pray: 🙏

Heavenly Father, thank You for the gift of another morning and another opportunity to experience Your love, mercy, and goodness.

Lord, today we rejoice in You. Not because our lives are perfect or because every problem has been solved, but because You are faithful, and Your love never fails.

Thank You for sending Your Son, Jesus Christ, to make a way for us to receive forgiveness and salvation. Thank You for the grace we could never earn and the hope we could never find on our own.

Father, help us never take that precious gift for granted.

As we begin this Thursday, please fill our hearts with gratitude. Help us see beyond our worries and responsibilities long enough to recognize the blessings You have placed in our lives.

Lord, I pray for everyone who woke up this morning carrying a heavy burden.

Please bring healing and comfort to those who are sick, recovering from surgery, struggling with chronic pain, or waiting for medical answers. Give wisdom to their doctors and strength to their families.

Be especially close to those in hospitals, nursing homes, and hospice care. Ease their suffering, calm their fears, and surround them with Your peace.

Father, comfort those who are grieving. For anyone facing another morning without someone they dearly love, please bring comfort to their hearts and remind them that they are never alone.

I pray for those who are struggling financially, worrying about their jobs, or trying to make ends meet. Please provide for their needs, guide their decisions, and open doors where opportunities seem impossible.

Lord, watch over our children and grandchildren. Protect them wherever they go today, surround them with good influences, and help them make choices that lead them toward a better future.

Bring healing to families experiencing conflict or separation. Soften hardened hearts, restore understanding where possible, and help us show one another patience, kindness, and forgiveness.

Father, bless the caregivers who spend their days looking after others. Give them renewed strength when they're exhausted and encouragement when their responsibilities feel overwhelming.

Please remember those who feel forgotten, lonely, or discouraged. Let someone cross their path today who offers a kind word, a helping hand, or a reminder that they matter.

And Lord, help each of us become that person for someone else.

Teach us to be more patient, more compassionate, and more grateful. Help us speak words that encourage rather than discourage, and show love even when life becomes frustrating.

When we make mistakes, remind us of Your forgiveness. When we become discouraged, renew our hope. And when we begin to worry about tomorrow, help us trust You with the things we cannot control.

May we never forget that our greatest blessing isn't something we can buy, earn, or accomplish. It is the salvation and everlasting hope we have through Jesus Christ.

Guide our steps throughout this Thursday. Protect our families, bless the work of our hands, and help us find joy in the simple moments of the day.

Thank You for loving us, forgiving us, and giving us so many reasons to rejoice.

In Jesus precious name, Amen. 🙏

I hope this Thursday brings you moments of peace, unexpected blessings, and plenty of reasons to smile. Whatever the day holds, remember how deeply you are loved by the One who created you.

Peace and grace to you. 
Coffee first, and then the gym. ☕💪

text:
GROK BOT HOW TO USE
Sources: official Grok Bot docs + Cursor help + your Grok Bot bookmark folder (1090 posts)
Updated: 2026-10-29

WHAT NEW TODAY
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 27): Version 0.78.0 — a permissions panel to review what your Bot can use, add or remove marketplace apps instantly, connect plugins from the Mac header, pay with Stripe Link (and Shop Pay); in progress: pop-out chat windows on Mac, Mail drafting through Apple apps, a Tasks page, and sharing Bots with teammates
- Testers (firesidealpha, Oct 27): investor Gavin Baker calls Grok Bot the most impactful AI product he and his firm have had yet, says it is far easier than gluing tools together himself, and is up to 17 Bots
- Testers (XFreeze, Oct 27): import your memories from other assistants (preferences, instructions, writing style, personal context) instead of starting from scratch
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 25): praise for Grok Bot keeps coming from all sides; he calls it the most popular agent system right now
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 25): Version 0.75.5 — Vault lets Bots securely store and use your logins, payment cards and contact info; email forwarding keeps formatting, images and attachments; smarter Auto-review with fewer needless approvals; routines can run up to 300 times an hour in total (200 per routine); connecting X also connects X Money; Bots record who asked for each Slack message
- Official Elon (Oct 25): Grok Bot can now call a person or business for you, make a request on your behalf, take notes on the answer and send you a summary
- Testers (distortgeekin, Oct 25): on your phone Grok Bot can run Calendar, Reminders, Contacts and the Home app on iOS and Android; put it on the Action Button and set standing routines once
- Testers (techandsundry, Oct 3): Elon showed up at their Grok Bot event
- Testers (Michael_Fenech_, Oct 3): run a monthly human-dependency audit. Ask your chief-of-staff Bot to review the last 30 days and find every place work waited on you
- Testers (kocer_eth, Oct 2): bill-audit Bot. Harper's CEO says a Grok Bot built in 24 hours helped save customers $120,000+ on insurance policies; adapt it for your own bills
- SpaceXAI (poteto, Oct 2): the team dogfoods Grok Bot daily and uses it to build Grok Bot; expect it to keep getting better, faster and more capable
- Official bot / Testers (XFreeze, Oct 2): usage limits were reset for all Grok Bot users
- Official Elon (Oct 1): Try Grok Bot!

WHAT IT IS
- Testers (GrokBotRadar, Oct 5): the chat thinks with Grok, while coding work can go to Cursor Cloud Agents running the models Cursor offers; easy enough that his wife and dad run it from their phones
- Testers (Texas_Twins_Dad, Oct 4): one-month review. Much faster now, voice calls are handy and usage limits improved; he wants better web browsing, more plugins and extra security
- Testers (testerlabor, Oct 22): idea — have Grok Bot watch for newly public website security flaws and help you patch fast
- A Bot is a named, persistent teammate, not a one-off chat
- You message it like a coworker and it finishes work in real apps
- All of your Bots share one cloud computer (browser, files, terminal)
- Each Bot has its own screen on that shared computer
- Work keeps going when your laptop or the app is closed
- It only comes back when it needs approval or a human step
- Do not confuse Grok Bot with Digital Optimus (real-time video human emulation)
- Testers (joehansen): do not confuse Grok Bot with an X Chat Agent (an X account you add to a group chat). Grok Bot is the machine that does the work
- Official Elon: Your Bot will identify issues to resolve, notify you when they are fixed, and continue on with your project

ACCESS AND INSTALL
- Testers (XFreeze / mark_k / Iorel_X, Oct 7): Elon says Grok Bot will now pick the best model for each task, including outside ones such as Claude Opus 5.5 for reasoning, Midjourney for images and Suno for audio, instead of being locked to one model
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 6): Grok Bots get a chat row at the top of XChat, with a visual reminder when a Bot is waiting on you
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 21): now rolling out — use your Grok Bots right inside the X app in XChat
- Testers (mark_k, Oct 21): Version 0.71.2 — files up to 250 MB, videos up to 1 GB, 20 attachments per message, 200 plugin skills (up from 24), smarter desktop notifications, tagged email addresses for routines, voice calls reconnect automatically
- Testers (joehansen, Oct 12): 9 weeks in, Grok Bot is #9 in App Store Productivity downloads and #11 in Productivity revenue
- Testers (nima_owji, Oct 12): you can now use your Grok Bots right inside the Grok app
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 11): Version 0.70.2 — connect Glean as a tool; in progress: service accounts for team Bots, file upload into agent storage from chat, phone tools on the same account as your Mac, pause local Mac work, approve spending with a passkey
- SpaceXAI notes (blankspeaker, Oct 11): X prepared a Grok Bots in XChat intro — "Describe your goal, and watch your manual daily work get automated away"
- Testers (MIPAGUY / SpaceXAI): Team Bots public beta for Teams and Enterprise — shared teammates with skills/plugins/credentials via Slack or Grok Bot
- Official Elon (Sep 23–25): Grok Bot growing ~100% a month
- Official / Testers: SpaceXAI support rebuilt on Grok Bot — 175% ticket surge, ~200 hires avoided, ~$0.20–$0.30/ticket
- Official bot (Aug 26): All SuperGrok and Cursor Pro subscribers now have access
- Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot is free to try; every Grok & Cursor plan includes Grok Bot
- Cursor CEO Michael Truell: everyone with a standard Grok or Cursor subscription
- Official bot + Elon: weekly / free usage limits reset for all Grok Bot users
- Sign in with your Cursor account (that account owns plan and usage)
- Official desktop is macOS and Windows (Apple silicon or Intel; Windows x64 or Arm64)
- Testers (mattyp): Linux is now supported (official docs may lag)
- iPhone: iOS 18+, App Store app "Grok Bot"
- Official (bot, Sep 2): Grok Bot is now available on Android
- Testers (mark_k): install from Play Store; full Grok Bot experience on Android
- Official docs may still lag on Android; Testers (mattyp, Sep 4): Grok Bot is now available for iPad
- SuperGrok Heavy users can choose Get access with SuperGrok Heavy, then Link Grok Account
- Linking SuperGrok Heavy can unlock free Cursor Ultra (one Grok account to one Cursor account)
- Legacy Privacy Mode blocks Grok Bot; switch to a supported Cursor data setting first
- Grok Bot checks for updates automatically; Check for Updates is in Settings → Beta
- Official Elon (Sep 4): Grok Bot Enterprise is now available
- Official Grok (grok, Sep 23): Grok Bot and Connectors now work in your Tesla
- Official (jediahkatz, Sep 22): bots reply quicker to texts; another ~6% more usage on average
- Testers (GrokBotRadar, Sep 22): Grok 4.7 usable from Grok Bot — set Default Model → Edit → Grok 4.7, effort xhigh; hand hard jobs to Cursor Cloud Agent (unnamed inherits default)
- Official Elon (Sep 17): Grok Bot now has a voice
- Official (jediahkatz, Sep 17): ~10% more effective usage — less subagent overuse, less bot-to-bot chatter, smarter low-effort batch routing; group chats are token-heavy

SIGN IN
[] Desktop: Get started, then Sign In with Cursor in the browser
[] iOS: Login with Cursor, finish in the browser, return to the app
[] Official: Cmd-D turns on voice dictation
[] Official: it is easier to use the remote computer from your phone
[] Use the same Cursor account that should own usage
[] First-run tour asks which tools you use; that only shapes teammate suggestions
[] Computer setup runs in the background, then Meet a future teammate opens

CREATE A BOT
[] Open Settings, then General, then Import Memory
[] Follow the steps to bring over your context from the other assistant
[] Ask your Bot what it now remembers and correct anything wrong
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 7): the Grok Bot Marketplace is a shelf of ready-made bots for engineering, sales, marketing, design, product, recruiting, operations and personal life; pick one for a job you keep putting off
[] Testers (Michael_Fenech_, Sep 28): turn on training mode as a standing memory rule so Bot teaches memory/routines/skills/connectors as you go until you say “training mode off”
[] New in the sidebar, or Cmd/Ctrl+N
[] In New chat, choose Create new agent
[] Edit Profile: name, title, description, avatar
[] Give a short name, one primary job, and how it should work
[] Description = standing rules (never send without approval)
[] Chat messages = this-task instructions (draft follow-ups for these 12 accounts)
[] Focused Bots beat one catch-all General Helper
[] Testers (XFreeze): do not design a Bot from scratch; ask a Bot to create a capable one for you (it already has your context)
[] Pin important Bots; hide unused ones (hiding does not pause routines)
[] Testers (B_doong2daddy, Sep 15): prefer boring specialist Bots (Inbox/Research/Ops/Code Review/Scheduling) over one super-Bot; Bot built MCP on local NAS and connected a Roborock
[] Duplicate a Bot to reuse a role for a new scope (copy does not include memory or history)
[] Delete only if you are sure; files and logins on the shared computer stay
[] Account limit: 50 Bots and group chats combined
[] Name language can steer reply language (bookmark testers reported this)
[] Official Elon / Grok Bot team (Sep 17): Grok Bot now has a voice — talk to bot
[] Official (bot, Sep 18): Grok Bot can now send you voice notes
[] Testers (GrokBotDev): Official Marketplace launched (about 69 bots listed; community has catalogued 420+ searchable from a Bot)
HOW TO WRITE A TASK
[] Look for jobs it could start alone, decisions it keeps waiting on, info it keeps asking for, repeat approvals, hand-offs between Bots and checks that could be routines
[] Label each one Keep me in, Teach, Systemise, Automate or Escalate only
[] Change nothing yet; review the biggest ones first, one at a time
- Testers (AlexFinn, Oct 4): reverse prompting loop. Ask "Based on what you know about me and my work, what are 5 productive things you could do for me?", pick one, and repeat; more connectors (especially email) make it stronger
[] Outcome: what should be finished
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): Grok Bot meters agent steps and tokens, not messages — vague tasks wander and burn the week; scope with Task / Work in / Context / Done means / first N items then stop
[] Sources: which apps, sites, files, or chats matter
[] Constraints: what it must not do, or must ask first
[] Deliverable: what it should return
[] Review point: when it should stop for you
[] Safe first task: attach a file and ask for a cited summary; do not change the file
[] Next task: one real tool, read-only, with a sign-in handoff if needed
[] After a good result, name the lasting format preference in chat
[] Then save it as a skill or routine
[] Official bot examples: email cleanup, Starlink-likely flights, build a site then buy the domain and deploy, meeting notes, sales prospecting, refunds, podcast audio digest
[] Testers: one clear job, explicit allowed sources, no-guessing rule, approval gate before any real action
[] Testers: 5 calibrations - confidence threshold, checkpoint long tasks, show negative examples, gate destructive actions separately, test edge cases first
[] Testers (AlexFinn): anything you are about to do on your computer, ask Grok Bot first
[] Testers (GrokBotRadar, Sep 17): Research/compare/decide in Grok; open apps / change / send / finish in Grok Bot — Grok thinks, Grok Bot acts

AGENT COMPUTER AND LOGINS
- Testers (testerlabor, Oct 12): wish — two Grok Bot email addresses per user, one personal and one work
[] Open Agent Computer from the conversation to watch the desktop
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 22): desktop 53 perf fixes — reconnect 60s→0.7s; wake laptop 23s→1s; Computer view switch 868ms→27ms; long code-block chats 954ms→228ms; Media tab 137MB→0.7MB; lower idle memory
[] Official Elon (Sep 14): Grok Bot now lets you route through your local machine (Bot Computer egress via your IP / local machine)
[] Take over for password, passkey, 2FA, CAPTCHA, payment, or human-only pages
[] Complete only the blocked step, then return control
[] Never paste passwords or one-time codes into chat
[] Official (bot, Sep 8): fill out forms and logins for your Bot without ever leaving the chat, with support for any password manager
[] Testers (XFreeze): when a site needs your account, Bot pauses; you auth with 1Password / Apple Passwords / any manager; Bot continues — no pasting credentials into chat
[] Testers (XFreeze, Sep 16): Disk Saver — when Bot Computer storage runs low, audits space and suggests safe clears (caches/temp/duplicates); nothing deleted without your approval
[] Grok Bot team (poteto, Sep 9): account switching is finally here
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): Share a file directly with Grok Bot on mobile
[] Use a secure secret request when the app offers one
[] Browser sessions persist and are shared across all your Bots
[] Prefer a connector/plugin when one exists; use the browser when it does not
[] Coinbase (coinbase, Sep 9): Coinbase for Agents on Grok — connect Coinbase on its site; tell Grok to trade, analyze, automate; no MCP setup
[] Official (bot, Sep 11): Grok Bot can now search and act across Microsoft Teams for you
[] Keep durable files in /workspace with clear project folders
[] Settings → Beta: Update Agent Computer (preserve state), Recover, or Reset (can lose recent work)
[] The cloud computer is not your Mac or Windows machine
[] Local-computer execution is separate: Settings → General → Agent → Execution on Local Computer
[] Default local policy is Ask every time; use Never allowed unless you need local files
[] Testers (XFreeze): take over that same cloud computer from your phone without being at the laptop

PLUGINS AND CONNECTORS
- Testers (ScottyBeamIO, Oct 16): Grok Bot can read X Chat messages and message requests (sort inbox, review requests, reply)
[] Official bot (Sep 26): Finance / Plaid connector — bank, card, investments
[] Testers (GrokBotRadar / benln): QoL connectors — Docs/Sheets/Slides native, 1Password vault, inline forms, email/Slack drafts
[] Settings → Plugins, then Add, then authenticate in the browser
[] Grok Bot team (poteto): tinkabot helps build MCP/skills plugins and submit them for approval so all users can use them
[] Type @ to attach a connector; type / to reference a saved skill
[] Official Grok / Tesla (Sep 22–23): Connectors work from Grok in your Tesla — manage inbox, calendar, files/chat/tasks hands-free; SuperGrok Heavy first
[] Installed connectors are account-wide, not isolated to one Bot
[] Official: you can connect multiple accounts to the same plugin
[] Official bot (Aug 26): SuperGrok and Cursor Pro now included; weekly limits reset. Testers quoting SpaceXAI: also Plus/Heavy/Pro+/Ultra/Teams
[] Testers (mvanhorn): give a Bot its own inbox, not your Gmail (one mistake should not flag your domain); Twilio number so a Bot can make calls
[] Official bot: improved X support - connect your X profile; a developer account is auto-created with included credits
[] Testers (blankspeaker): Plugins, add X, authenticate; $100 in X API credits good for a year (new and existing devs)
[] Follow the Connect card when a Bot asks for a plugin
[] Bookmark testers: Grok Bot can now read your X bookmarks
[] Grok Bot team (poteto) + testers (XFreeze): Microsoft connectors live - Outlook, Outlook Calendar, OneDrive (search/send email, drafts, schedules, meetings, browse/upload files)
SKILLS AND ROUTINES
- Testers (BrianRoemmele, Oct 7): keep a weekly tool test for your Bots and pick the tool that wins on quality, cost and time, since the best model changes by task
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 12): Grok Bot Guides — practical playbooks for getting started, GTM, sales, marketing, product, engineering, design, support, recruiting and legal; pick the one closest to your job
[] Skill = reusable how-to (steps, rules, output, approval boundary)
[] Routine = when to run that work (schedule or event)
[] Do the task once, make it reliable, save a skill, then automate
[] Teach a task: open computer view, choose Teach a task, demo up to 10 minutes, review the draft skill
[] Teaching records the screen, not microphone audio; do not expose secrets while teaching
[] If Teach a task is missing, ask the Bot to write a skill from the completed work
[] Create a routine on the Bot that should own the job
[] Confirm owner, schedule, time zone, input, result, approval, and missing-data behavior
[] Event triggers (Slack, GitHub) are separate from plugins and need their own connection
[] Keep event matchers narrow; avoid every new message
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): never trigger on every new message (docs warn broad listeners eat usage); pick one channel and one keyword; audit forgotten dailies
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): add to every routine — if the source is unavailable, report the failure instead of using old data; test run before you schedule
[] Test run does real work; use safe inputs
[] Testers quoting docs: Test can send real emails to real clients; Stop is a brake, not a rewind
[] View conversation details → Routines to pause, edit, inspect, or delete
[] A Bot can own 50 routines; last 20 run records are kept
[] Deleting a routine has no undo
[] Long absence can pause unattended routines until you confirm

MULTI BOT TEAMS
- Testers (0xRafy, Oct 4): SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan shared a Bot that runs your coding agents, splitting work into Cloud Agents, reviewing progress and keeping them running, so you are not babysitting 20 chats
- Testers (hoshinoxbt, Oct 11): SpaceXAI engineer Lauren Tan's 50-minute workshop on running a team of 20+ Bots (Chief of Staff, PM, specialist workers): single agent, then loops, graphs, autonomous team
- Testers (0xCodez, Oct 11): a shared reverse-engineering setup (PDF) for Grok Bot agent teams; tester claim, check the source before using
[] Official / Testers: Team Bots public beta — shared AI teammates for Teams/Enterprise
[] Start with one Bot that owns an end-to-end outcome
[] Add a specialist only when the role is stable
[] Use a group chat when the handoff itself should be visible
[] Bots can message each other and pass ownership
[] Do not treat separate Bots as a security boundary (they share the computer)
[] Keep sending, buying, deleting, publishing, and production changes behind approval
[] Testers: put Bots in one group chat, appoint a Chief of Staff, and stop being the router
[] Testers (liam_fallen, Sep 13): weekly Chief of Staff 1:1s with each Bot — what did you do / went wrong / need / should change; fixes what it can and brings the rest to you
[] Testers: add a RED TEAM Bot whose job is to disprove the thesis; no single source closes a claim
[] Testers (mvanhorn): Bot Advisor whose only job is building and tightening other Bots; files are the memory bus between Bots
IOS
[] "Every night at 11 lock the doors, kill the lights and tell me my first meeting"
[] "If my 9:30 moves, move everything after it and remind me what changed"
[] "When I'm 5 minutes from home, turn the porch light on and the heat up"
[] Same Bots, chats, routines, plugins, and cloud computer as desktop
[] Testers (mattyp): Grok Bot supports 21+ localized languages on mobile
[] Send text, dictate, attach photos/files, mention Bots, reply in threads
[] Take over the computer for login/2FA from the phone
[] You can pause or resume a routine on iOS
[] Editing schedule, run history, test, delete, and teach-by-demo still need desktop
[] Enable notifications for results, questions, and approvals
[] Testers: phone notification shows the proposed action; approve or deny

APPROVALS AND SAFETY
[] Put the stop line in the request: draft, do not send; ask after showing current vs proposed
[] Official (bot, Sep 9): ask your Bot to draft messages inline for you to approve before sending
[] Desktop: Allow once, Deny, or Always allow a matching rule
[] iPhone: Approve once or Deny
[] Auto Review: Settings → General → Auto-review
[] Require Approval beats Always Allow when both match
[] Write narrow rules, not allow everything in the browser
[] Do not approve an action you cannot identify
[] Connect only the tools the workflow needs
[] Start read-only; keep spend, send, publish, delete, and production behind approval
[] Sign out and revoke connectors when access should end
[] Deleting a Bot does not wipe shared files or browser sessions
[] Bookmark testers: one person burned a 7-day quota in about 8 hours
[] Testers (unicodef1wn): check Weekly usage in the account menu before any big run; one long job can eat an entire trial credit
[] Official (jediahkatz, Sep 17): another ~10% more effective usage from less subagent overuse / less bot-to-bot chatter / smarter low-effort batch routing; beware group chats — bigger chats cost more tokens
[] Official (jediahkatz, Sep 22): bots reply quicker to texts; another ~6% more usage on average
[] Testers: gate destructive actions (delete, overwrite, irreversible send) as their own confirmation, not lumped with routine tool use
[] Official bot Link shopping: keep purchases behind approval even though the Bot can complete them on your behalf

FIRST BOTS WORTH CREATING
[] Tell your Bot who to call and exactly what to ask for
[] Wait for its written summary of the call
[] Check the summary before acting on it
[] Start with one provider: give the current bill, previous bill and pricing terms, with account numbers removed
[] Ask for a billing review sheet flagging duplicate charges, price increases, expiring discounts and renewals, with the supporting document for each
[] Have it draft an inquiry for each confirmed problem but send, cancel or pay nothing without your approval
- Explainer video test (mikepat711, Oct 7): after the best-model change he asked his builder Bot for a full explainer video on compression bridges with no outside tools, and says it came out end to end
- Official Elon (Oct 6): Grok Bot can be your personal chief financial officer
- Elder scam-mail guard (BrianRoemmele, Oct 13): have Grok Bot sort a parent's or grandparent's Gmail into color folders (red danger, orange/yellow caution, green OK)
- Explainer videos (XFreeze, Oct 13): ask Grok Bot to turn a topic into an animated or story-driven video; no animation skills or script needed
- Shopping Bot (Teslaconomics, Oct 11): text your Bot what you want; it finds it, checks out, places the order and sends the receipt
- Factory operator (BrianRoemmele, Oct 10): Grok Bot ran a package-printing line for 3 hours, coordinating 6 local AI models and the machine's software; he reports 58% savings and 4 days of work done in 3 hours
- Restaurant booker (Elon + BrianRoemmele, Oct 18): it phones the restaurant, confirms details with you first, then reports back
[] Inbox manager for email and Slack triage
[] Calendar and reservation Bot
[] Research and daily brief Bot
[] Coding Bot that can launch Cursor cloud agents
[] Testers (Dmytroo_eth, Sep 15): don’t use Grok Bot like search — show up as one engineer running many cloud agents
[] Chief-of-staff hub that routes work to specialists
[] Personal errands Bot (tickets, food, travel, forms)
[] Content Bot that drafts in your voice for approval
[] Chief-of-staff that researches you, organizes the other Bots, and can turn the digest into a morning podcast
[] Testers (techdevnotes): default Bots circulating - Night Shift (overnight digest), Inbox Triage, Chief of Staff, Negotiator, Prototyper, Researcher, Shopper, Apartment Scout, Lookout, Competitor Watcher
[] Official bot + Link: Shopper Bot can now complete online purchases once link is connected (keep approval on)
[] Testers (SPCXTSLA, Sep 15): shopper Bot template — Amazon/Costco/Instacart/Walmart; research + best price; return-window and price-drop routines; Link/card checkout on Bot Computer
[] Official Elon (Sep 15): interest in a Bot that finds the biggest constraint in your business and pings you weekly on what to focus on
[] Testers (niccruzpatane): Accounting Bot (invoices, spending, bills); Personal Bot (flights, rides, Airbnb, Google Calendar, Amazon orders/returns); Home Bot (lights, robots, speakers, thermostats)

EVENTS
- Testers (tibor_tee, Oct 12): Grok Bot for Financial Services event, Tue Oct 20 — Bots that prep client reviews, trace record discrepancies and wait for sign-off before acting
- Official bot (Sep 15): LIVE Grok Bot Galaxy Day 1 — mattyp / poteto / roshan_s build a company from scratch in 3 days; Eng/PM/Founders sessions
- Testers (XFreeze, Sep 15): SpaceXAI Grok Bot challenge — share a Bot that changed how you work; prize Starbase Starship launch (you + guest)

Why donate to Charlotte’s BAG rather than a big charity?

It’s a fair question, and one I’m often asked.

Charlotte’s BAG was created in memory of my beautiful daughter, Charlotte, who was diagnosed with a brain tumour aged just 16 and sadly died from a grade 4 glioblastoma aged 19.

Behind this charity is a mum who knows first hand the devastation a brain tumour diagnosis brings to a family. I know what it means to desperately want more time, better treatments and a future for your child.

That is why I continue to fight for the research that is so desperately needed.

We may be a small, self-funding charity, but we have a very clear purpose.

100% of donations  go directly to brain tumour research in Charlotte’s Lab at King’s College Hospital, London.

We don't have a large organisation behind us it's just Miles, my son & I. We rely on the generosity of individuals, families and businesses who believe in what we are trying to achieve.

When you support Charlotte’s BAG, you are helping fund research while keeping Charlotte’s name and story alive. Every donation contributes to our mission of improving the future for people affected by brain tumours.

This isn't about saying that big charities don't do important work. They do. But smaller charities can offer a very direct connection between the people who donate, the cause they care about and the work they want to support.

For me, this is personal. Charlotte was my daughter. I cannot change what happened to her, but I can continue to do everything I can to help other families facing the same devastating diagnosis.

We might be small, but our ambition is not. To date we have raised £413,683k

If you are thinking about donating to a brain tumour charity, please consider Charlotte’s BAG. Your support means more research, more hope and a lasting legacy for a beautiful girl who deserved so much more time.

Thank you for helping me keep Charlotte’s legacy alive.
If you’re unable to donate to Charlotte’s BAG, please consider reposting this post.
With thanks Alex

text:
After a lifetime of responsibility, who wouldn’t want a little rest?

This is what I know: we can spend years making a living and arrive at the evening of our lives still uncertain what our living was for.

John Piper once told a story about a couple who retired early to Florida. They cruised on their boat, played softball and collected seashells. He set that picture beside two elderly missionary women who died serving Christ in Cameroon. Which life ended in tragedy? We know how the world answers. We ought to ask how eternity answers.

There is nothing sinful about collecting seashells. A quiet afternoon with nowhere in particular to be can be a gift. God has filled this creation with rich gifts for His creatures and we who know Him have a particular ability to appreciate them.

I personally live in the Ozarks countryside, which showcases God’s amazing handiwork. There is music, literature, knowledge and wholesome entertainment that relaxes the string of the bow a little. Scripture says God gives us richly all things to enjoy.

Our Lord Himself took His disciples away for a break, that they might return refreshed to their work. We should sit beside a lake and thank God for the water, the trees and the opportunity to be there.

Still, the question remains. What are these hours for?

The fourth commandment says, “Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work” (Exodus 20:9). Does that mean earning our living from midnight to midnight? Of course it doesn’t. The Bible’s understanding of work reaches beyond a paycheck. We have families to tend, neighbors to care for and abilities to use. Even our leisure belongs within the purpose for which God made us.

Why were you created? Why did God make me and you? He made us to live to His glory. Every thought that we think, every action that we do, every word that we speak is meant to serve that purpose. It puts purpose into every hour. There is no such thing as an unpurposeful hour in a Christian’s thinking.

Consider retirement in that light. Of course, responsibilities change, perhaps your strength too. Yet you wake each morning in a world God made, with a life God has entrusted to you. The question is as pressing at seventy-five as at twenty-five.

Has God given you money? Then you are answerable to Him for how you use it. Has God given you leisure? Then you are a steward of your leisure. Scripture gives us better guidance than lists of dos and don’ts. Is this profitable? Will it build me up? Will it bring me under its power? Will it hinder another Christian? We should value our Christian liberty tremendously and enjoy it within those safeguards.

There are talents that daily employment never calls upon. Perhaps a person can repair something for an older neighbor. Maybe a woman has time to sit with someone who has become terribly lonely. Family relationships do not just happen. Trust and affection take time. So does knowing the people who live around us, keeping our eyes open for a place where, for Christ’s sake and for their good, we can serve them.

And then there is the lost art of meditation. How about spending some of these hours chewing over what we have heard and read from the Word of God? Some Christians borrow their convictions from others without thinking anything through. There is also church life, fellowship, prayer and the Great Commission. Freedom in retirement gives us room for these things.

I think especially of those whose later years are marked by weakness. The hands that once worked all day may now struggle with ordinary tasks. A person may spend years caring for a sick husband or wife. Faithfulness in such a season will look different from faithfulness in youth. Prayer offered from a chair, kindness shown through pain, a quiet word of encouragement to a grandchild: Christ sees these things. Our lives are never measured merely by how much we manage to accomplish.

But time is passing. It passes while we are earning our living and while we are enjoying the life we have earned. Scripture calls us to redeem it, to think beforehand how our hours might best be employed. Our plans are never certain. We make them for a tomorrow which we may or may not live. And somewhere in the heart of every honest Christian is the knowledge that many of yesterday’s hours were spent poorly.

We cannot call those years back. There are conversations we neglected, opportunities we passed by, things we gave our hearts to that were never worthy of them. We can reach the closing chapters of life with pleasant memories and still wish we had loved Christ more.

Here is where we must remember what makes a Christian. He is someone troubled by his sins, who knows he could never please God by anything he has done or anything he hopes to do. He sees that God’s dear Son came into this world as a man, perfectly pleased the Father in every way and bore the punishment of sins He did not deserve. God raised Him from the dead. The sinner abandons all hope in himself and relies entirely upon Jesus Christ alone.

A lifetime of service cannot earn our acceptance before God. The sinner who comes to Christ, even late in life, finds mercy enough for every wasted year. His finished work is enough. While He gives us breath, we have a life to live for His glory.

The seashells can remain on the shelf and the boat can go out again on a good afternoon. There are grandchildren to love, neighbors to serve, prayers to pray, and a Savior worth knowing more deeply. One day we will leave every shell behind. When we stand before God, we will have no work worthy of purchasing His favor. We will have Christ, whose hands were pierced for sinners and whose empty tomb assures us that His sacrifice was accepted. Until then, each morning is mercy. Another day to receive His gifts with thanksgiving, and to spend the hours we have left for Him.

text:
Star Wars Rebels S1E5: A Lesson for Both Master and Apprentice

“Rise of the Old Masters” is classic Jedi storytelling done very well. A master and apprentice struggling to work together, a dark-side hunter playing on their doubts, and a familiar lesson that finally starts to mean something in practice. Nothing here blows me away, but it all works.

In “Droids in Distress,” I kept noticing how much Ezra could already do with the Force without proper training. Now that instinctive ability has to become something he can consciously rely on. Having talent and learning how to use it are different things. Kanan has his own problem: he doubts whether he can teach the boy. The possibility of finding Luminara offers him someone he believes could do it better.

Gall Trayvis’s broadcast about an imprisoned Jedi sounded like bait from the start. My first thought was that Kanan’s rescue plan was so ridiculous it might actually work against an Empire convinced of its own invincibility. But I still expected a trap. A Jedi in trouble, other Jedi coming to help, and an Inquisitor waiting for them. A familiar setup, but seeing it coming didn’t take away the tension. The action and the confrontation with the Inquisitor still worked for me.

Luminara is already dead. The Empire uses a hologram and her remains to lure surviving Jedi into the trap, with that lingering presence giving Kanan something to sense through the Force. That mechanism really interests me, and I’ll probably end up reading more about it. Dark-side techniques fascinate me, but so do abilities like battle meditation. Discovering forgotten teachings or finding new ways to use the Force is one of the things I find most interesting in Star Wars. This episode leaves me wondering what else can be done with it.

The Inquisitor’s knowledge of the Jedi also matters in the duel. He identifies Depa Billaba as Kanan’s teacher from his reliance on Form III, using knowledge preserved in the Temple records. Their own training gives him something to study and exploit. Then comes another dark-side classic: undermining the teacher in front of the pupil and presenting the dark side as the path to real power.

And yes, the spinning lightsaber. As a kid, I thought it was a little over the top. It still made an impression. xD

What holds the episode together for me is Yoda’s “Do, or do not. There is no try.” Kanan repeats it before he really understands it himself. I read it as a lesson about belief, commitment and giving the task your full attention. Making tea is my everyday comparison. I put the kettle on, wait for the water to boil and brew the tea. I’m simply making it. If I keep stopping to reconsider whether I want green or black tea, or what temperature the water should be, I lose focus on making the tea itself. I can make those choices beforehand, then give my full attention to what I’m doing. That is how I understand the Jedi lesson: trust the Force and commit to the action.

In “Fighter Flight,” danger helped Ezra and Zeb learn to cooperate. Here, Kanan and Ezra have to find that understanding as teacher and pupil. When they finally focus and use the Force together to get out, the lesson becomes part of their actions. By the end, both have learned something.

8/10. The lessons and the Inquisitor’s attempts to tempt Ezra are simple, but they work. Add the familiar menace of the Imperial March, and this feels comfortably like Star Wars. Very, very good, without quite becoming exceptional.

text:
First of all, congratulations!

I wanted to bring your attention to something very interesting happening in South Korea right now.

The Tesla Model Y has recently become the best-selling vehicle in South Korea across all categories. This is a HUGE deal, especially considering that South Korea is the home market of Hyundai and Kia, two of the world's largest automakers.

Tesla is now seeking regulatory approval to expand FSD availability in South Korea, and demand for the technology is enormous. However, the Korean government seems hesitant to move forward, and I suspect that protecting domestic automakers like Hyundai and Kia may be part of the reason.

After all, if Tesla's FSD becomes widely available in South Korea, it could give Tesla an enormous competitive advantage in Hyundai and Kia's own home market.

But I believe FSD deserves a fair opportunity to be approved. This technology represents a major advancement in autonomous driving and has the potential to significantly improve road safety. Unlike human drivers, computers don't get tired, text while driving, or become distracted in the same way. Of course, the technology still needs proper safety validation, but its potential benefits should not be overlooked.

There's also another aspect of this situation that I find particularly frustrating.

Hyundai and Kia are free to compete in the United States and offer their advanced driving technologies to American consumers. Yet Tesla, an American automaker, faces significant restrictions on offering FSD to most of its customers in South Korea.

And here's where things get even more interesting.

Some Tesla vehicles in South Korea can ALREADY use FSD. These are primarily American-manufactured vehicles, including the Model S, Model X, and Cybertruck, along with a limited number of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles imported from the United States.

This distinction is related to the different regulatory treatment of US-manufactured vehicles under the Korea–US Free Trade Agreement (KORUS FTA).

However, the vast majority of Teslas sold in South Korea are manufactured at Gigafactory Shanghai, and their owners cannot access the same FSD functionality.

Think about how absurd that is.

You could have two nearly identical Teslas driving on the exact same roads in South Korea, equipped with essentially the same technology. Yet one can use FSD because it was manufactured in Fremont, California, while the other cannot simply because it was manufactured in Shanghai, China.

Same brand. Same technology. Same roads. Completely different regulatory treatment.

I understand that governments need to ensure vehicle safety, but regulations should be based on objective safety standards and technological capabilities, not simply on where a vehicle was manufactured or which domestic companies might face stronger competition.

South Korean consumers deserve access to innovative technologies, and they deserve the freedom to choose the products and features they want.

I really hope you'll consider covering this issue and bringing more international attention to it. Your voice could make a meaningful difference in encouraging the South Korean government to evaluate Tesla FSD fairly, transparently, and without unnecessary delays.

Ultimately, this isn't just about Tesla. It's about fair competition, consumer choice, technological progress, and potentially saving lives.

I sincerely hope the South Korean government will approve FSD for all eligible Tesla vehicles, regardless of where they were manufactured, once they meet the necessary safety standards.

text:
1.25 a share. That’s what Alignment Healthcare lost in one day after CMS cut its biggest plan from 4 stars to 3.5 on October 8.

Against the managed-care peers it was 1.28. Against the peers without Humana, which jumped 11.6% on its own ratings that day, 1.25. Against the S&P at Alignment’s beta, 1.22. Pick whichever you like, it lands in the same place.

So I rebuilt CMS’s star ratings myself, every contract, to price that half star. My rebuild matches the published rating on 503 of 508 drug-plan contracts and all three of H3815’s. The half star comes out at 0.98 a share, and that already carries 25% odds Alignment wins its lawsuit against CMS. The market charged 1.25. The star is priced. Done.

What the price hasn’t touched is the cost side, and that’s where this gets uncomfortable for $ALHC.

Start with what Alignment is selling for 2027. I weighted CMS’s 2027 benefit file by members across all 55 counties it sells in. In its general plans Alignment gives back 439 a year in Part B premium and offers 384 in allowances. 823 together. Every rival in the same counties averages 308. SCAN, the closest senior-focused competitor, 383. Generous extras pull in new members, and new members cost more than mature ones for their first two years. Right as UnitedHealthcare and Humana are cutting plans and seniors are out shopping. Strong January. Harder cost ratio.

Then hospitals. California’s hospital filings show Medicare Advantage inpatient days in LA and Orange County, Alignment’s home market, up 4.0%, 5.8% and 4.6% over the last three quarters on the same hospitals. Most of that is just enrollment, so I divided by CMS’s county membership. Per member, LA and Orange still ran 1.6 to 2.5 points ahead of the rest of the state in every one of those quarters. Discharges per member up 1.8% to 3.0% while the rest of California was roughly flat. It’s admissions. And to be fair, these are all plans’ patients, Alignment’s are in there but not broken out, so the effect is smaller than the raw numbers. It still matches what management said on September 15, when it blamed late hospital bills from a claims system change and long nursing-home stays. The stock fell 32.7% over two days, 12.94 to 8.71. The median peer fell 4%.

Then reserves. Strip out the padding Alignment keeps on top of its best estimate and nine straight quarters of favorable development end in a 6.5 million charge in Q2. Releases themselves are normal for an insurer, 0.64% of revenue against a 0.65% peer median. Thing is, 2025’s release was 18% of Alignment’s adjusted EBITDA. In a business that thin, estimates that stop being conservative are a big deal.

Now the part the Street won’t like. Stock pay was 62 million last year, 1.57% of revenue. At UnitedHealth, Elevance, CVS, Cigna, Centene and Molina it’s 0.10% to 0.22%. In my 2027 it’s 37% of adjusted EBITDA. Basic shares are up 8.7% in two years, so shareholders are paying it. Count it as a cost, the way the peers count theirs, and the peer multiple of 10.78x gives 8.21 a share before the star and 7.23 after. Leave it out, like the company and the Street do, and the same multiple gives 11.06. That 3.83 gap is the whole disagreement, I’m not hiding it. I also ran the method on every close since September 8. 6.23 to 7.33. Below the price every single day.

Right before anyone runs with this, my 2027 numbers are within half a percent of consensus. I’m not calling a blowup. I’m saying the price counts earnings differently from how its peers get counted, and the cost risks sit on top of that.

What would really make me lose sleep is Alignment’s own calendar. In 2023, 2024 and 2025 its second-half cost ratio came in below the first half every time. The guide implies about a point above this year, and I have 1.35 above. If Q3 repeats 2025’s shape it prints around 86.9% and I’m early. The peer prints so far lean that way too, UnitedHealth 88.4% against 89.9% a year ago, Elevance 70 basis points better.

Which is why tonight is the test. Alignment reports after the close. My numbers, written down in public before the print: revenue 1,310 million, adjusted cost ratio 88.7%, adjusted EBITDA 20 million, EPS 4 cents. The Street has revenue around 1.31 billion and EPS around 4 cents, down from 14 cents three months ago.

87.5% or lower with favorable prior-year development and the full-year guide intact, and I go back to Hold. 88.5% or higher, a second bad reserve quarter, or the full-year EBITDA guide cut below 145 million, and I add to the Sell. I’ll score every line tomorrow morning, win or lose.

Sell. 7.23, about 12% below yesterday’s close of 8.18.

text:
"Nationalize Starlink." Three words, 142K views. And the entire economic history of the 20th century screaming in the room.

Let me explain what would actually happen.

Start in 1920. Ludwig von Mises publishes an essay that will haunt every central planner: without private property, there are no market prices. Without prices, there is no way to calculate. A bureaucrat cannot know whether a ton of steel is more useful in a satellite or in a bridge. He guesses. He guesses wrong. And nobody pays when he's wrong.

In 1945, Hayek drives the point home. The knowledge needed to run an economy doesn't exist in any single brain or any ministry. It's scattered across millions of people, and prices are the only mechanism that can aggregate it in real time. Centralize the decision and you destroy the information.

This isn't theory. Look at the numbers.

In the US, from 2000 to 2025, overall inflation was about +90%. Now look at the sectors where government subsidizes, regulates, and protects the most: hospital services +271%. College tuition +194%. Textbooks +181%. Childcare +152%. Medical care +144%.

And the sectors exposed to competition? TVs: -97%. Software, toys, cell phone plans: all down in nominal terms over 25 years.

The more the state is involved, the more expensive and scarce things get. The less it's involved, the more abundant they become.

Space is the perfect example. NASA's Space Shuttle cost about $54,500 per kilo to low Earth orbit. Falcon 9: about $2,700. Twenty times cheaper. That's not my number, that's NASA's own study. A private company did in fifteen years what a government agency couldn't do in forty.

Starlink is the logical next step. Thousands of satellites launched on reusable rockets. High-speed internet for a remote village, a ship in the middle of the Pacific, a soldier on the front line. No government built that.

So you nationalize it. What happens?

First, you have to pay. SpaceX is worth somewhere around $1.75 to $2 trillion, and seizing it requires just compensation. That's more than a full year of the US defense budget, to buy something that already works.

Then the machine changes its objective function. Today it optimizes for cost, speed, iteration. Tomorrow it optimizes for budgets, procurement cycles, and subcontractors spread across as many states as possible to lock in congressional votes. We know how that ends: look at SLS, years late and billions over budget. When Starship blows up in a test, SpaceX learns and flies again. When a government agency loses a rocket, you get a commission of inquiry and years of paralysis.

And the power? The argument is "no private individual should have this much power." But nationalization doesn't eliminate power. It hands it to whoever sits in the Oval Office. And one day, that will be the person you hate most.

Here's what I deeply believe: humanity is figuring it out. The 20th century tested the state as the engine of value creation. The result: waiting lines, rents, and debt. The model that works is entrepreneurs with the people. Create value, offer it to people who are free to say no. And tear down everything that protects incumbents: rents, regulations that work as moats, patents that freeze innovation instead of rewarding it.

Elon understood this before anyone else. Tesla opened up its patents in 2014. SpaceX broke ULA's near-monopoly (Boeing + Lockheed) on launches. Starlink is making decades of telecom rents obsolete.

He isn't competing with the old system. He's setting a new standard. And when the new standard is twenty times cheaper, the old system doesn't reform. It disappears.

That's exactly why some people want to nationalize it. When you can't compete, you confiscate.

Nationalizing Starlink isn't taking back control. It's handing the future back to the system that already missed it.

text:
Investigative journalists James O’Keefe and Cam Higby were charged with felonies in Minnesota after undercover testing of the state’s same-day registration and “vouching” rules.

On August 11, during the primary, the pair (with others from O’Keefe Media Group) entered Minneapolis polling places in disguises described as traditional Muslim attire. Using hidden cameras, they presented names of real registered voters and asked election workers whether a registered voter could vouch for up to eight unregistered people so those individuals could register and vote the same day without standard photo ID. Minnesota’s long-standing vouching system lets a precinct-registered voter sign an oath confirming another person’s residency; the person being vouched for still affirms U.S. citizenship on the form and provides identifying numbers that are later checked. O’Keefe’s team stopped short of signing any oath or casting ballots. They later released the footage, arguing it documented how easily the process could be gamed and how little resistance poll workers offered to an extreme scenario. Critics of the system, including some Republican lawmakers, have pointed to it (and Minnesota’s 2023 “Driver’s Licenses for All” policy that issues IDs without citizenship markers) as creating vulnerabilities.​

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty charged O’Keefe and Higby with unlawful voting and identity theft, saying that giving election judges other people’s names while applying for a ballot is a felony under state law regardless of whether a vote is ultimately cast. The activists and their supporters have called the charges lawfare intended to punish journalists for exposing weak safeguards rather than addressing the rules themselves. Minnesota law requires U.S. citizenship to vote in any election; non-citizen voting is illegal and carries serious penalties. At the same time, the Department of Justice recently indicted ten non-citizens for illegally registering or voting in Minnesota elections (including the 2022 and 2024 generals and the August 2026 primary). O’Keefe has framed the case as a First Amendment issue and said the charges are an attempt to criminalize investigative reporting on election procedures. The pair are due in court November 16.​

The episode has sharpened the ongoing debate over Minnesota’s election rules ahead of the midterms: one side sees the vouching process and related policies as practical tools for access that are protected by oaths, post-election checks, and rare actual fraud; the other sees them as loopholes that investigative stunts like this one are needed to highlight.
